Georginio Rutter scored twice and set up one as Brighton thrashed Kauno Zalgris 4-0 to get their Conference League campaign off to a winning start.

Brighton were dominant from the first whistle to the last against the Lithuanian Cup winners and took the lead through Rutter, but only after a VAR check. The ball had initially been deemed to have gone out of play before Ibrahim Osman's cut-back to the Frenchman, but the goal was awarded after review.

Image: Brighton and Hove Albion's Jack Hinshelwood (second right) is embraced by his team-mates

Rutter then turned provider as Brighton doubled their lead on the stroke of half-time when Hinshelwood - returning to the side for the first time since the Premier League opening weekend - slotted into the corner.

The third came after a lung-bursting run from Malick Yalcouye, who played Osman through to cross for Rutter to turn into the net with ease.

Matt O'Riley made it four with a header as he scored his first Brighton goal since August 2025. The Australia international should have got his second with another header late on, but was denied by an excellent save from Tomas Svedkauskas.

It is now five straight wins in all competitions for Fabian Hurzeler's side who host rivals Crystal Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

Hurzeler: Disciplined performance sets us up

Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler:

"We showed a good performance, a disciplined performance, a performance where we kept a clean sheet and a performance where a lot of players used the opportunities.

"This will be key for the season, that we can really rely on each other."

'Convincing win for Hurzeler's side'

Analysis from Sky Sports News' Sophie Evans:

"A convincing win for Fabian Hurzeler's side as they kick off the club's second chapter in Europe in style. The fans around the stadium are already confident of a strong run in this competition, chanting 'we're going to go to Istanbul'.

"The Brighton boss joined his team in applauding this evening's home support. He said that their energy would be crucial in making the Amex a fortress for the opposition this season.

"It's five wins in a row in all competitions for the Seagulls. They were already the favourites to win the Conference League and their dominant performance this evening will only drive that narrative."

Key moments from the Amex Stadium...

3: CLOSE! Costinha heads over from six yards out! Excellent early opportunity for Brighton.

14: SAVE! Gross shoots from the free-kick, but his effort is tipped over by the goalkeeper!

32: CLOSE! Dunk whips a shot at goal from distance that goes just over and lands on the roof of the net!

35: SAVE! Gross with an excellent delivery from the right for Hinshelwood who heads into the ground forcing the goalkeeper to make an acrobatic one-handed save.

43: GOAL! Rutter opens the scoring after turning in Osman's cross. The goal is awarded after a VAR check.

45+1: GOAL! Rutter turns provider and crosses for Hinshelwood who produces a tidy finish across the goalkeeper to double Brighton's lead.

49: SAVE! Gross picks out De Cuyper with a lovely ball, the substitute crosses on the volley for Hinshelwood whose header is tipped over.

53: GOAL! Rutter scores his second of the night after a quality ball from Yalcouye to Osman who cuts back for the Dutchman to apply the finish.

67: GOAL! O'Riley heads across the goalkeeper and into the net to make it 4-0 to the home side.

79: SAVE! Costinha with a header at the back post. Well saved by the goalkeeper!

82: SAVE! O'Riley's bullet-header is saved brilliantly by the Kauno Zilgris goalkeeper.

What the result means and next fixtures...

Sports.title: Serbian tennis player handed 24-year ban for match-fixing
Sports.content:
A Serbian tennis player has been handed a massive 24-year ban for match-fixing.

Stefan Milicevic led a "corrupt network" of match-fixing between 2022 and 2024, according to the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), with the 29-year-old shown to have fixed six matches - five of which he played in - and attempted to with six more.

Milicevic, whose highest ATP ranking was 1338, did not engage or co-operate with the investigation, according to the ITIA, and was also fined 70,000 US dollars (£52,800).

The ITIA's statement on Thursday said: "Milicevic was also charged with recruiting or attempting to recruit multiple professional players as part of a corrupt network during the same period, resulting in a number of other players fixing matches."

Milicevic's suspension will officially come to an end on October 8, 2050, by which time he would be 53 years old.

The ITIA added: "While suspended, Milicevic is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association."

Sports.title: LIV Golf accuses DP World Tour of interference in bankruptcy process
Sports.content:
LIV Golf has accused the DP World Tour of interference in its bankruptcy proceedings at a hearing in which Bryson DeChambeau and others were released from their contracts.

The breakaway league is attempting to relaunch next year with new money from BC Partners Capital after Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund withdrew its support having ploughed in $5bn (£3.7bn) over four years.

But in order to do that it has had to apply for Chapter 11 bankruptcy and, as a result, it has had to cancel the contracts of the existing players so they can be re-signed on new terms to LIV 2.0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking to the Bloomberg New Economy Forum in New Delhi, Rory McIlroy says LIV Golf was 'half a good idea, executed poorly', and admits he felt the breakaway series 'wasn't good' for the game

However, the DP World Tour confirmed this week it was taking a harder line than previously and any player committing to LIV 2.0 would be ineligible for its membership and therefore also ruled out of Ryder Cup contention.

It has been seen in many quarters as an attempt to deliver the final blow to LIV's fading hopes of survival and, according to reports in the US media, its attorney Robert Fitzgerald told the US Bankruptcy Court in New York: "We're continuing to monitor this situation very closely and we're quite concerned by it frankly.

"The timing in particular strikes us as a clear attempt to interfere with our process, with our players and potentially our reorganisation writ large."

Guy Kinnings, CEO of the DP World Tour, said in a statement on Monday: "Players need to make a choice. As we have said for many years, we have rules and regulations which are there to protect our Tour and which our members must all abide by.

"Players who are not willing to comply with our rules and regulations should not be seeking to join our Tour."

Also at the US Bankruptcy Court hearing in New York, Judge Michael B Kaplan also approved a motion to reject the current contracts of 19 golfers after LIV stated they "do not reflect the contemplated compensation structure under LIV 2.0".

Image: Bryson DeChambeau is technically without a contract currently due to LIV's application for Chapter 11 bankruptcy

It means the likes of DeChambeau, Dustin Johnson, Bubba Watson and Lee Westwood are free to pursue other options should they wish.

Jon Rahm's release, confirmed at the hearing, has seen him give up all claims against LIV's bankruptcy estate, reported to be up to $150m (£113m).

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Inci Mehmet explains why Jon Rahm is to quit LIV Golf after deeming the terms offered for the proposed relaunch of the breakaway series 'unacceptable'

LIV has given up nearly all rights to use Rahm's name, image, likeness, trademarks and branding going forward, while Rahm has retained control of his LIV team Legion XIII's intellectual property and trademarks.

The next hearing in LIV's bankruptcy case is scheduled for October 20, with a deadline for player commitments agreed between LIV and BC Partners set for October 25.

Sports.title: Martinez apologises for outburst after Wilcox talks
Sports.content:
Manchester United defender Lisandro Martinez has issued an apology for his outburst after Tuesday's Champions League loss at Atletico Madrid.

Martinez launched an extraordinary attack on the club's hierarchy after the 2-0 defeat in Spain, as he criticised the lack of summer investment in the squad and said he expected more from "upstairs" after he singled out technical director Jason Wilcox.

Sky Sports News understands Martinez met the club's hierarchy, including Wilcox and CEO Omar Berrada, on Thursday. Head coach Michael Carrick was also present at the meeting.

In a statement released on Thursday night, the defender said: "Today I met with the club's leadership and the manager.

"It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday's game.

"Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity.

"The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.

"Our club is at its best when we are all united, and I recognise that my words in that moment did not help with that.

"I know that every single person at Manchester United is doing everything possible to achieve our shared ambition: bringing the success that this club and its supporters deserve.

Sky Sports News understands it was Martinez's decision to publicly apologise and any disciplinary decisions or internal conversations will be kept private between him and the club, but he has reportedly been fined.

The club now consider the matter closed as they prepare for Leeds on Sunday, live on Sky Sports.

On Wednesday, Martinez issued a statement to clarify his outburst, but did not apologise.

Where does this leave Man Utd?

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Danyal Khan brings the latest update on the situation around Manchester United and Lisandro Martinez

Sky Sports News' reporter Dan Khan:

"In pre-season, the players all spoke about how close this group has been since Carrick was appointed.

"This will now really be tested. At least one player confronted Martinez after his comments.

"On balance, I spoke to Harry Maguire and others this season, who have talked about the need to bring in as many players as possible.

"Where this leaves the changing room? We'll have to find out. But for Carrick, this is the last thing he needed.

"Now they have to face another distraction as the pressure mounts on the head coach."

'No internal pressure on Wilcox'

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dave Reed updates fans on which Manchester United players will be out of contract in the summer

Sky Sports News' Football Correspondent Rob Dorsett:

There are real doubts about whether Martinez's contract will be extended when it expires in the summer.

Manchester United will focus on revamping their defence in the next transfer windows and have the formal option to prolong Martinez's stay for a further year.

Sky Sports News has been told United are looking at new centre-backs, as well as left-backs.

It is also understood that there is no pressure on Wilcox internally regarding his position.

Martinez has been keen on a move away from Old Trafford for some time.

In the summer, he pushed for a move to Atletico Madrid, the side that beat United in the Champions League on Tuesday night, to follow his good friend and international team-mate, Cristian Romero, who left Spurs for Spain.

No suitable bid for Martinez came in for Manchester United to consider.

The 28-year-old made similar explosive comments about his bosses when at Ajax in 2022. Martinez, who again wanted a move away, called their sporting director Gerry Hamstra a "nobody".

Sports.title: Blood clot rules Eagles QB Hurts out of Panthers game
Sports.content:
Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts has been ruled out of their game against the Carolina Panthers on Sunday due to a blood clot in his calf.

The Eagles said in a statement on Thursday that Hurts was injured in their Week Four defeat to the Los Angeles Rams on October 4 when he took a boot to his calf area, which led to the discovery of the clot.

The Super Bowl 59 MVP practised on Friday last week, before the team left for London to play against the Jacksonville Jaguars.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Henderson’s return to Merseyside

A lively reception awaits the former Liverpool midfielders Jordan Henderson and Xabi Alonso at Everton and, in the case of the former, any jeers can be considered an unintentional tribute. They will speak of what the 36-year-old is able to produce now as much as what, and where, he delivered in the past. With two goals and an assist against Bournemouth last Saturday, Henderson became the oldest player to contribute directly to three goals in a Premier League game, and demonstrated his role at Chelsea is not simply to elevate standards off the pitch. His midfield partnership with Moisés Caicedo gave Alonso’s team balance and enabled the front three of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer to flourish. Their confrontation against an Everton defence that had impressed this season, only to litter the draw at Hull with costly mistakes, will provide a stern test of the hosts’ unbeaten start and may well be dictated by the veteran behind them. Andy Hunter

Everton v Chelsea, Saturday 12.30pm (all times BST)

2 Bees a tougher test than Lask

Still unbeaten in the top flight, Brentford’s commitment to pragmatism is serving them well. Keith Andrews’ side like to sit deep, close off the middle of the pitch and force opponents to play around them, while flooding the opposition box at set pieces and throw-ins allows them to create the chances from which most of their goals arrive. In spanking six past Lask, the Austrian champions, Liverpool showed how good they can be on the front foot, but they will face far less obliging hosts at the Gtech Community Stadium. If Andoni Iraola’s side can dominate the ball and move it quickly enough to penetrate Brentford’s rearguard, they could win comfortably. However, the Bees’ efforts to turn the afternoon into a saloon brawl and capitalise on dead-ball situations may help to maintain their unbeaten run. Barry Glendenning

Brentford v Liverpool, Saturday 3pm

3 García needs to find finishing touch

Gonzalo García has one league goal from 18 shots this season. The striker joined Fulham from Real Madrid in the summer and has looked promising in patches. García is 22 and capable of getting on the end of chances. He has an expected goals tally of 3.60 but is underperforming with his finishing. The challenge is to become more clinical. Fulham, bottom of the league, have six goals in six games and García is without a goal since scoring on his debut, against Chelsea. Álvaro Arbeloa has put a lot of faith in his fellow Spaniard. The head coach is under increasing pressure and winless Fulham need García to fire when they host Hull City. Jacob Steinberg

Fulham v Hull, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Fulham’s Gonzalo García (second left) attempts a shot on goal against Manchester United. Photograph: PA Images/Alamy Stock Photo/Alamy Live News.

4 City still free-flowing after guilty verdict

Even when losing for the first time this season in Wednesday’s 4-2 Champions League defeat by Paris Saint-Germain, Manchester City appeared the real deal as they rallied from 3-0 down after 32 minutes to give the European champions a scare. Enzo Maresca deserves credit for following Pep Guardiola serenely; his City, so far, are a free-flowing attacking machine and invigorating to watch. If not for the guilty verdict against the club for serious financial breaches of Premier League rules, the perma-twinkling Italian might be more widely lauded. Ipswich last beat City at home in the competition in November 2000: do not expect the statistic to change on Saturday. Jamie Jackson

Manchester City v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

5 Jaissle should find his ‘inner Rafa’

Newcastle’s latest attempt to play vertical football left Matthias Jaissle’s side horizontal at Coventry on Monday night. That 4-1 defeat against Frank Lampard’s team has prompted quite an inquest on Tyneside where Jaissle could do without his players falling flat on their faces once more when Aston Villa visit St James’ Park. Jaissle maintains that his “vertical football” is the brand of high-octane, aggressive attacking that Newcastle’s hierarchy believes should become the club’s default, and is the way fans want to see the team play. That argument is not without validity but it is also worth remembering that, less than a decade ago, under Rafael Benítez’s charge, Newcastle often played a low block bolstered by three at the back, rarely took unnecessary risks and improved steadily. Admittedly resources were thinner then but the fans almost universally adored Benítez and were heartbroken when he eventually tired of Mike Ashley’s ownership and resigned. Quite apart from making his dislike for “chaotic football’ plain the Spaniard was a realist who knew a gung-ho approach would spell relegation. Granted tactical fashions have changed, but Jaissle could do worse than slow things down a bit and search for his “inner Rafa” against Villa. Louise Taylor

Newcastle v Aston Villa, Saturday 5.30pm

6 Eyes on Kluivert and Brobbey

With nine games each scheduled for the month between international breaks, Bournemouth v Sunderland will give an early indication of how both will cope during their first experience of such a relentless Thursday-Sunday autumnal grind. Sunderland are 17th, Bournemouth are 18th, and with seven points between them after six Premier League rounds, scaling similarly dizzy heights to last season already seems a lofty goal. For both clubs, European campaigns are far too much of an exciting novelty to be considered anything like a chore. In circumstances where squad depth is crucial, the returns of Justin Kluivert for the hosts and Brian Brobbey for the visitors will be welcomed by Marco Rose and Régis Le Bris. It would be no great surprise to see either Dutch international make a game-deciding contribution in what is already a six-pointer on the south coast. BG

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Bournemouth v Sunderland, Sunday 2pm

7 Brighton must buck Palace trend

Brighton’s momentum appears unstoppable at the moment, although supporters will be wary of Sunday’s showdown against Crystal Palace given their recent history. They haven’t beaten Palace since a 4-1 thrashing at the Amex in February 2024 when Roberto De Zerbi was in charge, while Fabian Hürzeler managed only a point in four encounters with the Eagles under Oliver Glasner. Both are having to juggle European commitments this season and Brighton will start as heavy favourites against Pierre Sage’s side after their superb start to the campaign. Palace have big concerns in defence, but can the Frenchman defy the odds against the Premier League’s top scorers? Ed Aarons

Brighton v Crystal Palace, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Jaouen Hadjam fires home Brighton’s final goal in their 2-0 victory at Sunderland. Photograph: Craig Cowan/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

8 Carrick confronts old nemesis Farke

Michael Carrick has lost five of his past six technical-area duels with Daniel Farke. Indeed the only time Manchester United’s manager has bested his Leeds counterpart was in a League Cup tie during his Middlesbrough tenure. If such statistics are not sufficient to put Manchester United’s currently beleaguered manager off a trip to West Yorkshire on Sunday, there is a sense that Leeds are overdue a first victory at Elland Road since 2002 against their arch-enemies from across the Pennines. One thing is certain; it will be a typically raucous latter-day War of the Roses. But, right now, while the White Rose blooms, its red counterpart is wilting alarmingly. Will Carrick survive this latest meeting with a manager who, at Championship level during his Middlesbrough days, proved something of a nemesis? He will not care to remember that, last January, a 1-1 draw at Elland Road proved to be Ruben Amorim’s final game in charge of Manchester United. LT

Leeds v Manchester United, Sunday 2pm

9 Forest a genuine threat to champions

Despite losing 3-1 to Crystal Palace last weekend, Nottingham Forest played some excellent front-foot football only to be let down by extreme profligacy in front of goal and vulnerability to their hosts’ counterattacks. Oliver Glasner attributed his side’s defeat to karma upon his return to Palace, saying: “It was like I didn’t deserve to win at Selhurst Park because the players did everything.” When they welcome Arsenal to the City Ground on Sunday, they will give the champions plenty to ponder if they can play as well again. Mikel Arteta’s side were unconvincing for 65 minutes against Leeds last weekend and failed to impress until they brought their heavy artillery around the same time against Lille on Tuesday. If one or both of Morgan Gibbs-White and Liam Delap can convert the kind of chances they missed at Selhurst Park, Forest have every chance of getting something. BG

Nottingham Forest v Arsenal, Sunday 4.30pm

10 On-song Coventry can pile angst on Spurs

The last time Tottenham hosted Coventry in the Premier League, Steffen Iversen, Les Ferdinand and Serhiy Rebrov scored in a comfortable 3-0 win. And while Spurs fans will almost certainly have envisaged a similar scoreline when the fixtures were announced, they will now be viewing Monday night’s fixture with even more than the usual amount of apprehension and dread. Like Tottenham, Coventry’s main problem until recently was an inability to convert chances, but in their demolition of Newcastle on Monday they visibly grew in confidence and swagger as four different players took the plaudits. While it’s taken a while and they may still struggle, through back-to-back wins Frank Lampard’s side have now announced themselves as a Premier League force to be reckoned with, which is something Tottenham haven’t managed in more than two years. BG

Sports.title: Martínez apologises to Manchester United’s director of football Wilcox after outburst
Sports.content:
Lisandro Martínez has apologised for claiming that Jason Wilcox, Manchester United’s director of football, failed to strengthen sufficiently in the summer window after discussions with the manager, Michael Carrick, and club hierarchy on Thursday.

While any disciplinary action taken against him will not be made public by the club, it is thought that Martínez has been fined.

The defender’s apology came on Thursday evening after the 28-year-old failed to offer one when issuing an initial statement on Wednesday regarding his outburst following Tuesday’s 2-0 Champions League loss at Atlético Madrid.

He posted on Instagram: “Today I met with the club’s leadership and the manager. It was a very positive conversation, where we were able to exchange views and speak openly about what happened after Tuesday’s game.

“Everyone knows that I am a passionate person and that I live football with great intensity. The frustration of the defeat led me to express how I felt at a time and place that perhaps were not the right ones, and for that I want to apologise.”

The apology is a considerable climbdown. After the Atlético defeat, Martínez was scathing of Wilcox and his recruitment in the last window.

He said: “I expect more [investment], 100%. I expect more from our technical director [Wilcox]. As players we have to do more but it is also important when you make a strong squad to be ready for this kind of night. Last season we did everything, we created the base to create an amazing team.”

Martínez claimed that Carrick had not been backed sufficiently. “I don’t think so. He does his best. You can’t keep changing, changing, changing the manager. What about other areas?” he said.

While it is understood Martínez’s apology was his decision alone, United spent £155m in the market – all on midfielders, Andrey Santos, Youri Tielemans, and Carlos Baleba, despite Wilcox targeting a left-back.

Sports.title: Evanilson, Rayan and Rodríguez goals seal Bournemouth’s historic home win in Europe
Sports.content:
An impossible dream realised: the Vitality Stadium staging European football, where the Europa League is becoming an oasis for Bournemouth. No wins yet in the Premier League, but beating Sturm Graz following up winning away at Real Sociedad should calm the domestic pressures mounting on Marco Rose. A pair of Brazilians secured club history, with Evanilson’s first-half header followed by Rayan’s later drive, a clincher coming just as the Austrian visitors were pushing hard for an equaliser. Álvaro Rodríguez’s stoppage-time penalty extended the celebrations.

Flag day at the Vitality. Elvis Presley’s high baritone and Andy Williams’ tenor on the public address system marked a different type of occasion. Bournemouth have come a significant distance. “Minus 17 to European dreams” read a banner in the Steve Fletcher stand, marking the journey from the foot of the Football League to becoming a model, continental club. Milan visit next week, an occasion to further broaden the smile of Bill Foley, Bournemouth’s financier present in the posh seats. “A long time coming,” said Bournemouth’s long-serving captain, Adam Smith. “The fans were up for it, the players were up for it.”

Bournemouth’s new head coach has described the chaos of English football, midfield areas that can resemble a rolling maul, but he has pledged to learn and adapt. “I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation,” Rose said. “If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it’s hard to beat us. That’s what we should take into the next game.”

Missing Eli Junior Kroupi so far this season, and lately Alex Scott, are regrettable problems within a small squad. Selling Scott for £80m in January, as has been speculated, speaks to the financial balancing act clubs such as Bournemouth must perform to progress. Following the 5-1 loss to Chelsea, Sunday’s Premier League meeting with Sunderland was prioritised in team selection though the second-half introduction of key men, including Rayan, proved decisive.

“Everyone deserves to play and it’s good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad,” said Rose, who revealed Smith had given a speech to his teammates after the loss at Stamford Bridge. “That’s my captain.”

View image in fullscreen Rayan doubles Bournemouth’s lead six minutes after coming off the bench. Photograph: Paul Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Smith supplied the first proper chance. Marcus Tavernier, cutting inside, shanked that wide before a Ben Gannon-Doak cross from the byline saw Rodríguez misjudge the flight. The summer signing, still raw at 22, finds decent positions only for his touch to betray him. His penalty, following an inadvertent handball from Jon Gorenc Stankovic, was his first goal and should help his confidence.

Graz, fourth in this season’s Österreichische Bundesliga, hardly exuded ambition, a defensive trio often morphing into a shell-like five. Amid such squeezed space, after a corner, Bournemouth had the ball in the net, for what seemed an own goal though it had struck Bafode Diakité’s arm. Tavernier struck the outside of a post, before Graz at last began to advance. The away contingent celebrated a penalty, but Belmin Beganovic was shown a yellow card for simulation. Fabio Ingolitsch, the Graz coach and a Rose protege, spoke to his own team’s realities by saying: “Bournemouth is the team with the biggest market value in the Europa League.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Another Smith cross supplied Evanilson’s goal, a header full of neck muscle looping off the angle for a first European goal celebrated in Boscombe. “Many more to come from him,” said Smith of the perpetual motion No 9. Graz fans sang whatever the game state, that being the continental way, but there became more to encourage them beyond the break. Simon Seidl’s shot whistled wide, Jürgen Heil struck a post before Jacob-Peter Hödl forced a remarkable reflex save from Djorde Petrovic on the rebound. The spectre of Premier League travails, where positive play has been unrewarded, loomed as Graz interchanges became crisper.

The 70th-minute triple introduction of Rayan, Justin Kluivert and Ryan Christie proved to be Rose’s successful method of locking down midfield and increasing his team’s attacking threat at the same time.

Rayan, a decent finisher when coming inside, snatched the contest from Austrian reach. Daniil Khudyakov, Graz’s Russian goalkeeper, first flapped at a corner and then got only a weak hand to the Brazilian’s drive through the proverbial forest of legs. Bournemouth’s European homecoming had been coupled with the victory the occasion had demanded.

Sports.title: Noah Sadiki stunner earns Sunderland dramatic late win against Torreense
Sports.content:
Three minutes into stoppage time Noah Sadiki hurdled a set of advertising hoardings, sprinted across a running track and hurled himself towards the ecstatic Sunderland fans.

Just as those supporters’ long-awaited party in Portugal had looked in peril of falling a little flat, the Democratic Republic of the Congo midfielder capitalised on excellent work from Enzo Le Fée and Granit Xhaka to half-volley an eye-catching first goal for Régis Le Bris’s side.

It ensured a largely unconvincing Sunderland came from behind to secure a second straight Europa League win and their relief was evident as every outfield player followed Sadiki in vaulting those hoardings to join the celebrations.

“It was a difficult game,” said Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager, with considerable understatement. “Torreense are a good team.”

With their home ground too small to accommodate European football, Leiria’s stadium stood in. It proved quite some substitute. An arena overlooked by a 12th-century castle constructed to defend this attractive medieval town against reconquest by the Moors created an imposing backdrop to Sunderland’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years.

Back in 1973 they were second division FA Cup holders. Torreense know the feeling. Having provoked widespread shock by beating Sporting to win the Portuguese Cup last spring, Luís Tralhão’s second-tier side relish their underdog status.

After winning at Lillestrøm last month, Torreense aimed to keep the surprises coming and duly left a heavily rotated Sunderland trailing at the break. Le Bris had left, among others, Xhaka, Le Fée and Nordi Mukiele on the bench ahead of Sunday’s vital Premier League trip to Bournemouth. This reshuffle permitted Luke O’Nien, a survivor from League One days, to captain Sunderland at a ground transformed into a sea of red and white. Although only 4,000 official tickets were allocated to the visitors more were readily available locally and estimates suggested the formal allocation had doubled.

As the sun dropped and the temperature fell from a high of 28C those fans watched a disjointed first half on Sunderland’s part. It seemed telling that the normally fairly impassive Le Bris looked distinctly, and unusually, irritated and frustrated at times.

View image in fullscreen Sunderland supporters enjoy their club’s first competitive trip to the continent for 53 years. Photograph: Ana Brigida/AP

Granted his humour was hardly helped by the referee’s penchant for detecting phantom Sunderland fouls but ominously Malick Fofana, a £30m summer signing from Lyon, struggled wide on the left. Ditto Nilson Angulo on the right wing.

Torreense, 15th in Portugal’s second tier might not have been threatening Robin Roefs’s goal but they succeeded in blocking and clearing pretty much everything that came their way. Indeed Tralhão’s defence looked almost as well fortified as that ancient castle towering over them.

Admittedly, midway through the first half Timur Tutierov, Sunderland’s centre-forward, thought he had headed the opener but that effort was disallowed due to shirt pulling on Omar Alderete’s part.

Then, with the interval fast approaching, Le Bris adopted hand-on-hips mode as Torreense reminded everyone precisely why they have built such a giantkilling reputation by scoring with their first shot.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

It came from centre-back Volnei Feltes. With Sunderland losing concentration and standing off, he was permitted to advance unopposed before cutting in on his right foot and sending a sublime 20-yard curler into the top corner.

Although Angulo forced Lucas Paes into a fine save he, like Fofana, was soon replaced as Le Bris made a quadruple substitution involving the introduction of Le Fée, Xhaka, Mukiele and Reinildo.

This infusion of quality left Torreense a little groggy and the midfielder Jules Ahoka –a highly impressive 20-year-old £8.5m summer buy from Royal Antwerp – was able to equalise by heading his first goal for Sunderland courtesy of Mukiele’s deft dink.

View image in fullscreen Jules Ahoka scores Sunderland’s first goal against Torreense. Photograph: Luis Loureiro/Shutterstock

When the lively Tutierov went down in the box, the referee immediately pointed to the spot. However, a linesman’s flag indicated an offside so it seemed there would be no penalty. Or at least not until the video assistant referee intervened – lengthily; the eventual conclusion was no offside, no foul and no penalty.

No matter; when Le Fée dinked a gorgeous ball into the box and Xhaka played it into Sadiki’s path, the scorer waited for it to drop across him before applying the expert finishing touch on the half-volley.

Sports.title: Europa League: Lyon take down Crystal Palace as Benfica overwhelm Celtic
Sports.content:
Pierre Sage endured a frustrating return to Lyon in the Europa League as his Crystal Palace side lost 3-2 to his former employers at the Groupama Stadium.

Corentin Tolisso opened the scoring for the hosts and Ernest Nuamah doubled Lyon’s advantage late in a first half without a shot on target for the visitors. Yéremy Pino halved the deficit five minutes after the break before Pavel Sulc restored the Ligue 1 side’s two-goal advantage. The Palace substitute Daichi Kamada pulled one back with nine minutes remaining in a better second half for Palace, who could not find an equaliser.

Days after beating his predecessor, the Nottingham Forest manager, Oliver Glasner, at Selhurst Park in the Premier League on Sunday, Sage found himself returning to the home of the club he managed for 14 months.

Ismaïla Sarr, who claimed the Conference League golden boot last season, was in the Crystal Palace starting lineup for the first time this season.

Celtic found a clinical Benfica side too much to handle during a 4-1 defeat in Lisbon. The Colombia striker Jhon Durán scored for the hosts with a penalty after just five minutes having been fouled by Dane Murray and completed his double in the 35th minute, after the defender Alexander Bah had doubled Benfica’s lead earlier in the half.

Martin O’Neill’s side were cut apart at times but could have scored themselves on a couple of occasions before the break. The visitors eventually reduced the deficit in the 63rd minute through a brave header from Camilo Durán – who had joined up with the squad late after remaining in Glasgow for the birth of his second child – but they could not close the gap any further before the substitute Vangelis Pavlidis fired in a fourth for the home side with two minutes remaining.

Quick Guide Conference League roundup Show Georginio Rutter got Brighton’s campaign off to a flying start and sent a message to his manager, Fabian Hürzeler. Rutter has lost his place to Charalampos Kostoulas and was making his first start since the opening day of the season against the Lithuanian champions Kauno Zalgiris. The French forward responded by scoring twice and creating another as Brighton cruised to a 4-0 victory at the Amex Stadium, with Jack Hinshelwood and Matt O’Riley also on target. Hearts suffered a frustrating start to their campaign as Nordsjælland scored a late equaliser to secure a 1-1 draw in an entertaining encounter at Tynecastle. The home side went ahead through Oisin McEntee’s close-range finish in the 33rd minute and had several chances to add to their lead. But they lost their way in the closing quarter of the match and Nordsjælland, fourth in the Danish Superliga, claimed a point through a deflected strike from Nicklas Røjkjær. Press Association Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Randal Kolo Muani scored a stoppage-time header to give Juventus a 2-1 win at Celta Vigo which leaves them top of the standings. Hugo Álvarez had put the home side in front early on before Nick Woltemade equalised on the hour and Kolo Muani then nodded in from close range during the second minute of added time.

Milan cruised to a 4-0 victory at RB Salzburg, courtesy of a hat-trick by the Italian teenager Alphadjo Cissè. Milan’s record signing Gonçalo Ramos made it four on 72 minutes before a red card for Filippo Terracciano took some of the shine off the win for Ruben Amorim’s side.

View image in fullscreen Milan’s Alphadjo Cissè points to the crowd after scoring the opener in a 4-0 win at RB Salzburg. Photograph: Martin Divíšek/EPA

Bayer Leverkusen put themselves top of the standings after the early kick-offs as they followed up their opening 2-0 win with a 4-0 success at Polish side Lech Poznan. The Czech striker Patrik Schick was on target twice from the penalty spot in the first half, either side of a Malik Tillman goal, to ensure the points were wrapped up for Carles Martínez’s side before the interval. Ibrahim Maza added a late fourth.

Real Sociedad followed up their opening defeat at home to Bournemouth with a 1-1 draw at Union Saint-Gilloise.

Sports.title: Alex Scott quits Disney+ role as Women’s Champions League presenter
Sports.content:
Alex Scott, the former Football Focus host, has left her role as a presenter of the Women’s Champions League coverage on Disney+.

It is understood it was Scott’s decision to walk away and focus on other projects, including her new show, One More Word WSL, with her fellow former England internationals Anita Asante and Fara Williams.

Scott had fronted the streaming platform’s coverage of the elite women’s European club competition since it obtained the rights in 2025. However, Disney’s production levels were criticised after the opening round following a series of technical problems. These included an unscheduled advert break that interrupted the second half of Arsenal’s 1-0 win over HB Køge for more than three minutes.

A spokesperson for Disney+ told the Guardian: “We would like to extend our sincere thanks to Alex Scott for her contribution to our coverage of the Uefa Women’s Champions League on Disney+. Her passion for the women’s game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed. We wish her every success.”

Scott, a former England and Arsenal defender and former contestant on the BBC’s Strictly Come Dancing and ITV’s I’m a Celebrity … Get Me Out of Here!, has also presented major sports shows for the BBC, including coverage of the 2020 Olympics. Scott’s representatives said: “Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future.”

Scott presented the BBC’s Football Focus show for five seasons before its closure this year. At the start of this season’s Women’s Super League campaign she launched One More Word through her own production company, First Cap Productions, and has previously explained that show was createdin response to the BBC cancelling its weekly WSL highlights show.

Scott, who turned 42 on Wednesday, told the Observer, this month: “I feel like there’s always an excuse about women’s football shows not working because of the viewership or needing to save money. Whereas I think if they are done right, they can work, if things are given a fresh idea or a fresh format, they can work.”

In the same interview, discussing some of the criticism aimed at Disney’s Women’s Champions League coverage this term, Scott said: “Ultimately, do I agree with all the decisions that were made? Absolutely not. Did I try and advise? Yes, but I can only do so much.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“But nobody sees the conversations, the fights I have behind the scenes. But I can hold my head up and know that I’ve always tried my best for the greater good of women’s sport.”

Sources have told the Guardian the presenter’s relationship with Disney remains positive. Disney, whose coverage is produced by ESPN, secured an exclusive five-year deal to broadcast the Women’s Champions League across European broadcast territories in 2025. It is understood its presenting team will continue to include Shebahn Aherne, Nedum Onuoha and Lianne Sanderson. The lineup includes commentators such as Vicki Sparks and Jacqui Oatley. The competition resumes on 28 October.

Sports.title: Apologetic Infantino ‘not fit’ to lead Fifa, claim European FA heads after meeting
Sports.content:
European football leaders are increasingly confident they will find a candidate to stand against Gianni Infantino in next year’s Fifa presidential election, with the heads of the English and German football associations questioning his fitness to govern after a three-and-a-half-hour council meeting.

Infantino began the long-awaited gathering of Fifa’s 37-strong executive board by apologising for failing to consult them over his abandoned World Cup sell-off plan but failed to provide answers to dozens of questions posed by the European FAs on a range of subjects including the Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, Donald Trump’s Fifa peace prize and the Folarin Balogun affair, when the USA striker’s World Cup suspension was overturned after lobbying from the US president.

Infantino’s apology was followed by a 30-minute presentation on FFE from two American lawyers, who described the $20bn (£15.1bn) valuation and proposed sale of a 20% stake to Thrive Capital as a good deal for Fifa. At the insistence of some attenders, the lawyers were asked to leave the meeting after they had presented. When questioned, one of them confirmed he had been commissioned and paid by Fifa to produce a review of FFE.

Quick Guide How do I 

“The main objective for Gianni was to survive this meeting and nothing more,” one council member told the Guardian.

Council members succeeded in deferring, until they receive more information on Balogun, a Fifa proposal to amend its disciplinary regulations by removing the scope for players shown a straight red card to have it rescinded. Infantino pledged to provide that information by their next meeting in Doha on 16 December, after nominations close on 18 November for March’s presidential election.

The issue of whether the Fifa peace prize will be revived this year or Trump left as a standalone winner has been referred to Fifa’s social responsibility committee, and the Asian Football Confederation president, Sheikh Salman bin Ibrahim al-Khalifa, has been appointed to chair a new committee examining governance reform. But otherwise the meeting broke up without tangible answers, to the frustration of the English FA’s chair, Debbie Hewitt.

“We didn’t get answers to anything that we had specifically requested,” Hewitt said. “I think the man [Infantino] has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, he’s not fit to be Fifa president. That was what was shared in the meeting.”

The German FA’s president, Bernd Neuendorf, went further by calling for wholesale reforms of Fifa’s administration, which he hopes will fall within the purview of Sheikh Salman’s governance committee.

“The whole administration has to be reformed and the whole governance has to be reformed,” Neuendorf said. “But I’m pretty clear here that this is not possible with Gianni as the responsible person at Fifa. So we need a complete restart, I think, a political restart of persons who represent Fifa.

“Yes he apologised, but I didn’t have the feeling that this apology was because of the FFE project in total. My impression was it was just because it wasn’t brought forward to the council and no one was involved.”

Neuendorf also said he was “very confident” that an alternative candidate would be found to stand against Infantino, a view shared by senior figures at Uefa, who expect a late declaration to limit the amount of time for Fifa to scupper the nomination.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

The respective presidents of the three continental confederations who have called for Infantino to go – Aleksander Ceferin of Uefa, Victor Montagliani of Concacaf and Sheikh Salman – have ruled themselves out and suggestions that high-profile figures such as Arsène Wenger or Michele Kang could put themselves forward have been dismissed.

A proposal to distribute $3.5bn (£2.6bn) from Fifa’s financial reserves, which would involve each national association receiving $25m over the next four-year cycle, was approved by council.

Montagliani is also understood to have been critical of Infantino, but Fifa’s president received strong support from council members from Asia and Africa.

“I am certain that Gianni Infantino is the right president,” Ahmed Yahya, president of the Mauritania Football Federation said. “The majority want Gianni Infantino to stay. After finally withdrawing this proposal, president Gianni Infantino apologised to the members of the executive committee. This was followed by a responsible debate, during which this issue was more or less shelved.

“In the interests of football, the executive committee is looking ahead and seeking solutions, by focusing on the good aspects that football has to offer and trying to move forward.”

Sports.title: Southgate ‘hardly watches’ football and does not envisage Premier League return
Sports.content:
Gareth Southgate has all but ruled out a return to Premier League management and revealed he “didn’t even enjoy the wins” for more than a couple of minutes towards the end of his time in charge of England.

Southgate, who has moved away from football since stepping down as the manager of the England men’s team after defeat by Spain in the Euro 2024 final, said he had not attended a game since watching his boyhood club Crystal Palace beat Manchester City in the FA Cup final last year.

The 56-year-old’s only taste of club management came when he spent almost three-and-a-half years at Middlesbrough after replacing Steve McClaren in 2006. Southgate was unable to keep Middlesbrough in the Premier League in 2009 and he indicated during an appearance on the Amol Rajan Connection podcast that he had no interest in seeking a return to top-flight management.

Quick Guide How do I 

“I don’t see a scenario where I do that,” he said. “Towards the end of my time with England, I stopped enjoying … at the very least for a period, the wins keep you going. By the end, I didn’t even enjoy the wins for any longer than a couple of minutes. So, I’ve hardly watched football.

“I went to the FA Cup final to see my team, Crystal Palace, win their first trophy. I’ve not been to a football ground since. So my sort of desire to be involved in football has changed.”

Southgate managed England for almost eight years and came close to ending their hunt for a first men’s trophy since the 1966 World Cup. But he has sought different opportunities since leaving the role. He has launched a podcast and fronted a BBC documentary this year in which he travelled across the UK to understand the challenges facing young men and boys.

“I’ve loved the last 18 months of my life,” Southgate said. “I’ve had 37 years where my sense of self depended on did I win or lose on Saturday. And actually I’ve loved having different experiences.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“I’ve met politicians, I’ve met people in the media industry, I have learned about leadership in all sorts of areas, I’ve travelled around the world learning things. I’ve just enjoyed playing a different film in my life.”

Sports.title: Jon Rahm leaves £75.5MILLION on the table to walk away from LIV as bankrupt tour lets go of one of its biggest stars in major blow
Sports.content:
Jon Rahm has left a staggering multi-million-pound sum on the table after walking away from rebel tour LIV Golf following Saudi Arabia's exodus from the sport.

The Spanish star deemed the terms of the LIV 2.0 to be 'unacceptable', after Saudi's Public Investment Fund (PIF) announced that it would stop funding the tour at the end of the 2026 season.

The tour plans to rebuild with new backers BC Partners, a private equity group, but Rahm will not be part of the cohort playing in 2027 after coming to a 'consensual separation agreement' with LIV.

Rahm and LIV have reached a deal to release all of his monetary and economic claims against the league, with Rahm previously the organisation's largest unsecured creditor owed £5.7m of his contract after LIV filed for bankruptcy last month.

But in walking away, Rahm has also foregone the remainder of his contract, which adds up to a staggering £75.5m ($100m).

In exchange for doing so, the 31-year-old is believed to receive rights to his name, image and likeness in return.

Jon Rahm has walked away from the £75.5m outstanding from his lucrative contract with LIV

This will mean the return of his nickname 'Rahmbo' used on the tour, and his 'Legion XIII' team name, which he played under on the LIV tour.

Confirmation of Rahm's deal with LIV will come on November 5, when it will be judged by US Bankruptcy Court of New Jersey Judge Michael B Kaplan.

Rahm has won the past three seasons of the tour after being tempted to join the Saudi-backed rebels by a mammoth contract agreed at a reported £258m ($350m) - to be paid out over multiple years.

While LIV 2.0 will hope that many of their big-name stars stay and continue to play for the second coming of the tour, their filing for bankruptcy in New Jersey opened the door for stars like Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton to wrap up their time on the tour.

Daily Mail Sport reported last month that while Bryson DeChambeau's deal expired at the end of the 2026 season, he is expected to recommit in return for equity in the league.

The rebel golf circuit, which launched in 2022 with the financial backing of the PIF, paid nine-figure bonuses to lure top players like Brooks Koepka, Dustin Johnson, DeChambeau and Rahm away from the PGA Tour.

Further temptations including lucrative prize money, with some tournaments offering up to $20million in funds.

But it all began to fall apart earlier this year with PIF's withdrawal, prompting a number of events to be cancelled in 2026.

Sports.title: Alex Scott QUITS Disney's 'Gen Z' Women's Champions League football show, just two rounds of matches in, after saying she 'didn't agree with all decisions' on 'Match of the Day with a dog'
Sports.content:
Alex Scott has left her role as part of Disney+'s Women's Champions League coverage just weeks after taking part in the launch of new show 'The Hangout', which was widely criticised by fans.

The former Football Focus presenter had worked with the streaming service since they were awarded the rights to Europe's flagship competition in 2025, but Scott has now stepped away with a view to focusing on other projects.

In a statement released by Disney+ and shared with the Guardian, the broadcaster thanked Scott and wished her 'every success', adding: 'Her passion for the women's game and the competition shone through throughout her time with us, and we are grateful for all she contributed.'

A representative for Scott told Daily Mail: 'Alex is grateful for the opportunities she has had to work with the team at Disney+ and hopes that they continue to work together in the future.'

Scott leaves the streaming service shortly after the debut of a new Match of the Day-style programme launched for the competition which was mocked for its chaotic launch episode.

She fronted the programme alongside fellow former professional Lianne Sanderson, and influencers Tyra Mills and Alex Bailess.

Alex Scott has left Disney+'s coverage of the Women's Champions League just one season on from the broadcaster winning the rights

Scott celebrated her birthday on Wednesday evening, the day before the announced, with her partner musician Jess Glynne (Source: Instagram/Alex Scott)

A move to appeal to Gen Z viewers seems to have been made, with football at times seeming peripheral to discussions, and an influencer dog named Barley was also introduced, with the animal asked to pick the winner of the Champions League through food.

The show featured a 'watch party' with Dutch twins Sanne and Merel van Dongen, with Sanne a former basketball player and Merel a footballer.

Fans were left in disbelief at what was unfolding on social media, with one writing: 'Disney said they were a brand and ran with it. They thought a revolving sofa and dog would keep the attention of the girls whilst watching the football and stuck an ad mid game because no one's really watching. You get comments about how empty the stadiums are but how are we growing the game if it's still being dressed up with a pink bow on the top?

'Then bored men with no club football will s**g it off because some football account is making fun of it.

'If we like women's football, we like it for the game, for the players, for their skill, our clubs. JUST like you would for a men's game. Disney, the fans of women's football do not need cute, we'd love impartial analysis, post-match interviews with the team that's played and less dog.'

Another added: 'Sorry the dog in the Disney studio for the UWCL coverage is finishing me like am I watching the coverage for the football or Crufts?'

There was no explanation for why Barley was on the show, though his 137,000 Instagram followers were mentioned.

Disney's production levels were criticised elsewhere on match day, with the broadcaster coming in for further criticism when it cut to an unscheduled advert break in the middle of Arsenal's clash with HB Koge.

Scott is believed to be set to be focusing on her other commitments including her recently launched WSL show, One More Word WSL.

The presented waved goodbye to her role on Football Focus, with the end of the programme after 52 years on air on the final day of the season.

The long-running Saturday programme was the victim of BBC cuts amid a decline of viewing figures in recent years.

Scott was left in tears after being overcome with emotion during the final episode, with returning presenter Garth Crooks gifting her a photo of her and the programme's first host Bob Wilson.

'That's got me,' she said as she looked at her present which had: 'Alex, congratulations for all you have achieved', written on it.

She later added: 'Thank you Garth for being here today. For 52 years, wow, this show has done one thing. Week in week out, it has brought football into your Saturday afternoons whether it was Bob Wilson in 1974 or any of the brilliant presenters that sat in this chair after him, the thing that never changed was you, the fans.'

Sports.title: Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon
Sports.content:
Cherries on top! Bournemouth make European history as Sunderland score last-gasp winner and Brighton enjoy easy win... but Crystal Palace fall to defeat in five-goal thriller against Lyon

This was a night for Bournemouth to look back as much as it was to look forward.

A night to reflect on how far they’ve come, from navigating a 17-point deduction that put their Football League status at risk in 2008 to playing – and winning – their first ever European home game, thanks to a sublime treble from Evanilson, Rayan and Alvaro Rodriguez, who added the cherry on top with a late penalty.

There was a special tifo behind one goal to mark the historic night, with a record crowd of 12,010 packed in to witness it.

It was Adam Smith, who has been with Bournemouth since 2010 when they played in League One, leading them out as club captain.

Here was owner Bill Foley, seeing his vision to get Bournemouth into Europe, a target he ambitiously but explicitly set back in December 2022, occurring a year ahead of his five-year target.

But when Smith’s cross in from the right was expertly flicked up into the air by Evanilson, looping over Sturm Graz goalkeeper Daniil Khudyakov, it was a moment for Bournemouth to look forward, too.

Tournament favourites before they beat Real Sociedad in San Sebastian last time out and back-to-back European wins has done little to rubbish that label. Bournemouth have had to take the long way to the top but now they are here, they are showing just how much of a punch they pack.

Evanilson scored Bournemouth's first European goal at home in their 3-0 win over Sturm Graz

Bournemouth fans celebrated the club's journey pre-match, with the club now among the leading contenders to win the Europa League

Boss Marco Rose, who made five changes for this one, described the weekend’s 5-1 drubbing at the hands of Chelsea as a ‘good slap’.

Bournemouth were ruthlessly dismantled in south-west London. But to paraphrase the iconic ‘Tubthumping’, a song by British band Chumbawamba, when you get knocked down, you get up again, and that’s exactly what Rose’s side did.

It was a suffocating first half for a Sturm Graz side that started with a back five before pivoting to a back four at the interval.

Bournemouth had 10 efforts on goal to the visitors’ zero, with Ben Gannon-Doak and Evanilson a constant threat down the Bournemouth right.

Good sides ride their luck at times, too, and Bournemouth are no different. Sturm Graz wanted a penalty just before half-time when Belmin Beganovic was clumsily felled by Smith, only for the referee to adjudge Beganovic to have dived.

In a much improved second half, Graz struck the post when Jurgen Heil was picked out in the area.

But when you’ve battled back from the brink of minus-seventeen in League Two, and all the perils that come with trying to gatecrash the Premier League elite from a starting base in the fourth tier, adversity in Europe is light work.

Second halves have been an issue that have pockmarked Rose’s tenure on the south coast so far, coming into this one having led in six out of eight, only going on to win two of them. It was an irritation away to Sociedad, and here was proof that Rose and his players are learning lessons on the fly.

Marco Rose wants his side to take their performance against Sturm Graz into the Premier League

Justin Kluivert, Rayan and Ryan Christie all formed part of the cavalry sent on by Rose in a bid to settle the game and allow the party atmosphere to kick into another gear and that roll of the dice paid off with 15 minutes to go.

Khudyakov dealt poorly with a Bournemouth corner and after dropping it in his six-yard box, Rayan smashed in as Rose threw both arms into the air in celebration.

Rose is already looking ahead to how they can now secure their first league win of the season - starting on Sunday, when Sunderland visit the Vitality.

'Performance-wise, clean sheet, attitude, effort - a deserved win and now we have to continue, have to get consistent in these things and Sunderland is the next challenge,' said Rose.

'I believe in this team and know they are always confident despite a difficult situation. The squad is working, everyone is keen to play, everyone deserves to play and its good for us for the busy weeks to have a competitive squad.

'If we stick together and play like this and we have our fans then we are hard to play and it's hard to beat us. That's what we should take into the next game.'

For all the fireworks, tifos, light shows, and noise that lit up the night sky, here was proof of just how far Bournemouth have come… and how much further this ascending group can go with Champions League football in their sights.

Torreense 1-2 Sunderland: Sadiki scores last-gasp winner

By Michael Pavitt

Regis Le Bris was forced to call on the cavalry to rescue his side as Sunderland came from behind to win their first European away match in 53 years in stoppage time against Portuguese second division side Torreense.

Noah Sadiki struck in the dying minutes prompting wild celebrations from the near 4,000 travelling supporters, who had earlier seen summer signing Jules Ahoka cancel out a spectacular opener from Torreense defender Volnei Feltes.

The winner owed much to the creativity of Enzo Le Fee and Granit Xhaka as the pair, who began the night on the bench, underlined their importance to the Black Cats.

Having watched their team-mates struggle to break down Torreense, Le Fee produced a delightful dinked pass into the penalty area to find Xhaka, with the Swiss flicking the ball first time into the path of Sadiki to score his first goal for the club.

‘When Granit touched it I heard him scream shoot and I didn’t think twice,' Sadiki said. 'I just hoped it was going in and the keeper wouldn’t save it. I’m really happy. It was a beautiful moment.’

Le Bris had taken the understandable risk by deciding to make seven changes for the fixture against arguably their weakest Europa League opponents, with Torreense currently lying 15th in the Portuguese second tier.

Noah Sadiki scored a stoppage time winner as Sunderland beat Portuguese side Torreense

Sunderland were forced to fight back following a stunning opener from Volnei Feltes

With just four points in the Premier League and five matches left to play this month, this was the match to give an opportunity to fringe members of the squad.

Torreense, though, have proved they are more than capable of springing a surprise. Their journey to the Europa League is one to rival Sunderland’s own having stunned Sporting Lisbon in last year’s Portuguese Cup final to qualify.

Their opening goal proved just as unexpected as that triumph.

Feltes was well inside his own half when he received possession and opted to embark on a forward run. After driving towards the Sunderland box, the Brazilian defender chopped between the challenges of Malick Fofana and Nilson Angulo and curled magnificently into the top corner.

Whatever happens to the minnows, they will come away with one of the best goals of this year’s competition.

Sunderland were forced to be patient when trying to break down their opponents, who dropped deep in the second half.

Le Bris turned to his bench moments after Nilson Angulo saw a header superbly kept out by goalkeeper Lucas Paes, with Omar Alderete failing to convert the follow-up.

His quadruple change of Xhaka, Le Fee, Reinildo and Nordi Mukiele proved crucial. The latter's cross for Ahoka to equalise with a header while Xhaka and Le Fee were central to Sadiki's winner.

'Winning this game just at the end is really special,' Le Bris said. 'It’s important for the club and the fans – they were fantastic once again.

'We are growing and we need experiences and I think the team showed the belief until the end which is really important for us. We showed again we have this mindset.'

Lyon 3-2 Crystal Palace – Eagles defence struggles again

By James Sharpe

Now Pierre Sage knows how Oliver Glasner feels. He knows how it feels to return to your old stomping ground, one where you achieved great things, and come away with nothing.

Just as Glasner took his new Nottingham Forest side back to Selhurst Park at the weekend and lost, so too did Sage as Crystal Palace endured a frustrating night in Lyon where he once helped save the French side from relegation.

In truth, a night like this has been coming. Palace cannot keep defending like this, be so open and unorganised, and expect to win matches. Sooner or later, you leave yourself with too much of a hill to climb.

It took Forest just three minutes to open the scoring at the weekend and Lyon needed only seven minutes and 31 seconds here. As always, it was all too easy.

A bog-standard corner into a crowded six-yard box and, despite the hordes of black Palace shirts, the ball still dropped to Lyon captain Corentin Tolisso.

Only this time, Lyon didn’t miss the rest of the chances that came their way like Forest did. On the stroke of half-time the hosts cut through Palace with simple passes and Keito Nakamura squared for Ernest Nuamah, who darted ahead of the defenders to finish. Tyrick Mitchell, for all his goalscoring exploits this season, made little effort to track his run.

It was this leakiness that caused a few shudders in the Palace boardroom, letting in 11 goals in their opening four matches, and sparked rumblings that Sage could be the first Premier League managerial casualty of the season.

Pierre Sage saw his Crystal Palace side fall to a 3-2 defeat against his former club Lyon

Ernest Nuamah was among the scores as Lyon capitalised on poor Crystal Palace defending

If there is a saving grace to which Palace can cling, it’s that when they do get it right under Sage, they do look menacing. There was little of that in a dreadful first half but, after the break, they clicked into gear. They are just, as yet, unable to find the balance.

Having wantaway forward Ismaila Sarr back in the line-up always helps with his directness in the final third.

And when you have the precision of Adam Wharton in your midfield, you will always stand a chance. It was his delightful first-time through ball to Yeremy Pino after a fine short corner routine that helped fire Palace back into the game.

The introduction of Daichi Kamada swung momentum further Palace’s way. He was bundled over inside the box but Palace’s furious protests fell on deaf ears. He had a shot from close range saved and, eventually, found the net after some chaos inside the box.

The only problem was that, by then, Lyon had already added a third courtesy of Pavel Sulc’s cheeky backheel flick.

Palace kept pushing as Chris Richards saw a late header from a corner saved but, ultimately, in vain. This time, it wasn’t enough. This time, they didn’t get away with it. This time, they gave themselves too much to do.

'I’m really frustrated about the result but really frustrated with the way of playing in the first half,' Sage said.

'Our game started at half-time and it was too late.

'We play too quickly sometimes with the idea to play out the back quickly in transition but we are not a team like this, we have only one or two players able to run and make the difference with the speed.

'That’s why we have to move with the ball, travel with the ball, and we did that in the second half.'

Brighton 4-0 Kauno Zalgiris – Seagulls cruise in Conference League

By Kieran Gill

It must be up there with the finest feelings in football – the relief that washes over when your team finally finds a way through that dastardly low block in front of them.

For Brighton, that arrived just before half-time. There was no blaming Kauno Zalgiris for their tactical approach. Hardly anyone other than Fabian Hurzeler, who was perhaps being polite when listing the Lithuanian side’s attributes before kick-off, gave them a hope in hell of escaping their first-ever fixture in the main stage of a European competition without losing.

Once Georginio Rutter found that first goal after 41 minutes, this turned into a much more enjoyable evening at the Amex Stadium. Even more so when Jack Hinshelwood, back from his ankle injury and appearing for the first time since August, added a second before the break.

With that, the floodgates opened, Brighton started their Conference League campaign in style, and truthfully, this competition should sit high on Hurzeler’s priorities this term.

Georginio Rutter scored the opening goal as Brighton overcame Lithuanian side Kauno Zalgiris

While we often praise Brighton for the way in which they work – including in the talents they find that the richer clubs then seek to steal – all that is missing is the silverware to complement it all.

Despite being brilliantly run, they have never won a major trophy in their history, and the Conference League is an opportunity to correct that. Other English clubs such as West Ham and Brighton’s rivals Crystal Palace have used it well. To sides such as Kauno Zalgiris, these are giants they are competing with, opponents competing on an entirely alien level to their own.

While Hurzeler had explained why Kauno Zalgiris would be confident – he warned us they were the champions of Lithuania and that they had won the Lithuanian Cup at the weekend – Brighton are in a happy place, too. This made it five successive victories for them in all competitions.

They are third in the Premier League behind only Manchester City and Arsenal, and into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup after winning away at Manchester United – a club now linked with liking Hurzeler in case they move on from Michael Carrick.

With that, we had an inkling as to how this game would go. Brighton would attack, and Kauno Zalgiris would defend, and the opening 30 minutes was all about blocks. From Anton Tolordava, from Nosa Iyobosa Edokpolor, from any Kauno Zalgiris player with a body for throwing at the ball.

But then arrived the breakthrough. It was a nice finish from Rutter despite the on-field officials thinking the ball had gone behind for a goal-kick in the build-up. It had not, and VAR overruled to award Brighton their opener. Hinshelwood added a second before the break before Rutter grabbed the third goal and Matt O’Riley the fourth.

‘We want to keep improving every game,' said Hinshelwood. 'What’s happened in the past has gone now. We want to look forward to the future.’

It was a good way to warm up for Palace in the Premier League on Sunday, though Brighton may be reminded by the Amex’s away end which side have won a trophy of late. Hurzeler should be embracing this European competition as a way to give his supporters a season to cherish.

Sports.title: FA pile pressure on Gianni Infantino - with chair saying he 'is not fit to be FIFA president' if he refuses to answer questions over World Cup sell-off
Sports.content:
Football Association chair Debbie Hewitt says Gianni Infantino is 'not fit to be FIFA president' if he does not answer questions about his World Cup sell-off plan or the Folarin Balogun case. Hewitt, also a FIFA vice-president, was one of the FIFA Council members who tried to hold Infantino to account in Zurich on Thursday at its first meeting since the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) plan came to light. Infantino apologised in the meeting for what he called 'mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process'. Hewitt said Council members had not received answers to 'anything we had specifically requested' regarding FFE or the Balogun incident, where the USA striker’s one-match ban was suspended following a call to Infantino from US President Donald Trump. Hewitt told reporters in Zurich: 'The man has to answer those questions, and if he doesn’t answer those questions, no, he’s not fit to be FIFA president, and that was what was shared in the meeting. 'He’s told us to submit those questions. There were so many of them, and now it’s up to him to do that, and do that in the open way. Debbie Hewitt has called for Gianni Infantino to answer questions over his World Cup sell-off plan and the Folarin Balogun affair ahead of FIFA's presidential elections 'The minimum is having the papers from FFE, because if there’s nothing to hide, then share them with us.' The FFE plan first became public knowledge in July. Infantino sought to create a company to manage the commercial interests of FIFA’s competitions, including the World Cup, but wanted a minority stake to be made available to private investors. The lead investor was set to be Thrive, a company founded by President Trump’s son-in-law’s brother, Josh Kushner, but the plan was abandoned on August 1 after three continental confederations rejected it. Among those within to publicly disagree with Infantino's plan were FIFA general secretary Mattias Grafstrom, senior advisor Carlos Cordeiro, chief operating officer Kevin Lamour and Arsene Wenger, who serves as FIFA's Chief of Global Football Development. Hewitt has previously written to Infantino demanding the release of documents related to FFE, while European football’s governing body UEFA has also submitted legal applications in the US seeking disclosure, which FIFA has challenged. Hewitt’s September letter to Infantino is also understood to have requested information on how the Balogun ban came to be suspended. Infantino has always maintained the decision was made independently of him by the FIFA disciplinary committee. Trump bragged about calling Infantino in the wake of Balogun's red card in the build-up to the USA's next game against Belgium, confirming that he 'asked for a review by FIFA'. 'I'm good at this stuff,' Trump added. 'That wasn't a foul. That wasn't even an infraction.' Hewitt said it was 'reasonable' for Infantino to request the submission of questions in writing, adding: 'He gave us the opportunity to say what we felt, and I think anybody that didn’t say what they felt in there, they’ve missed their opportunity. 'I have no new information that makes me feel any differently about how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of FIFA who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly, a promise again that we will get the information that we’ve requested.' Infantino said 'everyone had the opportunity to ask questions and express their views' on FFE. He added in a video released by FIFA: 'I apologised for the mistakes that we made in relation to the communication and consultation process related to the FIFA Forward Enterprise project which then led to many consequences. 'But what is important to remember is that it was a proposal, so in no way a done deal. Just a proposal that actually intended to enable FIFA to invest more in our member associations, as opposed to replacing support from existing resources.' UEFA has vowed to identify a credible candidate to stand against Infantino in next March’s presidential elections, having declared its loss of confidence in him in August over the FFE plan. The deadline for candidacies to be submitted is November 18.
