Sports.title: The not-so-obvious chance Leclerc missed to usurp Verstappen
Sports.content:
When Charles Leclerc had a better start than Max Verstappen and claimed the inside line for Turn 1, many in the media centre thought the Monegasque should have held his ground to take the lead.

However, Verstappen was on the outside, on the normal racing line that offered slightly more grip, and the Dutchman was prepared to take every risk. Verstappen had already told Autosport a day earlier that second or third place in the drivers' championship would mean nothing to him and that he simply wanted to go all-in for race victories.

In other words, Verstappen was willing to risk everything, although that was not even the main reason why Leclerc was unable to complete the move. The reference points drivers use under braking – such as the 150-metre and 100-metre boards – are on the right-hand side approaching Turn 1, but Leclerc could not see them because he was alongside Verstappen.

The Ferrari driver had to choose his braking point by instinct and tried to judge it as well as possible. As a result, he does not regard it as a missed opportunity, adding: "I would have done exactly the same."

No regrets in that respect, then, although Leclerc admits that he did let an opportunity to pass Verstappen slip away a few laps later.

Verstappen appeared to be managing his pace in the opening stages to preserve his tyres, but the four-time world champion revealed in the post-race press conference that this was not entirely a deliberate choice.

"We had a few laps with some deployment issues, so that's where Charles actually almost got me into Turn 7."

Verstappen managed to keep the lead into Turn 1, despite Leclerc's better launch off the line Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

Verstappen was not getting all the electrical power at the points where he needed it, something Arvid Lindblad at Red Bull's sister team Racing Bulls – which uses the same power unit – also complained about.

"Yeah, I also had issues with the PU, which we're trying to look after. I was getting driven past on the straights and the engine braking was really bad, which wasn't easy to drive", Lindblad said.

For Verstappen, the problem was limited to deployment issues in the opening stages of the Singapore Grand Prix, but Leclerc believes he should have taken advantage of them.

"There were a few opportunities in the first three laps when Max had the deployment issues, but I always thought that it was a one-off, so I wasn't really using my battery, which maybe was a mistake", Leclerc admitted.

Every time Verstappen was slow on the straights, the Ferrari driver thought it would be the last time, meaning he did not anticipate the problem recurring or adjust his own deployment strategy accordingly. By the time the issue occurred again, Leclerc could no longer react.

"When I was realising that he had no power at the end of the straight, I couldn't do anything. It was too late for me to use my power."

Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The question, however, is whether it would have made any difference to the final result. Track position is crucial at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, and in that scenario Leclerc would not have had to spend so long running in dirty air. On the other hand, he acknowledges that Verstappen was simply too strong and that Red Bull managed its tyres better.

"I don't know if it would have changed much. Of course, for the first stint it would have helped, but I think eventually they just had too much pace for us."

Leclerc made another attempt in the closing stages with a different strategy and a second stop under the virtual safety car, but a second win of the season, following his triumph at Silverstone, ultimately proved beyond reach.

"I’m happy, but not super happy. I mean, second place is a good result considering the tendency that we've had lately, where we were lacking just a little bit of pace.

"I feel like, particularly in qualifying yesterday, we had strong pace. Today in the race, Max had a bit more pace than we did, which was expected, but maybe we were a little bit closer than what we expected.

"It was a cool race and I believed in it until the very end, but unfortunately it wasn't quite enough."

Nevertheless, it was enough to secure Leclerc's first podium finish since the summer break and his fifth overall this F1 season.

Sports.title: The hidden factor that gives Verstappen and Red Bull extra hope for 2027
Sports.content:
With two victories in the last three Grands Prix and a deficit of just 0.196 seconds in Baku, Verstappen and Red Bull are firmly back at the front in Formula 1. The resurgence has understandably come too late to play a meaningful role in the title fight, although Verstappen now has a top-three finish in the drivers' championship in his sights.

Verstappen trails Lewis Hamilton by just eight points after the Singapore race weekend, while Russell is only 17 points ahead of the Dutchman. In other words, finishing runner-up in the championship is a realistic prospect.

When Autosport asked whether Verstappen is already starting to worry about 12 December – when the annual FIA gala takes place in Shanghai – a smile appeared on his face.

"Is that the prize-giving ceremony? Well, I was really ill last year! But we'll see what happens."

A second- or third-place finish in the final standings would not mean anything to Verstappen, however, as he told the Dutch media in the Singapore paddock. After the extremely difficult start to 2026 and the turnaround that followed, such an outcome might carry more significance than usual, but Verstappen does not see it that way.

"No, because ultimately you're not winning. You're not becoming world champion, and that's the only thing that matters to me."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Mark Sutton / Formula 1 via Getty Images

The aspect of 2026 that gives Verstappen the most confidence

While the title is out of reach this season, Red Bull's resurgence does provide confidence for next year.

"The most important thing is to look at where we were at the beginning of the season and where we are now", Verstappen said, referring to the fact that Red Bull was still fighting Haas and Alpine in China and Japan.

"All the upgrades that have been introduced on the car since then, and also the problems we had with certain parts of our car, we've managed to solve all of that. That's very important heading into next year.

"When you see that some teams still have doubts about certain aspects of their new upgrades, everything is working for us, and that's a real positive."

Verstappen has previously explained that certain limitations of the 2026 car can no longer be eliminated, meaning more fundamental changes will still be needed for next season's car.

Asked by Autosport whether the development direction is already 100% clear in that respect as well, and whether it gives Verstappen confidence, he replied:

"You never know fully. It's always very difficult to say that with things you're developing now that have never actually existed in real life, only on drawings.

“But everything we've introduced on the car this year has worked. That's very positive, and hopefully we can use that for next year."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing Photo by: Anni Graf - Formula 1 via Getty Images

What's the latest on Red Bull's long-awaited new wind tunnel?

Verstappen also brought up another, more hidden factor that could help Red Bull as 2027 progresses:

"Of course, we'll also have a new wind tunnel at our disposal next year. That's a separate matter, but naturally we hope it will work properly and help us as well."

The wind tunnel Red Bull currently uses is the oldest on the F1 grid. During his time as team principal, Christian Horner repeatedly described the wind tunnel as “a Cold War relic” and said working with the 70-year-old facility near Bedford was like looking at “two different watches”, highlighting how the correlation between the wind tunnel and on-track performance had failed more than once.

The fact that correlation has proved accurate in 2026 is therefore not something to be taken for granted, although Verstappen added that the new regulations and the dimensions of the cars may be helping as well.

"Those earlier problems might also have been partly down to the width and length of the car [and what you can replicate with the model]. Of course, we have different cars now, but the most important thing is that we'll be able to use the new wind tunnel next year."

Verstappen acknowledged that the new wind tunnel cannot yet be used for the initial development of the RB23 – after all, that development process is already underway – but it can be used for further development of the car throughout the season. That will still be crucial, as the second year under these regulations is also set to feature an intense development battle.

Pierre Waché previously told Autosport that the wind tunnel should be operational in early 2027, possibly in February, as Red Bull indicated in Singapore. However, the exact timing during the first quarter of 2027 will still depend on factors such as calibration, ensuring that Red Bull can have complete confidence in its new facility.

Sports.title: On This Day: Stroll wins final race before becoming a Formula 1 driver | Brief
Sports.content:
10 years ago today Lance Stroll scored his most recent victory to date, in his final race before he became a Formula 1 driver.

Just two weeks shy of his 18th birthday, Stroll’s promotion to F1 with Williams the following year had already been announced. He had clinched the European Formula 3 championship earlier in the season and won both of the preceding two races in the season-ending triple-header at the Hockenheimring.

For his last race at Prema, Stroll lined up fourth on the grid behind Joel Eriksson, Jake Hughes and Callum Ilott. Stroll wasn’t the only future F1 driver on the grid: others included Nikita Mazepin (10th), Zhou Guanyu (13th) and George Russell (15th). Anthoine Hubert, who tragically died in a Formula 2 crash in 2019, lined up seventh.

Sports.title: F1 could make call to move finale to Imola as late as ‘mid-November’ – report | Briefs
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses have said they want to know where the season finale will be held by mid-October.

The series intends to run its final two races as planned in Qatar and Abu Dhabi. However ongoing disruption caused by the US-Iran war has put that in doubt and led F1 to enlist the Imola circuit as a potential alternative venue for the final race.

A new report claims F1 could wait until the middle of November before deciding its plans for the final race of the season.

“There were also rumours in Malaysia and Singapore, where the sport has spent the last fortnight, that some sort of deal had been done between Qatar, the UAE and Iran to guarantee security, giving F1 increased confidence to press ahead,” adds the report in The Telegraph.

It comes after missile strikes hit an airport in nearby Saudi Arabia, whose world championship round was cancelled earlier this year. F1 is due to return to the country in March next year.

Sports.title: Official: Camara to make Formula 1 debut with Haas in 2027 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Ferrari junior driver Rafael Camara will make his Formula 1 debut for Haas next season.

Haas, one of Ferrari’s customer teams, confirmed the 21-year-old will take the seat vacated by Esteban Ocon at the end of the year. He is expected to partner Oliver Bearman, another member of Ferrari’s driver academy, who has driven for Haas since last year.

Camara has enjoyed a stellar rise through the junior formula series since being picked up by Ferrari in 2022. He currently leads the Formula 2 championship standings, with no indication yet whether the final rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi will be able to go ahead.

Like fellow Brazilian Gabriel Bortoleto, Camara won the Formula 3 championship at his first attempt. He also won the Formula Regional European Championship the year before.

Camara has already experienced one of Haas’s Formula 1 chassis in a Test of Previous Cars at the Autodromo do Algarve, which will hold the Portuguese Grand Prix next year. He has also tested for Ferrari.

Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu said he is “really excited to sign such a young, amazing talent like Rafael Camara.”

“He showed when we had him drive in our TPC program in Portugal that he could handle himself very well with not a huge amount of time to learn the car,” Komatsu continued, “he showed us more than just raw speed. Rafa managed to create an environment to get the best out of himself, it was very impressive and certainly the laps he completed were special.”

Camara thanked Komatsu, Haas team owner Gene Haas and the Scuderia Ferrari Driver Academy for his chance to make his F1 debut.

Sports.title: Colapinto tells his supporters to stop abusing rival drivers: “They don’t help me” | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Franco Colapinto has urged his supporters to stop abusing his rivals and others involved in the series online.

“They are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite,” Colapinto told his followers in a video posted on social media.

The FIA and Alpine issued statements in the last two months condemning the abuse which occured following the Dutch, Spanish and Azerbaijan grands prix. Neither specifically mentioned Colapinto’s supporters but both identified the victims of the abuse, including his team mate Pierre Gasly and FIA officials. “It has become a regular occurrence in recent races and cannot be condoned,” said Alpine in a statement last month.

Colapinto told his supporters the online abuse must stop.

“I know it makes you feel very proud when I do well, when I get points, me and the whole team, and I will always be very grateful for that,” he said. “But there are times when we end up attacking other pilots, other colleagues, my team mates, my mechanics, my engineers, people I work with day by day.

“I know they are thinking that they are defending me, but they are doing the opposite. They don’t help me. And I really want you to understand that this is what we have to change, all together.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We have to try to improve as a society, and to help me have a better performance, to help get my dream and my results, that is, to score points, I need you to help stop this, all of us together.”

Colapinto made his F1 debut with Williams in the second half of 2024, but the team had no space for him in their line-up for the following season. He joined Alpine, who promoted him to a race seat in place of Jack Doohan early in the season. Doohan later revealed he received death threats from those who wanted him out of the car.

Alpine issued the first in a series of reactions to abuse from Colapinto’s supporters this year following the Chinese Grand Prix, when Esteban Ocon collided with him. Some Colapinto supporters also accused Alpine of sabotaging Colapinto and failing to provide him with the same equipment as Gasly.

Recent flashpoints included the penalties Colapinto received for failing to slow sufficiently for yellow flags at Zandvoort, Colapinto’s brief delay behind Gasly at the Madring and the collision between the Alpine drivers and Lando Norris in Baku.

Sports.title: Social Media: Mekies extends contract to lead Red Bull until 2031 | Brief
Sports.content:
Red Bull has given a vote of confidence in its team principal Laurent Mekies by extending his contract to run the team until 2031.

Mekies took over from Christian Horner in charge of the team last year. Horner had run Red Bull since it entered F1 in 2005.

Under Mekies, Red Bull rebounded from a poor start to last season. From over 100 points behind, Max Verstappen came within two points of retaining his drivers’ championship title in one of the closest ever finishes to a world championship.

This year, in the team’s first season with its own power units designed in conjunction with Ford, Red Bull has won the last two grands prix.

Sports.title: Verstappen says Red Bull’s car was “scary” to drive early in 2026 | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Red Bull has made huge progress with a car which felt “scary” to drive early in the season, says Max Verstappen.

The four-times world champion has won the last two grands prix in a row and also took victory in the sprint race in Singapore last week. The team’s form has improved significantly since the beginning of the season, when Verstappen only reached the podium once in the first seven rounds.

Verstappen spun out of the British Grand Prix suffered costly spins in qualifying at the Red Bull Ring and Hungaroring as the team struggled to get on top of its car. However their most recent upgrades have transformed its performance.

“The car definitely felt a lot nicer from Baku onwards,” said Verstappen. “It’s just been a lot more balanced. Then naturally, of course, when you can compete a bit further up front without having too many issues with the car compared to the beginning of the year, where it was actually sometimes a bit scary to drive, that makes it a lot nicer.”

Verstappen finished a close second behind George Russell in Baku. He qualified only eighth but was in contention for pole position until his final lap was compromised by a yellow flag.

He has been undefeated since then and expects to remain competitive over the final rounds. “We’re not in a championship fight, and that’s why I think ’til the end we’ll just try to have a good time and try to add more podiums and hopefully a few wins.”

It is the second time in as many years that Red Bull has made a breakthrough with a troublesome car in the second half of a season. “Two completely different cars as well, with the regulations,” Verstappen noted. “Also two completely different problems.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“We had to find lap time. Plus, of course, also this year with the engine side of things, I think for everyone it’s been sometimes a bit complicated to get the most out of it.”

Red Bull needs to ensure they begin next year in better shape, said Verstappen.

“From race one to now, I think we’ve gained a lot of experience. Of course, we’re still not where we want to be, but I guess everyone will say the same thing.

“But we have learned so much and definitely also on the car side have fixed a lot of our weaknesses. We just need to keep improving, keep learning this year that so we can apply that also into next year.”

Sports.content:
Cadillac remain yet to score a point in their first season in Formula 1 but Valtteri Bottas says their progress is clear to see.

“We are definitely seeing an improvement somewhere every weekend,” he told the Financial Times. “It’s not necessarily in the results yet, but it’s in how we operate as a team in different areas.”

Bottas scored all 10 of his grand prix victories for Mercedes. He drove for the world champions between 2017 and 2021.

Cadillac is based partly at Silverstone, a short distance from Mercedes’ Brackley factory. Asked whether his new team’s facilities are better than the world champions’, Bottas replied: “I would say so.”

Sports.title: Formula 1 teams need decision ‘by mid-October’ on whether final races will go ahead | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Formula 1 team bosses say they need to know by the middle of this month whether the series’ final two races will go ahead as planned.

Qatar and Abu Dhabi are due to hold the final two races of the season in November and December. However the war in Iran, which forced the cancellation of races in nearby Bahrain and Saudi Arabia six months ago, put those plans in jeopardy.

F1 has a back-up plan to hold an alternative event at Imola. F1 CEO Stefano Domenicali previously said a decision would be made by mid-September. Teams say they need to know one way or the other soon.

“I believe Stefano was targeting to tell us in mid-October,” said Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu in Azerbaijan. “So, we all know what the situation is.

“I believe that Imola is getting ready in case we have to do it. I think the challenges are, for instance, things like European motorhome structure, etcetera. All those people who look after them, they have a winter job, so we need to find alternative people to do that.

“But I’m sure we all, as a family, community, will make sure if we have to do that, that will happen. But hopefully, as a baseline, we can go to Qatar and Abu Dhabi. That would be really good.”

Drivers have pointed out the conditions could be very cold if the series races in Imola in December. However Audi team principal Mattia Binotto believes it would be no cooler than some other venues the series visits.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

“The main challenges are more organisation and logistics,” he said. “I would think, from a technical point, often we may say wintertime and snow tyres, but at the end, as a matter of fact, the average temperature in Imola in that time of the year is hotter than Las Vegas.

“So I don’t think that’s a true concern. It’s more from the organisation and the logistics, really. And again, mid-October, hopefully we may do the right decision.”

Domenicali told the Financial Times the “decision is done” but also admitted “Imola is the place that eventually, in case of a force majeure before a certain date, would be ready to host it.”

Sports.title: Rico Verhoeven Accepts Deontay Wilder Fight Offer
Sports.content:
Rico Verhoeven has accepted an offer to fight Deontay Wilder on December 11, potentially adding another heavyweight bout to the Tyson Fury–Anthony Joshua undercard in Cardiff.

Wilder’s response is still outstanding, and the terms need to be negotiated. However, Verhoeven has made his willingness clear as he looks to continue boxing after his stoppage loss to Oleksandr Usyk.

“I can’t confirm just yet,” Verhoeven told talkSPORT. “What I can tell you is that they offered me the fight. They offered me Deontay Wilder. I said yes.” “The details need to be talked about still. But for that, I’m waiting on a response. So, if there’s a yes from the other side, it’s going to happen.”

Verhoeven did not identify who made the offer. His comments introduce another possible opponent for Wilder, who had been linked with a fight against Jai Opetaia on the same card.

Wilder would give Verhoeven an opportunity to turn the praise he received against Usyk into a victory over an established heavyweight. Going deep into a fight with Usyk earned him attention, but beating Wilder would give him something firmer to build on.

There is an obvious danger in treating Wilder as a faded name to collect. His right hand still gives Verhoeven a reason to be careful. Yet Wilder’s reduced activity and hesitant offense in recent performances could allow the Dutchman time to settle into the fight.

Verhoeven also made clear that he intends to remain in boxing after considering several offers.

“I want to make a statement,” he said. “I want to show that … I am able to transition into the sport of boxing.”

Peter Fury remains in his corner, and Verhoeven is already looking beyond the proposed December appearance. He hopes Joshua beats Fury because he wants that fight himself.

“I hope that Anthony Joshua’s winning that fight because then I’m next for him.”

Beating Wilder would give that ambition a stronger foundation. First, Wilder needs to accept.

Putting Wilder against Verhoeven spares Jai Opetaia a bizarre heavyweight detour that threatened to derail his cruiserweight meeting with David Benavidez. That alone makes it slightly more tolerable than the initial rumor, but it remains a carnival booking.

Wilder has looked completely spent for years. At 40, his trigger is hesitant, his balance is compromised, and the reflex to pull the trigger on his right hand has eroded. Grinding past an aging Derek Chisora by a 12-round split decision did not erase the one-sided beatings he took against Joseph Parker, Fury, or Zhilei Zhang.

Verhoeven, 37, proved his toughness by surviving into the eleventh round against Oleksandr Usyk, but surviving is not contending. He is an elite kickboxer with a tiny boxing resume, still learning basic ring craftsmanship under boxing rules.

Sticking two aging names together with mismatched pedigrees belongs on the preliminary streaming portion of the broadcast, not sharing equal billing right beneath Fury against Joshua. It caters to novelty rather than sport.

Sports.title: Frank Warren Rates Dubois Wardley Rematch Even
Sports.content:
Frank Warren still views Daniel Dubois against Fabio Wardley as a 50-50 fight heading into Saturday night at the O2 Arena in London. Even though Dubois won their violent clash in May, Wardley dropped him in the first and third rounds, proving his power can alter the course of the bout instantly.

Dubois weathered that storm to secure the stoppage, yet those early visits to the canvas give Wardley massive confidence that he can flip the script. The real challenge for Wardley will be finishing the job if he gets Dubois in trouble again.

“I just feel that either of them can win. I think it’s still an even-money fight,” Warren told talkSPORT. “Daniel will go as favorite because he’s probably … got more experience as amateur as well as pro.”

Surviving clean bombs once does not guarantee Dubois can take them a second time. At the same time, reckless aggression could cost either man dearly.

“You’ve got to remember he called for this rematch,” Warren said of Wardley. “It was a brutal fight in May, and here we are now, and it’s on, and he believes that he can win it.”

Warren believes victory hinges on establishing the jab instead of hunting for wild knockout blows right away. For Dubois, a sharp jab keeps Wardley on the outside and stops him from landing cold early.

“For me, the key to this fight is getting behind the jab,” Warren said. “Not looking to lead with big punches, to actually go out and try and … jab and then let your shots go.”

Both heavyweights know what to expect after their first battle. The winner will be the man who made the right adjustments and capitalizes on them first. Neither fighter is built to play it safe, which is why Warren expects another explosive finish before the final bell sounds. Dubois proved his resilience, Wardley proved his firepower, and both step into the ring knowing one clean shot can end it.

When promoters preach boxing fundamentals and patience for a high-profile rematch, they are usually trying to protect their fighters from another grueling brawl. The problem is that fans are paying for fireworks, not a tactical chess match.

“They know each other’s strengths and weaknesses,” Warren said. “It’s who’s learned from the last fight and who can exploit what he’s learned.”

If Dubois and Wardley actually listen to Warren and spend 36 minutes trading cautious jabs from ring center, public reaction will be brutal. Paying premium pay-per-view prices on DAZN just to watch two sluggers neutralize each other behind the lead hand is the exact opposite of what made their May fight thrilling.

“I don’t think the fight’s going to go the distance, whatever happens.”

The thin undercard makes that risk even worse. Here, there is zero safety net. If the headliner devolves into a safety-first sparring session, the whole broadcast will disappoint, and the backlash from paying customers will land squarely on Warren.

Sports.title: Ermal Hadribeaj Taunts Sebastian Fundora Ahead Of Upset Bid
Sports.content:
Sebastian Fundora gave Ermal Hadribeaj an icy glare during Thursday’s final presser at The Cosmopolitan of Las Vegas. Tension spiked when Hadribeaj aimed an imaginary sniper rifle directly at the champion’s chin.

Fundora kept his cool. The towering titlist didn’t swat the hand away. He didn’t shove the challenger. He simply stared him down, leaving the theatrics entirely to the Albanian contender.

Many boxing fans dismiss Saturday’s DAZN broadcast as a total mismatch. They might be forgetting history. Brian Mendoza knocked Fundora out cold in 2023. Erickson Lubin battered him. Tim Tszyu landed heavy leather on him. Those past fights prove the champion absorbs massive punishment when his defense gets sloppy.

The height gap between the two southpaws is ridiculous. DAZN’s faceoff clip showed the eight-inch difference clearly. Hadribeaj stands five feet ten inches tall, forcing him to point his fake rifle skyward toward Fundora’s 6’6″ stature.

Landing real leather will prove vastly tougher than gesturing on stage. Hadribeaj has to slip past huge reaching punches. He must escape clean counters. Closing distance against the champion is tricky because Fundora actually loves trading in tight phone booths.

That exact habit offers Hadribeaj his clearest path toward an upset. Fundora constantly surrenders his height by planting his feet inside. Shorter opponents suddenly find themselves in prime position to connect clean shots.

Mendoza exploited that flaw with a brutal left hook. Hadribeaj hasn’t demonstrated that kind of world class power against elite fighters yet. Still, writing off the challenger ignores the defensive gaps Fundora regularly presents.

The champion stayed composed on stage. Bringing that same discipline into Saturday night keeps the challenger outside, preventing Hadribeaj from getting the messy close-quarters brawl he desperately craves.

Hadribeaj’s taunting is unlikely to get Fundora to fight with reckless anger. Fundora has been through heated build-ups before, taken real damage in wars with Lubin and Tszyu, and generally keeps an even temper outside the ring. At the presser, he watched the sniper pantomime without flinching or retaliating.

The interesting part is that Hadribeaj probably does not even need to make Fundora angry to get the fight he wants. Fundora naturally surrenders his eight-inch height advantage without any emotional prompting. His default setting is to march forward, plant his feet, and throw uppercuts and hooks in a phone booth.

He gives up range as a matter of style, not because his temper got the better of him. That was how Mendoza caught him, and that was how Tszyu landed punishing overhand rights before the cut changed the dynamic.

Hadribeaj’s hurdle is what happens when he actually gets inside. Fundora is lethal in close quarters, throwing sharp uppercuts that chew fighters up as they try to stay under his reach. If Hadribeaj spends energy looking for one theatrical, loaded-up counter shot against a guy who throws heavy volume in the pocket, he risks getting overwhelmed by the sheer number of punches coming back at him.

Sports.title: Devin Haney-Shakur Stevenson Purse Clash Could Sink Fight
Sports.content:
Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson finally agreed on 145 pounds, but dividing the revenue could scuttle their bout before either man steps into the ring.

Talks have reached a critical point, putting the targeted November 28 date in Atlanta in real jeopardy. Settling on a catchweight gave both camps a clear target. Splitting the revenue creates a deeper rift because it hinges entirely on personal market valuation.

Haney’s November 28 date allows almost no room for further haggling. Just over six weeks remain on the calendar, meaning both boxers require signed contracts right now to launch proper training camps. Every day squandered bickering over percentages pushes that target closer to collapse.

Haney has every right to challenge an even split. He already proved his drawing power as a headline attraction. Agreeing to parity would concede commercial ground that his team believes Shakur has yet to earn.

Backing from Turki Alalshikh changes the financial landscape. Deep financial support guarantees a massive overall purse, but funding a guarantee is not the same as generating revenue through paying customers. Haney’s side will almost certainly demand terms that honor that distinction.

“A potential fight between Devin Haney and Shakur Stevenson is facing obstacles,” Mike Coppinger reported, adding that negotiations were “reaching a critical stage to keep this fight alive.

Coppinger did not reveal the figures being discussed, but if Shakur wants an equal or larger share, that could be where the talks are getting stuck.

Haney holds the cards here. Devin has options, commercial value, and a willing audience. Shakur cannot afford another inactive stretch where he sits around polishing belts while the division moves on without him. If he lets his ego dictate both the scale and the purse split, Haney will simply walk, leaving Shakur with an empty calendar and nobody to blame but himself.

Sports.title: Ryan Garcia-Teofimo Lopez Talks Advance For Early 2027
Sports.content:
Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are moving closer to a welterweight title fight in the first quarter of 2027, according to Mike Coppinger.

The January-through-March target gives Ryan a major payday to pursue without squeezing in another appearance in December. No firm date or venue was included in the update, and the fight has yet to be announced.

“Ryan Garcia and Teofimo Lopez are now in advanced talks to fight in the first quarter of 2027, sources tell. Expect this welterweight title fight to happen next. And it’s a big one,” said Coppinger on X. “I believe the Garcia-Teo fight will happen regardless of the WBA’s ruling here. Catterall could end up being elevated.”

Teofimo’s WBA mandatory obligation to Jack Catterall remains unresolved, but that doesn’t have to stop the Ryan fight. The WBA belt isn’t needed to sell this matchup. Ryan’s WBC championship would still be available, and the appeal comes largely from putting these two recognizable names together.

The belt’s greater value to Teofimo could be at the negotiating table. Arriving as a fellow champion gives him another argument when discussing his share of the money. Relinquishing it would remove that bargaining point.

However, if Ryan, his promoters, and the financial backers are willing to offer Teofimo comparable money without the WBA title, keeping it becomes harder to justify. He could surrender the belt, remove the mandatory obligation, and proceed directly toward the bigger payday.

Facing Catterall first would introduce a risk that negotiations alone cannot remove. Teofimo could lose, suffer an injury, or come through a difficult fight needing more recovery time. Any of those outcomes could affect the timing or financial terms of a Ryan matchup.

Catterall has publicly opposed stepping aside. The WBA ordered the fight and gave the camps until October 22 to reach an agreement, leaving Teofimo with a decision if the organization insists on enforcing its mandatory.

That makes the financial terms of the Ryan negotiations especially interesting. If the offer depends heavily on Teofimo bringing his championship, he has a reason to seek permission to bypass Catterall. If the money is essentially the same either way, relinquishing offers a straightforward route.

The WBA can determine what Teofimo must do to retain its belt. Whether that belt is worth keeping could ultimately come down to how much Ryan’s side is willing to pay him without it.

Sports.title: Agility Drills Cannot Mask Canelo Alvarez’s Fading Gas Tank
Sports.content:
Canelo Alvarez is putting his feet through plenty of work ahead of Christian Mbilli, but a movement-heavy approach could leave him short of energy before their October 31 fight reaches its toughest rounds.

Alvarez trying to reinvent himself as a nimble mover at age 36 looks like a recipe for disaster. The math simply does not add up when looking at his gas tank and output history.

Against Terence Crawford, Canelo was barely working, averaging just 28 punches a round while trying to plant his feet, load up on single power shots, and conserve energy. Even with that rock-bottom volume and virtually zero ring traversal, he was visibly gassing by round six. His body has shown clear signs of mileage for several fights now, and stamina has always been his primary limitation whenever opponents force him to work at a sustained clip.

Now his camp is circulating clips of him running agility ladders, doing cone drills, and practicing lateral movement to stay off the ropes against Christian Mbilli. While it makes for good social media optics, applying that in a real fight is completely detached from reality. Moving your feet constantly under pressure takes far more conditioning than standing your ground and picking spots.

The work doesn’t stop for Canelo! 💯 🎥: @Canelo 🎟️ Buy #CaneloMbilli NOW at https://t.co/yxybEeoyF5 | Oct 31 | Mexico vs The World | Live on DAZN | @RingMagazine https://t.co/zDOn7OR9xH — DAZN Boxing (@DAZNBoxing) October 15, 2026

Mbilli is a pure volume puncher who thrives on throwing 70 to 80 punches a round, pressing forward with reckless abandon. If Canelo’s tactical adjustment is to skip around the ring, make short escapes, and play keep-away, he is volunteering to burn the exact energy reserve he does not have. Avoiding shots on the move still costs cardio, and Mbilli will not politely hit pause between drills to let him recover.

Canelo has never been an elusive ring mechanic. He built his career on upper-body slips, tight high-guard defense, and brutal counter-punching off a solid base. The only way he beats a swarmer like Mbilli is by doing what he has always done best: planting both feet and landing shots hard enough to break Mbilli’s spirit and stop the forward march. If he spends the first four rounds burning his legs on lateral movement, Mbilli is going to drown him in volume before the second half of the fight even gets started.

That script is practically already written. If Canelo gasses out trying to play Willie Pep at 36 and drops the belt to Mbilli, the post-fight press conference will be a masterclass in deflection.

Fighters with that level of clout rarely say, “I cooked up a terrible game plan in camp, convinced myself I could turn the clock back eight years, and completely misjudged my own gas tank.” Instead, the narrative instantly shifts into passive corporate speak. It becomes “we made tactical adjustments that didn’t materialize on the night,” or Eddy Reynoso will quietly take the heat to protect the brand, talking about camp fatigue or lingering elbow issues that allegedly flared up in the dressing room.

The irony is that Canelo’s entire late career identity has been built on stubborn pride. He genuinely believes his ring IQ can outsmart the physiological clock. Attempting to dance and pivot away from an engine like Mbilli is purely an ego-driven attempt to prove he still possesses the agility of his prime 154- and 160-pound runs.

Sports.title: Fabio Wardley Puts Rematch Pressure on Daniel Dubois
Sports.content:
Fabio Wardley believes Daniel Dubois faces the greater pressure in their rematch, with the champion needing to repeat his victory against a challenger who believes he has corrected the mistakes that cost him their first fight.

Dubois recovered from two early knockdowns to win. Wardley admits he became overconfident after that success, giving the champion an opportunity to recover. If Wardley avoids those mistakes, Dubois could face a different task this time.

“I think that for me, like again, it’s something Daniel’s gone through, but now he’s got three losses on his record,” Wardley told Fight Wire. “Two of those to Oleksandr Usyk, so you chalk them up a bit differently.”

Wardley argues that another defeat would put Dubois in a difficult position, while he views his own first loss as something he can repair.

“It just frees me up. It’s okay, we had a loss. Things didn’t go too great. Not the end of the world,” he said.

The pressure on Dubois goes beyond the number of defeats. He needs to demonstrate that his previous victory was repeatable, rather than a result that depended on Wardley getting careless after putting him down twice.

Wardley believes he has identified how he let that opportunity slip. Better decisions could leave Dubois with fewer chances to recover, although maintaining pressure without wasting energy or walking into punches will require more than determination.

“There’s a few adjustments to be made, a few things we need to capitalize on better, and then the fight’s ours,” Wardley said.

Dubois proved he could beat Wardley that night. Whether he can handle a more disciplined version remains unanswered. Wardley still has to deliver those improvements under fire, but the champion cannot assume the same openings will appear again.

Wardley also questioned Dubois’s conflicting comments about his punching power, suggesting some of his opponent’s remarks sound rehearsed.

“Especially when the camera comes out, some of the lines you can very much tell are forced, or they’ve at least been told to him to put in there,” he said.

The verbal sparring adds to Wardley’s portrayal of himself as the more relaxed fighter. Dubois’s harder task is showing that he has answers for the changes Wardley brings into the ring.

Sports.title: Edgar Berlanga Calls Sebastian Fundora A Cheat Code
Sports.content:
Edgar Berlanga can’t understand how Sebastian Fundora fits into the 154-pound division. Looking at a workout photo of the WBC champion, he compared Fundora to a video game character and suggested he should be making his money in the NBA.

Fundora’s long legs and arms dominate the picture. Berlanga fights two divisions above him at super middleweight, yet even he sounds taken aback by the sight of someone that tall competing at light middleweight.

How do they allow him to box at 154lb he’s a cheat code character from GTA WTF 🤣🤣🤣 listen he would have been a 200 million dollar NBA player. This is unacceptable he looks like a building https://t.co/AYW3y9aSuM — Edgar Berlanga Jr (@EdgarBerlangaJr) October 15, 2026

Berlanga isn’t the first fighter to reach for a video game comparison. After Fundora stopped Erickson Lubin in April 2022, Terence Crawford called him “a cheat code,” comparing him to a created Fight Night boxer with the height turned up in a smaller weight class.

It’s an understandable reaction. Finding sparring partners who can prepare an opponent for Fundora is difficult enough. Then comes the task of getting past those long arms and landing on a head that sits well above the usual target.

The odd thing is that Fundora often gives opponents a chance by coming to them. He likes fighting up close, throwing short punches rather than spending every round keeping shorter men at the end of his jab. They don’t always have to chase him to get their shots off.

That makes him entertaining, even if Berlanga thinks his dimensions look unfair. Fundora can make 154. The men across from him have to figure out the rest.

His WBC title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj this Saturday is a harder sell. Hadribeaj is the mandatory challenger, but most fans know little about him. They’re waiting to see Fundora against the bigger names in a division with plenty to offer.

Hadribeaj gets his chance to make himself known once the fight starts. Until then, Fundora’s unusual frame is likely to draw more conversation than the matchup itself.

Ghana News.title: Fiscal policy implementation poses downside risk to inflation – BoG
Ghana News.content:
Bank of Ghana Governor, Dr Johnson Asiama.

The Bank of Ghana has described the implementation of the government’s fiscal policy in 2026 as posing a downside risk to inflation.

According to its Monetary Policy Report, the US-Iran conflict, with its impact on crude oil prices, may put pressure on the government to offer periodic reliefs, which may pose some challenges to the budget.

“The rest of 2026 is expected to witness a scale-up in government spending and there are concerns over the absorptive capacity of contractors executing government projects, which could have implications for inflation”.

It, however, assured that the government remains committed to controlling expenditure, boosting efficiency gains, and adhering to value-for-money standards.

At the same time, it pointed out that the government aims to strengthen domestic revenue mobilisation to enable it to meet debt service obligations, thus ensuring long-term debt sustainability.

“It must also be noted that the full completion of bilateral and commercial debt restructuring is expected to lead to an increase in future debt service payments”.

With respect to debt sustainability, it called for the strengthening of fiscal management to reduce the rate of debt accumulation and the resulting debt servicing costs.

“The currently high proportion of short-term debt heightens rollover and refinancing risks, potentially limiting the fiscal space for productive investments and growth-enhancing expenditures. In the long term, higher domestic savings will be required to meet external debt repayments, with potential implications for exchange rate stability”, it added.

The Central Bank concluded that sustained real Gross Domestic Product growth, lower real interest rates, and continued exchange rate stability are the prerequisites for improving Ghana’s debt sustainability and preserving its status of moderate risk of debt distress.

Ghana News.title: Organised Labour should seek fair adjustment, not excessive pay rise – Labour consultant
Ghana News.content:
Labour consultant Austin Gamey has urged Organised Labour to pursue a fair adjustment in the 2027 base pay negotiations, cautioning that excessively high expectations could delay an agreement with government.

He said the proposed increase should be guided by economic data, including previous inflation projections, actual inflation figures and current forecasts, rather than perceptions about the cost of living.

Speaking in an interview on Joy FM’s Newsnight o thursday, octoer 15, Mr Gamey said labour was justified in seeking an adjustment but needed to ensure its expectations reflected prevailing economic conditions.

“I wouldn't like to use the word demand, for an adjustment that is commensurate with the situation on our hands. But it has to be based upon data,” he said.

Mr Gamey explained that Organised Labour should first establish the extent to which workers' purchasing power needed to be restored before determining any additional adjustment to cushion them against rising living costs.

He added that workers' productivity and the country's economic performance should also inform the negotiations.

According to him, pushing for an excessively high increase could create further inflationary pressures and undermine the intended benefits of higher wages.

“The macro indicators are quite reasonable, and therefore you can't go too high, otherwise you're rather creating further inflation in the system, and it's your own making,” he said.

Mr Gamey's comments come as government and Organised Labour prepare to negotiate the 2027 base pay, with the current agreement reflecting a nine per cent increase across the Single Spine Salary Structure for 2026.

Organised Labour has maintained that slowing inflation has not translated into lower market prices or restored workers' purchasing power, and intends to make a strong case for a higher adjustment.

However, Mr Gamey questioned what he described as an overemphasis on the high cost of living, arguing that prices of some commodities, including tomatoes and ginger, had begun to decline.

He urged stakeholders to rely on economic data in assessing price movements rather than generalising about the cost of living.

On the possibility of a deadlock before the 2027 Budget is presented, Mr Gamey said the parties should resort to established dispute-resolution mechanisms rather than allow negotiations to stall.

He suggested mediation through the National Labour Commission or an alternative dispute resolution centre to help government and organised labour reach an agreement.

Ghana News.title: BoG maintains medium-term inflation target of 8 ± 2%
Ghana News.content:
The Bank of Ghana has maintained its medium-term inflation target of 8 ± 2% barring any shocks.

This follows a third consecutive increase in year-on-year inflation in September 2026.

At the 132nd Monetary Policy Committee, the Committee expressed concerns about the elevated external risks arising from the global economy amid relatively favourable domestic conditions.

The Committee also observed an uptick in headline inflation in August, driven largely by an increase in non-food inflation.

Despite this uptick, the Committee noted easing inflation expectations and core inflation over the period, suggesting moderating underlying inflationary pressures.

Following its evaluation of global and domestic developments, it maintained that headline inflation remained on course to return to its target range of 8±2% over the medium term, barring any shocks.

“Upward adjustments in utility tariffs, rising ex-pump petroleum prices, strengthening of the US dollar, and adverse spillovers from global supply chain disruptions posed upside risks to the inflation outlook,” it said.

These risks were, however, expected to be largely offset by downside risks emanating from fiscal consolidation, improved food supply conditions, and exchange rate stability.

Headline inflation rose to 5.2% in September 2026, up from 5.0% in August 2026.

Consumer Price Inflation went up 1.1% month-on-month in September, reversing the previous month's trend.

Food Inflation picked up to 4.0% in September from 3.0% in August, whilst non-food inflation eased slightly to 6.2% in September 2026 from 6.8% in August 2026.

Ghana News.title: Sammi Awuku urges NPP Germany to unite ahead of 2028 elections
Ghana News.content:
Sammi Awuku

New Patriotic Party (NPP) Member of Parliament for Akuapem North, Sammi Awuku, has urged the party’s Germany Branch to prioritise unity, humility and collective commitment as it prepares for the 2028 general elections.

He said the newly elected national executives and party structures at all levels must work together to strengthen the NPP and position it to regain power in 2028.

Mr Awuku made the call when he addressed members of the NPP Germany Branch during a Thanksgiving Service and Unity Dinner held in Hannover from October 9 to 10, 2026.

The two-day event began with an Islamic prayer session in Frankfurt on Friday and ended with a Christian worship service and Unity Dinner at Hütten Str. 228 in Hannover on Saturday.

The gathering was attended by NPP MP for New Juaben South Michael O. Baafi, Member of the NPP National Council of Elders Eileen Mary Posch-Oduro, Mayor of Mündenheim Rheinland-Pfalz Raymond Höptner, NPP Germany Branch Chairman Dr Nana B. Enninful and Hannover Chapter Chairman Bright Otchere.

Mr Awuku described his visit as that of a “John the Baptist”, saying it was intended to prepare the ground for an anticipated engagement between the NPP Germany Branch and former Vice-President Dr Mahamudu Bawumia on November 21.

Dr Bawumia is expected to visit Germany at the invitation of the Konrad Adenauer Stiftung and interact with members of the NPP Germany Branch.

Mr Awuku said the new national executives needed the cooperation of all party members and structures to enable the NPP to effectively campaign for the 2028 presidential election.

He also stressed the importance of the party’s external branches in contributing to efforts to address what he described as Ghana’s current socio-economic challenges.

Leadership

Mr Awuku reminded party members that the NPP belonged to everyone who served it and urged them to support the newly elected executives.

He called on the leadership of the Germany Branch, particularly its chairman, Dr Nana Benyin Enninful, to exercise humility, respect and selflessness in the discharge of their responsibilities.

“A mandate is a privilege, not a licence to disregard others; trust must be earned through service,” he said.

“A leader who wins the hearts of the people strengthens the office; one who loses their trust weakens it.”

Drawing on his experience as a young party organiser, Mr Awuku said his success in previous youth and national organiser contests demonstrated the importance of mobilising and working with party members.

He used the proverb, “It is the feathers that make the bird beautiful,” to emphasise the contribution of individual members to the strength and influence of the party.

Criticism of government

Turning to national politics, Mr Awuku described the work of the NPP’s 87 opposition MPs as challenging but said they would remain committed to what they considered to be Ghana’s best interests.

He criticised the government’s performance in areas including education, health, sports and industry.

He also raised concerns about the implementation of the government’s 24-hour economy policy and cited what he described as a failure to secure placement for more than 50,000 Junior High School graduates.

He urged Ghanaians in the country and abroad to remain actively engaged in the political process.

He also encouraged members of the diaspora to engage their families in Ghana on the NPP’s policies and vision ahead of the 2028 elections.

Mr Awuku urged the Germany Branch to put past challenges behind it and concentrate on rebuilding its structures and strengthening its mobilisation efforts.

“Unity is not a slogan; it is the work members do together,” he said.

“When leaders serve with humility and members contribute with commitment, the whole Branch becomes stronger.”

Other speakers at the event also appealed to members to support the NPP and contribute to efforts to strengthen the party ahead of the 2028 general elections.

Ghana News.title: The Inconvenient Truth: We cannot pray for the cure while protecting the disease
Ghana News.content:
Ing Prof Douglas Boateng

Africa’s greatest obstacle is not that we fail to see what ails us, but that we have grown comfortable defending it. The unborn child will inherit our choices, not our excuses.

By Ing. Prof. Douglas Boateng, Chartered Director UK | Chartered Engineer UK | Fellow, Institute of Directors UK | Fellow, Ghana Institution of Engineering | Governance, Industrialisation and Supply Chain Strategist | Founder, Boardroom Governance Summit | Founder and Scriber, NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom)

A doctor will tell you that the most difficult patient to treat is not the one who is unaware of his illness. It is the one who knows exactly what is wrong, understands the consequences, has access to treatment, and still defends the habits that are making him sick. Yet when whole societies behave in the same way, we tend to give it gentler names: politics, culture, loyalty, survival, or simply the way things are done.

This is one of the most uncomfortable truths facing many developing societies, including our own. Our greatest difficulty is not that we fail to see what ails us. It is that we see it clearly, sometimes defend its causes, and still expect our children to inherit a healthy nation.

We complain about corruption while admiring unexplained wealth that happens to benefit us. We condemn indiscipline while seeking exemptions from the rules that inconvenience us.

We denounce environmental destruction while buying from, financing or shielding those responsible. Then we raise our hands and pray for national transformation. Even the most generous rain, however, cannot yield a healthy harvest from soil the farmer insists on poisoning.

NyansaKasa: “A society that protects the causes of its suffering should not expect time alone to deliver the cure.”

When The Abnormal Becomes Normal

Corruption, inequality and weak institutions are not uniquely African conditions. The real danger begins when abnormal behaviour becomes normal and normal behaviour starts to look strange.

Consider the procurement officer who insists on due process and is accused of delaying progress. Consider the board director who raises an uncomfortable question about a doubtful investment, only to be met with the kind of glances usually reserved for someone who has arrived at a funeral carrying a trumpet. And consider the citizen who refuses a dishonest arrangement and is gently advised to “be realistic”.

Since when did being realistic mean making peace with what is wrong? What once shocked us becomes familiar; what is familiar becomes tolerated; what is tolerated becomes defended; and what is defended eventually becomes institutionalised. At that point a society is no longer merely suffering from a problem. It is helping the problem survive.

NyansaKasa(words of wisdom): “When wrongdoing becomes ordinary and integrity becomes exceptional, society has not merely lost its standards; it has reversed its moral compass.”

When Political Colours Decide Right And Wrong

Political competition is healthy and necessary. It becomes unhealthy, however, when party loyalty replaces moral consistency.

Too often, a questionable contract is condemned when linked to opponents and explained away when linked to allies. The evidence stays the same; only the colours change. It is almost as though morality alters its chemical composition whenever a government changes, becoming poisonous in opposition and medicinal in power.

This observation is not aimed at any party, government or country; it describes a human weakness that crosses borders. Its cost, however, is real. When wrongdoing is judged by affiliation, institutions lose authority, citizens lose confidence, and accountability becomes selective. A nation must always be larger than the parties competing to govern it.

The Environment Does Not Accept Our Excuses

Nowhere is the contradiction more visible than in how we treat our land and water. In January 2025, Ghana Water shut its Bonsa headworks, which supplied about 75 per cent of the drinking water for Tarkwa Nsuaem, because illegal mining had so polluted the river that, in the plant manager’s words, it had become “just mud”. Such activity is sustained by a web of financiers, operators, buyers, weak enforcement, economic hardship and social tolerance. At times the same community that demands government action also expects enforcement officers to spare particular relatives, friends or the politically connected. That is rather like a patient demanding treatment while threatening the doctor who tries to remove the infection.

Flooding tells a similar story. On 3 June 2015, floodwaters and a fire at a fuel station near Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra claimed more than 150 lives. A decade later, drains remain choked with refuse and structures still sit across waterways, yet whenever the streets flood, rainfall becomes the principal suspect. Polluted water, after all, does not ask for party membership before it enters a household.

NyansaKasa(words of wisdom): “A nation cannot continuously block its waterways with yesterday’s indiscipline and expect tomorrow’s rainfall to negotiate politely.”

Corruption Is Never A Solo Performance

Transparency International’s 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index scored Ghana 43 out of 100, against a sub Saharan average of 32, while UNCTAD estimates that Africa loses about $88.6 billion every year to illicit financial flows, more than the continent receives in development aid. It is convenient, but incomplete, to treat corruption as something that begins and ends with public officials. Corruption usually depends on a chain of participants: someone offers, someone receives, someone prepares the documents, someone approves, someone conceals, and many remain silent in the hope of eventually benefiting.

When communities celebrate wealth without asking where it came from, when families press relatives in office for favours beyond legitimate means, and when businesses treat bribery as an ordinary operating cost, we collectively create the rewards that make misconduct attractive. Change is possible. Singapore, through decades of sustained enforcement, now scores 84 and ranks third in the world, and closer to home Seychelles (68), Cape Verde (62), Botswana and Rwanda (58 each) show that African nations can rise well above the regional average. Africa need not copy any model mechanically, but the lesson is clear: consistent rules and credible consequences matter.

NyansaKasa(words of wisdom): “When society applauds unexplained wealth more loudly than honest achievement, it should not be surprised when integrity struggles to attract investors.”

Governance Begins At Home

We often speak of governance as though it starts in Parliament, the boardroom or the courts. Much of it starts at the family table. Children learn early whether promises are kept, whether rules apply equally and whether dishonesty is excused. A parent who condemns corruption on television but celebrates a favour secured through connections is teaching two lessons at once, and the child may remember the practical one more vividly.

Government carries heavy responsibilities that cannot be delegated, from competent leadership to security, justice and a productive economy. Citizens, equally, carry duties no government can perform on their behalf, from paying legitimate taxes and disposing of waste responsibly to rejecting bribery and demanding evidence. Blaming government for everything is as incomplete as blaming citizens for systemic failure.

NyansaKasa(words of wisdom): “Government may steer the national vehicle, but citizens who continuously remove its wheels should not complain that the journey is slow.”

We must also resist confusing activity with progress. A bridge that is 95 percent complete is of little comfort to the stranded traveller; development must be judged by outcomes, not announcements.

The Path To Recovery

Reversing the trend begins with honest diagnosis, separating symptoms from causes and resisting explanations chosen for political comfort. It requires enforcement that is consistent, lawful and fair, because laws applied selectively lose their moral force. It demands institutional continuity, so that useful policies survive changes of government, as South Korea demonstrates: around 1960 its income per person was broadly similar to Ghana’s, yet decades of patient institution building have since made it many times richer. It calls for incentives that protect whistleblowers and reward competence, and for boards that insist on effective audit and ethics oversight. And it needs schools, traditional authorities, faith communities and professional bodies that cultivate civic responsibility and own the change.

Above all, it requires each of us to stop treating personal responsibility as something meant mainly for other people. This is not an invitation to blame ourselves, but to examine ourselves, which is where lasting change begins.

The Unborn Child Will Inherit Our Choices

The consequences of what we tolerate rarely end with our generation. A polluted river does not run clean because the official who ignored it has retired.

Imagine an African child born 25 years from now who studies the records and discovers that we knew. Experts warned, committees investigated and governments promised, yet too many of us kept protecting the behaviours behind the problems. What would we tell that child? That the offenders belonged to our party? That everyone else was doing the same?

NyansaKasa(words of wisdom): “The unborn child cannot vote against today’s mistakes, yet tomorrow that child may spend a lifetime paying for decisions made before birth.”

A sick society can recover. But no doctor can permanently cure a patient determined to protect the disease. Perhaps, then, our national question should no longer be simply “What is wrong with our country?” but the more courageous one: “Which of the things we know are wrong do we continue to tolerate, excuse, celebrate or personally benefit from?” The honest answer may implicate institutions we belong to, parties we support, customs we inherited and, at times, the person in the mirror.

Africa’s future does not require a continent without problems. It requires a continent increasingly unwilling to defend their causes. Let us stop protecting the disease while praying for the cure, and stop confusing loyalty with complicity. The unborn African child will not inherit our intentions, only the consequences of our choices. The Africa we desire is in our own hands, and so too is the Africa we may one day regret leaving behind.

About the Author

Ing. Professor Douglas K. Boateng is a strategist in governance, industrialisation and supply chains, and serves as a professional chairperson, an international Chartered Director (UK) and a Chartered Engineer (UK). A Pan-Africanist and social entrepreneur at heart, he has spent his career working across public institutions, corporate boards and industrial policy, in Africa and beyond, guided by the conviction that strong institutions are built one honest decision at a time. His contributions to industry and academia have earned him more than six lifetime achievement awards. He is the founder of NyansaKasa (Words of Wisdom), a collection of daily aphorisms he has written and shared since late 2019, distilling decades of experience advising governments, boards, and enterprises on governance, accountability, and institutional resilience into words meant to challenge and endure. He convenes the Boardroom Governance Summit, Africa’s largest boardroom-focused summit, and writes a widely read weekly op-ed series titled “Inconvenient Truth” and “What Is Wrong With Us”, featured on some of the region’s leading digital media platforms. Professor Boateng can be reached via LinkedIn or at info@panavest.com.

Ghana News.title: MTN Ghana trains civil society organisations on artificial intelligence
Ghana News.content:
Telecom giant MTN Ghana has organised a one-day Artificial Intelligence (AI) workshop for Civil Society Organisations (CSOs) at its Head Office in Accra, as part of efforts to deepen understanding of AI and its impact on society.

The event was attended by over 100 participants is an annual programm introduced as part of the company’s commitment to develop human resources in Ghana.

Delivering the opening address, the Acting Senior Manager for Corporate Communications at MTN Ghana, Efua Falconer, said AI is transforming every aspect of life, and no stakeholder should be left behind. "AI, transformation. It is indeed transforming everything around us. And we cannot leave you behind," she said.

We've had these conversations in secondary schools, in the communities, in the markets, with our media, our regulators, across all the different stakeholders that we work with. And today is your turn," she added.

Ms Falconer said the workshop brought together seasoned AI professionals to build the capacity of participants through practical and interactive sessions. She urged participants to be attentive, engage fully, and follow the practical demonstrations on their laptops.

Our message here today is very simple. It's an interesting conversation. You will learn a lot if you are attentive. Please make sure you ask questions; there's a lot of practical work. Engage, take your laptop and just follow along," she said.

She explained that while government regulates and companies like MTN build the infrastructure powering the AI journey, civil society plays a critical role as the voice of the vulnerable.

You are the mouthpiece of the vulnerable, the youth, the market woman who doesn't know a lot about data, the school children who are using data. You are the people who speak for the vulnerable in society. So we cannot leave you out of this conversation," she stressed.

Ms Falconer said MTN was confident participants would take the knowledge acquired beyond the walls of the training room and apply it in their various spheres of influence.

"If we don't, we are going to be left behind. You give the kids today a mobile phone, and the kind of things they are able to do within a short period; you at 40, 50, you can't do it. So please, they are leaving us behind. So we have to catch up.

And the youth, this is your time," she told participants.

Speaking on behalf of the Chief Corporate Services and Sustainability Officer, Madam Adwoa Afriyie Wiafe, the Senior Manager for Regulatory and Government Affairs at MTN Ghana, Samuel Bartels, challenged CSOs to make their knowledge visible online.

He said CSOs do advocacy, interventions, and community work and know communities better than anyone, yet their rich knowledge is missing from the digital space that powers AI.

Do you know that a lot of the things that concern Africans are not online? If you call an AI tool for some information, it may not give you that perspective, because some of the things are still hiding in the Balme Library, and AI doesn't travel to the Balme Library at the University of Ghana," he said. According to him, AI can only work with what has been codified and put online, and currently only about 2% of the data used to train Large Language Models (LLMs) is from Africa.

Quoting a book titled Best Story Wins, Mr Bartels said only those who tell their story win.

He warned that if CSO research and project reports remain as hardbound documents locked in cupboards at their secretariats, AI systems will never learn from them. "So, in terms of storytelling, we are falling behind in this AI revolution because our information is just not available to train an AI model. So, the AI model will still tell stories that paint poverty, conflict and disease about us, because they don't have the alternative story," he said. He lamented that much of the content Africans now produce online is for entertainment rather than for reflection and knowledge sharing.

Unfortunately, a lot of the content we develop now is just for people to laugh, and not necessarily for people to think or reflect.

So, in the storytelling game, Ghana and Africa will lose out because our stories are not out there," he noted.

Mr Bartels said as technology emerges, two questions arise: what can the technology do, and what should we do with the technology? He said while the workshop would address what AI can do, CSOs must help answer what should be done with it, given their closeness to communities.

This is why it was important to have this conversation with you. It's important that we also listen to your perspective. What you hear in the communities, we at MTN may never hear.

What we may miss, you see," he said. Facilitating the first technical session, Data Scientist at MTN Ghana, Elie Tetteh Wayoe, said AI has become an opportunity for everyone and must be leveraged responsibly to serve society. "There is a new area that is coming.

It's making life easier. But for it to have impact, it must be used in the right way," he said. Mr Wayoe said MTN's vision is to ensure AI is made accessible and scalable for everyone, not just as a business tool, but as a force for good that is deployed responsibly.

Presenting on the topic "MTN and AI, focusing on responsible innovation for social and systemic impact," he said AI is not here to take people's jobs, but to augment human efforts. "If you don't make use of it, then you are the one who is behind. We don't expect AI to take everyone's place; it helps augment us to become better," he said.

He outlined MTN's AI strategy, which focuses on value creation and building a foundation for practical use cases, with emphasis on responsible adoption. According to him, for AI to be adopted responsibly, there must be guardrails, governance, trust principles, and human accountability. "You have to be accountable for what you do, for ensuring things will be done in the right manner. There has to be trust.

Without governance, responsible adoption is impossible," he said.

He added that the training would also explore practical examples of how AI can be applied in the daily activities and advocacy work of CSOs to enhance efficiency and deepen their social impact.

Ghana News.title: GoldBod FX framework aims to make dollar supply predictable – Acheampong
Ghana News.content:
Economist and political risk specialist Dr Theo Acheampong says GoldBod’s foreign exchange framework aims to make dollar supply more predictable, while the Bank of Ghana retains its role in tackling excessive exchange rate volatility.

The Finance Ministry’s Technical Advisor said transparency and advance planning were central to the arrangement.

Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express Business Edition on Thursday, he explained that the framework should help the market anticipate foreign exchange needs and plan supply.

“What you want is a clear and transparent process that you know in advance how much, let's say, FX you need next week, next month, and then you can predict and provide that FX which is available.”

His comments followed a question from host George Wiafe about whether GoldBod’s involvement had the Finance Minister’s backing. The host also raised concerns about a possible overlap with the central bank’s responsibilities.

Dr Acheampong said the framework was already being implemented and that GoldBod had made its details public.

“GoldBod has communicated this very clearly to the market. The information is out there on their website.”

GoldBod announced its new Spot FX Sales and Intermediation Framework on October 5. It provides for dollar sales to authorised commercial banks, ordinarily on Tuesdays and Thursdays, through the GoFX platform.

Where demand exceeds available dollars, banks receive proportional allocations. The programme operates under the Bank of Ghana's regulatory oversight, with the central bank granted real-time access to the platform and to transaction reports after each sale.

GoldBod subsequently reported a maiden sale of approximately $125 million to commercial banks. The sale took place on October 6 under the new arrangement.

Dr Acheampong stressed that the central bank remained responsible for responding to sharp movements in the exchange rate.

“Remember that as part of the FX framework, the central bank would step in if they see excessive volatility within the exchange rate. That is the function of a central bank.”

He said instability in the cedi would require the Bank of Ghana to act.

“So if you see the cedi being wobbly and being all over the place, what is a central bank to do? It's meant to do its job.”
