World.content:
Farage proposes offering Trump Diego Garcia in exchange for his silence on the Falklands

14th Wednesday, October 2026 - 21:53 UTC Full article

“I’d have gone in and said, ‘Right, you know what mate? Chagos, it’s yours. Diego Garcia, in perpetuity, the most strategic American military base in the world’,” Farage said

Reform UK leader c has said that, if he were prime minister, he would offer US President Donald Trump the use in perpetuity of the Diego Garcia military base, in the Chagos archipelago, in exchange for him to stop talking about the Falklands. The proposal sparked a clash with Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch, who called it “humiliating”, and prompted the White House to come to Farage’s defence.

“I’d have gone in and said, ‘Right, you know what mate? Chagos, it’s yours. Diego Garcia, in perpetuity, the most strategic American military base in the world’,” Farage told the US podcast The Benny Show. “In return, just please stop talking about the Falkland Islands. I know you like Milei, but this really matters to us. And there’s a trade, you see.”

Badenoch responded in The Telegraph: “Giving away British territory in return for someone keeping quiet is not a deal. It is humiliating.” She added that “the Chagos Islands are British, and the Falklands are British and will remain British, regardless of what the American president says”, calling Farage’s remarks “careless, loose talk from a man who wants to be responsible for Britain’s national security”.

Farage didn't say that Trump/USA could use the Chagos Islands in perpetuity. In his interview he literally said he would trade the Chagos Islands for the Falklands. Reform officials and Farage can deny it all they like, but the evidence is right there and cannot be altered. https://t.co/84HYJw12sf — Thomas Evans @Renewal2030 (@ThomasEvansAdur) October 14, 2026

Farage replied on X that Badenoch “is lying again” and said he would offer the United States the use of Diego Garcia, not sovereignty over the archipelago, in return for America going “quiet on the Falklands”. A White House official quoted by The Times agreed: “He was obviously referring to the use of the Diego Garcia military base, which is critical to countering threats from China and Iran,” and accused Badenoch of peddling fake news and undermining the Anglo-American relationship.

The agreement signed by the British government in 2025 to transfer sovereignty over Chagos to Mauritius, with a 99-year lease for the base, is on hold following Trump’s opposition. The row comes amid an escalating dispute over the Sea Lion oil project: on Tuesday, Overseas Territories Minister Uma Kumaran told the House of Commons that Prime Minister Andy Burnham had raised with Trump the islanders’ wish to remain British.

World.title: What are the red notices Argentina has sought from Interpol over Sea Lion
World.content:
What are the red notices Argentina has sought from Interpol over Sea Lion

14th Wednesday, October 2026 - 21:45 UTC Full article

The chief executive of the islands’ government, Andrea Clausen, acknowledged that the use of Interpol poses a threat

Argentina has requested Interpol red notices against individuals linked to the Sea Lion oil project north of the Falklands, and the United Kingdom has asked the organisation to reject them as “politically motivated”, according to the British newspaper The Guardian. Interpol responded by reaffirming Article 3 of its constitution, which prohibits any intervention or activity of a political character.

A red notice is a request to police worldwide to locate and provisionally arrest a person pending extradition. It is not an international arrest warrant: Interpol reviews each request before circulating it, but each state decides whether to act. According to the newspaper, British officials are concerned that Argentina could persuade other countries that its requests are based on domestic law rather than political motives. It has not emerged how many people are affected or whether any notice has been issued.

The chief executive of the islands’ government, Andrea Clausen, acknowledged that the use of Interpol poses a threat. “One would hope that Interpol wouldn’t necessarily take action,” she said. “Certainly those of us who have an interest have had a look at certain sections of Interpol’s constitution to see what we think it could mean.” Workers in the oil and fishing sectors fear being detained if they travel, particularly to South America.

Argentina has launched criminal proceedings against Navitas Petroleum and Rockhopper Exploration, the project’s partners. British officials quoted by The Guardian describe Argentina’s campaign as the most serious since the 1982 war. On Tuesday, London announced measures to shield its companies from Argentine sanctions, and Argentina asked the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea to order a halt to Sea Lion.

World.title: HMS Protector breaks down and leaves UK without an Ice Patrol
World.content:
HMS Protector breaks down and leaves UK without an Ice Patrol

14th Wednesday, October 2026 - 21:10 UTC Full article

HMS Protector at Devonport Dockyard, Plymouth

Britain has been left without its Ice Patrol after HMS Protector on Tuesday suffered engine problems and had to be towed back to Plymouth, according to reports in the media. This could speed the Royal Navy’s assessment as to whether the vessel originally built in Norway and now with 25 years of rough seas in both poles has to be replaced.

The breakdown comes at a critical moment, when world powers are rushing to take advantage of navigation opportunities in the Arctic, particularly Russia, and in the southern seas, with as ever aggressive Argentina threatening the Falkland Islands development of its resources.

The Telegraph reports that Royal Navy sources admitted the situation as a “catastrophic failure”. And Commander Tom Sharpe, who commanded HMS Endurance, Protector’s predecessor, said it would be “poor timing” to remove the ship from service.

In March, Gen Sir Gwyn Jenkins, the First Sea Lord, admitted that the Navy was not ready for war. It has five active frigates, six destroyers and two aircraft carriers, alongside a submarine fleet of six Astute-class attack boats and four Vanguard-class subs, which carry the UK’s nuclear weapons.

Both carriers, HMS Prince of Wales and HMS Queen Elizabeth, have reported mechanical problems since their maiden voyages.

Military chiefs are waiting for the spending review for details about how the Government will meet a long-term Nato pledge of increasing the core defense budget to 3.5 per cent of GDP by 2035.

HMS Protector underpins the UK’s presence in the British Antarctic Territory, South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands.

In 2008, HMS Endurance, the Navy’s previous icebreaker, suffered a flood caused by “poor engineering standards”. At the time, the Navy insisted that she would be repaired and returned to sea. However, she was not and was eventually replaced by HMS Protector after around three years.

HMS Protector was originally named MV Polarbjørn, meaning Polar bear in Norwegian, before being leased in 2011 by the Navy for £8.7m a year. The UK government paid £51m to own the ship outright in 2013. Later refurbished, HMS Protector should expect to have another decade of use before being withdrawn from service.

With a crew of 88, she is typically lightly armed carrying machine guns, but often carries a detachment of Royal Marines. Although classed as a Royal Navy warship, the vessel has retained her original red and white paint scheme. The Royal Navy website says she is affectionately referred to as the “Swiss army knife – red, versatile, and always there when you need her!”

Last month, Defense Secretary Wes Streeting, described HMS Protector as an “essential presence” and confirmed she would be replaced at the end of her service life. He said the Ministry of Defense would replace HMS Protector with “a more modern variant” to ensure support for government activities in the Arctic and around the British Antarctic Territory would continue.

A Royal Navy spokesman said: “HMS Protector has returned to her home port of Devonport while investigations into a defect take place. As part of the defense investment plan, HMS Protector will be replaced with a more modern variant to maintain the ice patrol capability.

World.title: A tornado and an unusual spring hailstorm overwhelm Santiago, Chile
World.content:
A tornado and an unusual spring hailstorm overwhelm Santiago, Chile

14th Wednesday, October 2026 - 07:01 UTC Full article

An electrical storm with hail, unusual in the middle of spring, flooded streets, homes and businesses in Santiago, Chile, on Tuesday and produced a tornado that the Chilean Meteorological Directorate preliminarily classified as EF0, the lowest intensity category. The national disaster prevention and response service declared a red alert in the Metropolitan Region, five days after the mudslide that hit the Las Condes district.

The tornado struck a bus terminal in Estación Central, in the west of the capital, where the gust lifted dozens of zinc sheets into the air. The storm began around 3:30pm, as students and workers were leaving schools and offices, and within minutes flooded avenues, underground car parks and buildings, in some cases with water coming through the roofs. According to regional governor Claudio Orrego, around 20 millimetres fell in about two and a half hours, and districts such as Independencia and Providencia recorded some 18 millimetres in one hour.

Some 22,000 homes were left without electricity, according to the Superintendency of Electricity and Fuels. Classes were suspended at municipal schools in Santiago, Providencia and Ñuñoa, and Las Condes extended its restricted-movement perimeter because of the risk of further landslides. Interior Minister Claudio Alvarado said “all emergency institutions” had been activated and that the rain was expected to ease overnight.

“Because of global warming, weather processes are intensifying. And we have just had an electrical storm like none ever seen in Santiago,” climatologist Alejandro Vial told the newspaper El País, linking the episode to El Niño.

Last week, an atmospheric river intensified by El Niño made this the wettest October on record in the Chilean capital and caused the October 8 mudslide in San Carlos de Apoquindo, which left six people injured and around 2,000 homes damaged.

World.title: US sanctions horse racing network tied to the Northeast Cartel
World.content:
In a new round of sanctions, the U.S. Department of the Treasury has targeted a horse racing enterprise allegedly run by the Cartel del Noreste (Northeast Cartel) as well as the group’s broader criminal network.

Treasury announced on Tuesday that its Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) had sanctioned four individuals and eleven entities connected to the Cartel del Noreste (CDN), a Nuevo Laredo, Tamaulipas-based criminal group that was designated as a foreign terrorist organization by the U.S. government in February 2025.

“Those designated include individuals and businesses involved in quarter horse racing, construction, trucking, and the oil and gas sector, highlighting the cartel’s diverse commercial footprint,” Treasury said in a statement.

“… CDN has a long history of money laundering through the American Quarter Horse racing industry,” the department said.

“Between 2008 and 2012, Z-40 and Z-42 bought and sold racehorses with drug money and trained and raced them in the United States,” Treasury said, referring to Miguel Angel “Z-40” Treviño Morales and Óscar Omar “Z-42” Treviño Morales, brothers and founders of the CDN, which grew out of the notorious Los Zetas crime group.

“Over a 30-month period, Zetas-affiliated front persons and shell companies spent $16 million in New Mexico, Oklahoma, California, and Texas to support the operation and laundered upwards of $22 million for the cartel,” Treasury said.

“In June 2012, the U.S. Government seized 455 horses at an Oklahoma horse farm, racing venues, and training farms. CDN’s involvement in horse racing continues to this day.”

One of the 11 sanctioned entities is Club La Molienda, described by Treasury as “a horse racetrack, restaurant, and bar located on the outskirts of Nuevo Laredo that is controlled by CDN.”

“As the most prominent racetrack in Nuevo Laredo, La Molienda generates revenue for CDN, charging entrance fees for those racing their horses at the track as well as for spectators,” the department said.

“CDN leaders and members purchase horses, including many from the United States, to race at La Molienda. La Molienda is controlled by Z-40 but is ultimately overseen by various CDN leaders and associates while Z-40 is incarcerated in the United States.”

View this post on Instagram A post shared by LA Molienda Race Track (@clublamolienda)

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that the sanctioning of individuals and entities connected to the CDN “exposes Cartel del Noreste’s exploitation of the horse racing sector to launder illicit proceeds and finance cartel operations.” “This action marks Treasury’s most significant effort to date to disrupt Cartel del Noreste’s financial infrastructure,” he said. Treasury said on Tuesday that “as a result of today’s action, all property and interests in property of the designated or blocked persons described above that are in the United States or in the possession or control of U.S. persons are blocked and must be reported to OFAC.” It noted that “OFAC coordinated on this action and previous actions against CDN with the Government of Mexico’s Financial Intelligence Unit [UIF].” OFAC has previously sanctioned individuals and entities linked to various Mexican criminal groups, including the CDN, the Jalisco New Generation Cartel and the Sinaloa Cartel.

A ‘horse racing enthusiast’ and ‘a current CDN plaza boss’ among the 4 sanctioned individuals

The four individuals sanctioned by OFAC on Tuesday are:

Gamaliel Garza García , described by Treasury as “a Mexico-based businessman, horse racing enthusiast, and an associate of CDN.” Treasury said that Garza García is involved in horse racing in both Mexico and the United States, noting that his horses race at “some of the most prestigious tracks in California and New Mexico,” and at Club La Molienda.

Gamaliel Garza Elias , Garza Garcia’s son. Treasury said he was being designated for his involvement in CEGESA, a construction company owned by Garza García that has allegedly “been utilized by CDN to funnel money to election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates.” Treasury said that Garza Elias has “delivered cash to fund election campaigns for CDN’s preferred political candidates in Mexico.”

Treasury said he was being designated for his involvement in CEGESA, a construction company owned by Garza García that has allegedly “been utilized by CDN to funnel money to election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates.” Treasury said that Garza Elias has “delivered cash to fund election campaigns for CDN’s preferred political candidates in Mexico.” Pablo César Guajardo Álvarez , identified by Treasury as “a current CDN plaza boss of Nuevo Laredo and former leader of CDN’s sicarios.” Treasury said that Guajardo was arrested in 2020 for his connection to the January 4, 2017, assassination of Ricardo Martínez Chávez, a high-ranking law enforcement official in Tamaulipas, and four other public servants, “but has since been released.” It also said he has “been involved in arms trafficking on behalf of CDN.”

Like Club La Molienda, Tamex is one of the 11 entities sanctioned by OFAC, most of which are located in Tamaulipas.

The other nine are all owned, controlled or otherwise linked to Garza García. They include various construction and fuel and gas companies as well as a concrete company and a “Quarter Horse racing barn” in Nuevo León.

In addition to allegedly funneling money to “election campaigns of CDN’s preferred political candidates,” CEGESA has “corruptly obtained government contracts and then sub-contracted that work to CDN-affiliated individuals,” according to Treasury.

“CEGESA is a major recipient of government contracts in the north of the country, including from the governments of the municipality of Nuevo Laredo and the state of Tamaulipas,” the department said.

Treasury said that Garza Garcia also controls Cuadra San Dibanh, “an Anahuac, Nuevo León-based Quarter Horse racing barn.”

“Cuadra San Dibanh frequently races at La Molienda and other major racetracks throughout Mexico,” the department said.

With regard to Tamex, Treasury said that the company’s truck yard in Nuevo Laredo “has been the originator of at least two cocaine shipments bound for the United States.”

In its statement, Treasury also said that “CDN’s stronghold sits directly across the border from Laredo, Texas, the busiest port of entry (POE) on the southern border, where nearly 40 percent of all commercial traffic between the United States and Mexico crosses.”

The U.S. department said that the cartel’s “deep entrenchment in cross-border industries, combined with CDN’s ability to infiltrate local governments, steer public contracts, and manipulate regional elections, undermines legitimate authority and destabilizes communities on both sides of the border.”

World.title: A Tamaulipas teen built a fire extinguisher that puts out flames using sound
World.content:
A 17-year-old from the northeastern state of Tamaulipas is competing at an international science fair in Indonesia this week with a device she spent a year developing — a fire extinguisher that snuffs out small flames with sound instead of water or chemicals.

Ángela Karime Venegas Hernández is representing Mexico at the International Science and Invention Fair with Vortex Tech, a prototype developed with the help of her uncle, José Arturo Hernández Muñoz.

Her school, CETis 78 in Altamira, Tamaulipas, announced her participation in the fair being held this week at the University of Indonesia in Depok, near Jakarta.

Photographs shared by Mexico’s federal technical education agency showed Venegas wearing traditional Mexican clothing at the fair.

Venegas told the newspaper El País that a video of a large, roughly 4-meter (13-foot) sonic cannon extinguishing a flame — with air movement, not water or chemicals — inspired her to investigate whether she could build a smaller device.

She and her uncle, who holds a master’s degree in science, according to the Tamaulipas Education Ministry, spent about a year developing five prototypes, building on earlier experiments by others.

Just to create the first prototype — one that could extinguish a candle — took two months, not including preliminary research, she told the newspaper.

Vortex Tech uses a 12-volt battery, a frequency generator set to 30 hertz, an amplifier and a speaker. A modified bucket channels the output toward a flame.

According to Venegas’ explanation, the sound generates swirling rings of air that disrupt the oxygen supply sustaining combustion, extinguishing small flames within seconds.

The technology remains experimental. The newspaper El Universal reported that it works on small, nearby flames and does not replace conventional extinguishers for large fires.

Tamaulipas education officials said the project also includes thermal sensors designed to detect a developing fire and automatically activate the sound-based extinguishing system.

The state Education Ministry said Venegas advanced through regional, state and national competitions before qualifying for Indonesia. It also pledged support for her and her uncle/adviser’s participation.

With reports from El País, El Heraldo de México and El Universal

World.title: 2,500-year-old astronomical observatory in Puebla confirmed to be the oldest in Mexico
World.content:
A pre-Hispanic solar observatory in the municipality of Teteles de Ávila Castillo in the Sierra Norte region of Puebla has been confirmed to be the oldest in Mexico, dating back more than 2,500 years.

According to research carried out by the National Institute of Anthropology and History (INAH), a monumental architectural complex named “Grupo E” functioned as a solar astronomical observatory and is the oldest of its kind in Mexico.

Researchers believe the settlement’s inhabitants incorporated astronomical observations into the planning of their ceremonial buildings more than two millennia ago.

Heritage Daily —a digital publication specializing in archaeology, anthropology and palaeontology — says the discovery “provides remarkable evidence of sophisticated astronomical knowledge among ancient Mesoamerican civilizations.”

INAH says it is the first discovery of its kind outside the Maya region and is comparable to the observatory at the archaeological site of Uaxactún in Petén, Guatemala, which has been identified as the first and defining archetype for ancient Maya astronomical observation complexes.

While both the Uaxactún and Teteles complexes are believed to date to the Middle Preclassic (from 1200 to 400 BCE.), the Uaxactún structure is approximately twice the size of the one in Puebla.

Researchers have confirmed that the original layout of the “Group E” settlement (also known as Tetelihtic) and the orientation of its pyramidal structures are based on an understanding of celestial bodies.

Archaeologist Alberto Diez Barroso said the ancient settlement is an outstanding example of pre-Hispanic urban planning — shaped by the observation of the surrounding landscape, such as the nearby mountain peaks, as well as the astronomical horizon — making it “a significant point of reference for Mesoamerican studies in this field.”

Tetelihtic consists of a quadrangular courtyard flanked by two platforms at its eastern and western ends. The eastern platform is elongated (90 m from south to north by 40 m from east to west), while the western structure is smaller (46 m from north to south by 27 m from east to west) and served as an observation point.

The elongated platform does not mark the equinoxes at its center, however.

“It apparently served to establish the beginning of the pre-Hispanic Mesoamerican calendar in February and the harvest period in October, making it a complex and unique feature,” Diez said.

However, the eastern platform did function as a solar calendar; observations have confirmed that, from its front, one can track the sun’s path at dawn during the equinoxes and solstices.

Archaeologists believe the finding could provide insights into the cultural relationship between the Huastec and Maya groups during the early stages of human settlement in the Sierra Norte as it serves to confirm the Maya ethnolinguistic roots of the Huastec groups.

A Maya presence at Teteles may date back as far as 3,000 years — a possibility suggested by the Puebla observatory.

With reports from INAH, Heritage Daily and Ambas Manos

World.title: Mexico targets cheap Chinese bicycles with six-month anti-dumping duty
World.content:
Mexico has imposed a provisional anti-dumping duty of US $68.60 per unit on adult bicycles originating from China, after the Economy Ministry preliminarily determined that Chinese bicycles were being sold below fair market value, harming domestic manufacturers.

The measure, which took effect on Oct. 13, will remain in place for six months and will apply to adult bicycles with a wheel size larger than 20 inches, including urban and mountain models, with or without gears, as well as unassembled units. Electric bicycles and racing or road bikes are excluded from the measure.

The decision traced back to an anti-dumping investigation requested in April 2025 by the National Association of Bicycle Manufacturers and the companies Mercurio, Veloci, Benotto and Línea Siete. The investigation formally began in August of that year.

According to preliminary results, Chinese bicycles accounted for 95% of Mexico’s imports of adult bicycles in 2024. Apparent national consumption of Chinese bicycles rose from 53% in 2022 to 61% in 2024, while the average price of imports fell 35% during that period.

In 2024, Chinese bicycles cost 27% less than their domestic counterparts. According to the Economy Ministry, this difference pressured the Mexican industry to reduce prices by 4% to stay competitive.

As more low-cost Chinese bicycles entered the country, Mexican manufacturers saw a significant drop in business. The Economy Ministry found that between 2022 and 2024, adult bicycle production fell by 34% and domestic sales declined by 32%. Meanwhile, employment dropped by 29%.

Sales revenue in the domestic market fell by 36% in the same period, while the industry’s operating profits swung into the red, a 111% drop. These figures led investigators to conclude that low-priced Chinese imports caused material harm to Mexican manufacturers.

During the six months that the preliminary duty will remain in effect, interested parties may submit evidence for or against the measures, while the investigation continues to determine whether to establish more permanent duties.

The provisional anti-dumping duty is part of a broader trend toward increased trade protection in Mexico. According to data from the Economy Ministry, imports falling under the 1,463 tariff classifications subject to new levies — approved in December 2025 — declined by 23% between January and May 2026, compared to the same period the previous year.

China, the primary supplier of the goods subject to duties, was the hardest hit, as its tariffed goods fell by 28% — from $10.1 billion to $7.2 billion.

With reports from Milenio and Diario de Tabasco

World.title: American Airlines is the latest carrier to drop service to Tulum
World.content:
American Airlines is dropping flights from Miami to the Yucatán Peninsula destination of Tulum as part of its cutback of several international routes, including its Charlotte-Los Cabos service.

American (AA) — the largest U.S. airline by passenger numbers — joins other major carriers, including Aeroméxico and Volaris, in dropping or pausing routes to the resort town on the state of Quintana Roo’s Caribbean coast.

AA had already announced that its Miami-Tulum route would be on seasonal pause through Nov. 19, after which it would continue again until Dec. 1. The current plan is to then resume service one last time from Dec. 17 to January 5, 2027, before stopping it completely.

Los Cabos is also slated for service cuts

AA ended its service to Tulum from Charlotte, North Carolina, in February, 2025, less than a year after its launch. Next year, the only AA route from the U.S. to Tulum will be from or through the Dallas/Fort Worth hub.

American has also announced plans to remove its Charlotte-San José del Cabo route from its future schedule, after its current seasonal pause. The route was originally planned to return to normal operations in November, but the schedule now reportedly shows only sporadic operations.

That limited service will end in August of 2027. A possible motive for the discontinuation is that the route’s flights on average were just 73.69% full between June 2025 and June 2026.

With reports from Simple Flying

World.title: Rachel death toll rises to 8 in Baja California as newly formed Hurricane Trudy heads for Jalisco coast
World.content:
While Pacific Coast residents are still reeling from the passage of Polo, Rachel and Simon, the newly formed Hurricane Trudy threatens to bring more chaos and disruption to the region.

Eight deaths have been attributed to Hurricane Rachel, while at least four people remain missing and the military has been actively carrying out search and rescue operations. And Simon, lurking near the Jalisco coast south of the tip of the Baja California Peninsula, is expected to remain a Category 1 hurricane through Friday.

In light of the devastation, President Claudia Sheinbaum on Thursday activated the Defense Ministry’s DN-III emergency protection plan and the Navy’s “Plan Marina.”

Sheinbaum also ordered the Interior Ministry to stay in close contact with the Baja California governor in order to provide any support that may be needed, especially as Simon is expected to move toward the peninsula on Saturday.

Last month, Polo — the second most-intense Pacific hurricane on record — made consecutive landfalls on the peninsula and then mainland Mexico on Sept. 29.

Now comes Trudy, which became a hurricane before dawn Thursday.

The storm system was located about 300 miles (480 kilometers) southwest of Acapulco and 445 miles (720 km) south-southeast of Manzanillo, Colima, while registering maximum sustained winds of 75 mph (120 km/h), with gusts of 93 mph (150 km/h).

According to the U.S. National Hurricane Center (NHC), Trudy is undergoing a period of rapid intensification as it moves northwest at 9 mph (15 km/h) and is expected to bring heavy rains to Oaxaca and Guerrero today (Thursday).

Forecast models project it will become a major hurricane as it approaches the coast of southwestern and west-central Mexico this weekend, bringing rainfall of 4 to 8 inches (101 to 203 millimeters) through the weekend across Colima and Jalisco states.

Meanwhile, Simon remains virtually “frozen” a few hundred kilometers west-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Jalisco, and is expected to continue orbiting in place with sustained winds of 75 mph (120 km/h) and gusts of 95 mph (150 km/h).

Sustained winds were about 130 miles (210 kilometers) per hour as the week began, and the storm’s inner core was brushing up against the Jalisco coast.

The topography of the Sierra Madre mountains appeared to temper Simon’s intensity and shrink the size of its wind field, the NHC said. Still, as the storm system weakened from a Category 4 to Category 1 it delivered heavy rain and flooding to coastal areas, including the port city of Manzanillo, Colima.

With reports from La Jornada, The Associated Press, El Economista, Meteored and CNN en Español

World.title: International tourist spending grows 8% in August despite a dip in arrivals
World.content:
International tourist arrivals in Mexico declined year over year in August for the first time in almost a year, according to official data, even as total expenditure by international tourists increased by over 8%.

The national statistics agency INEGI reported Wednesday that 3.76 million international tourists came to Mexico in August, a decline of 0.5% compared to the same month of 2025.

International tourists are classified as foreign residents who spend at least one night in Mexico during their visit to the country.

In August, 1.39 million of the 3.76 million international tourists flew into the country, a decline of 6.5% compared to a year earlier. International tourist arrivals by air declined during every month between February and August.

The remainder of the international tourists in August entered Mexico by land, with most of that cohort staying within the northern or southern border region. INEGI’s data shows that two-thirds (67.1%) of the tourists who came to Mexico in August and traveled beyond the border regions are residents of the United States.

The year-over-year decline in international tourist arrivals in August was the first annual decrease since September 2025.

Humberto Molina, an expert in tourism economics at the consultancy firm Grupo Empresarial Estrategia, attributed the decline to a range of factors, including the presence of sargassum on Mexican beaches, insecurity and a lack of tourism promotion.

International tourist expenditure increased 8.1% in August

While in Mexico in August, international tourists collectively spent US $2.16 billion, an increase of 8.1% compared to the same month of 2025.

Each international tourist spent $573.30 on average, up 8.6% from August 2025.

Individual expenditure by international tourists who flew into Mexico was more than double that amount at $1,269.60, an increase of 15.2% compared to August 2025.

International tourists who flew into Mexico collectively spent $1.77 billion while in the country, a figure that accounts for 82% of total international tourism expenditure.

Despite decline in international tourists, international traveler numbers reached a record high in August

While international tourist numbers declined 0.5% year over year in August, international traveler numbers increased 1.3% to reach 7.98 million, the highest figure on record for the month of August.

INEGI’s international travelers category includes international tourists and international day-trippers (excursionistas internacionales). The latter enter Mexico by land or sea but don’t stay the night. International day-trippers include cruise ship passengers and people who spend a few hours in Mexico after entering the country via border crossings with the United States, Guatemala and Belize.

Just over 4.2 million international day-trippers came to Mexico in August, an increase of 3% compared to the same month of last year. Around 81% of the international day trippers (3.43 million) entered Mexico by land, while 785,558 came into the country by sea. Sea arrivals increased by 12.3% compared to August 2025, while land arrivals rose 1.1%.

Total spending by international travelers in Mexico in August was $2.4 billion, a 7% increase compared to a year earlier. International tourists spent 90% of that amount, while international day-trippers contributed the other 10%.

While expenditure rose in dollar terms, it declined 5.51% annually in real peso terms, according to Banco Base analysts, who took inflation and the USD:MXN exchange rate into account. The USD:MXN exchange rate was 17 at the end of August compared to 18.66 a year earlier.

More than 32 million international tourists came to Mexico between January and August

INEGI data shows that 32.68 million international tourists came to Mexico in the first eight months of 2026, a year-over-year increase of 3.9%.

International traveler numbers rose 6.3% annually in the same period to reach 67.69 million.

In a statement, Tourism Minister Josefina Rodríguez said that data from the first eight months of the year indicates that “Mexico could end 2026 with a record in international tourist arrivals.”

“Mexico is in vogue and we’re continuing to work so that more people visit us, get to know our cultural and natural wealth and contribute to the well-being of communities,” she said.

Total expenditure by international travelers in Mexico was $24.15 billion between January and August, an increase of 0.9% compared to the same period of last year.

Mexico is one of the world’s 10 most visited countries, ranking sixth or seventh in recent years. One of the goals of the federal government’s Plan Mexico economic initiative is to make Mexico one of the world’s top five tourism destinations by 2030.

With reports from El Economista, La Jornada and Reporte Indigo

World.title: MND Local CDMX: Brugada’s big plans, a sinking city and methane mitigation
World.content:
In this week’s MND Local for CDMX, Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada touted her administration’s accomplishments and outlined future priorities during her second annual “state of the city” address. Meanwhile, new research highlights the capital’s ongoing sinking problem, and officials are pursuing efforts to reduce the city’s methane emissions.

Let’s get into it.

Mayor Brugada delivers 2nd ‘state of the city’ address

Earlier this month, Mexico City Mayor Clara Brugada delivered a “state of the city” address, touting her administration’s accomplishments across various sectors, including social services, security, infrastructure and healthcare. It was Brugada’s second such address since she assumed office on Oct. 7, 2024.

The theme of Brugada’s speech was “utopias,” which she said are the cornerstone of her administration’s policies.

“We want to build the city of Utopias, the city where all possible utopias fit: the utopia of well-being, democracy, social justice, fraternity and freedom,” Brugada, who belongs to the ruling Morena Party, said.

She touched on several future priorities and projects the administration intends to carry out, including criminal justice reform that centers on reintegration, establishing three new public universities outside Mexico City’s core, and constructing five new high schools that serve the city’s Indigenous population.

Utopian visions

Meanwhile, she touted myriad accomplishments over the past two years, such as a 48 billion peso (US $2.6 billion) investment in the city’s metro system, resulting in 100 kilometers of electric bus routes. She also pointed to 1 million square meters of public space that have been reclaimed, 600 new public women’s spaces, a 1 billion peso (US $54 million) investment in agriculture, and an 85% increase in social programs, which now cover 2.6 million people across the capital, among other things.

“Let’s continue building all possible utopias,” Brugada said during her address, per La Gazzetta DF. “Let’s strive for more, for much more. With the memory of those who fought before and the hope of those who will come after. This is our city, this is our time, this is our history, and we are writing it together.”

While Brugada’s approval rating currently stands at 60%, according to the most recent polling from El Financiero, her tenure has not been without controversy.

During her speech, Brugada touted a significant reduction in crime over the past two years, including a 24% dip in “high-impact crimes” and four consecutive months with homicides at historic lows. However, her administration’s failure to hold anyone accountable for the assassinations of two of her deputies in 2025 continues to dog her legacy.

Mexico City is sinking … still

A new study published Oct. 12 in “Nature Cities” suggests that areas of Mexico City are sinking as much as 8.5 inches per year, while the citywide average sits somewhere around 0.3 inches per year.

The study, led by Shengli Tao and Xie Hu of Beijing’s Peking University, used high-resolution satellite data collected over nine years, from 2014 to 2023. Of the 465 cities across 107 countries that were surveyed, Mexico City recorded the fastest localized sinking.

The 8.5-inch figure hovers around a similar analysis published in May, which found that Mexico City is sinking by nearly 10 inches (about 25 centimeters) a year and has sunk by nearly 40 feet over the past century.

That study relied on NASA satellite data from NISAR, a joint U.S.-India satellite project. NISAR uses advanced radar imaging — effectively a microscope in space — to measure changes in Earth’s land, ice, sea level rise and groundwater.

It’s a different approach from Tao and Hu’s team, which used satellite interferometric synthetic aperture radar, which basically functions like a ruler that measures ground movement over time.

Mexico City details methane mitigation efforts

Meanwhile, Mexico City is attempting to tackle a significant driver of global warming — methane emissions.

Earlier this month, the city hosted Mexico Climate Week, which included a session dubbed “Accelerating Methane Action in Mexico City.” The event brought together domestic and international stakeholders representing government, academia, civil society and the private sector.

According to Ricardo Cepeda of the U.S.-based nonprofit C40 Cities, methane mitigation efforts are one of the best, most demonstrable ways to slow climate change in the near future.

“The objective is not to create more strategies, plans or projects,” Cepeda said. “The objective is to reduce methane emissions.”

Despite Cepeda warning governments off endless strategy meetings, Maritza Florez, who works with Mexico City’s Environment Ministry, did just that, detailing the capital’s methane mitigation strategy. It includes preventing food waste, expanding composting infrastructure and developing four additional treatment facilities for organic waste.

While much of the infrastructural onus lies with city leaders, residents are encouraged to develop composting and food waste prevention initiatives in their own communities.

“Methane mitigation is the brake for climate change,” said Mexico City Environment Ministry Secretary Julia Álvarez Icaza, adding that better waste management and separation systems are key to controlling the capital’s methane emissions.

“When waste is not mixed, it can be valued and utilized. When it is mixed, it becomes garbage,” Icaza said.

Drew Pittock serves as Mexico News Daily’s features director. He is based in Mexico City. Have an idea for a feature story or unique event in CDMX? Send an email to drew.pittock@mexiconewsdaily.com.

SENEGAL · BUDGET

Key Facts — The country Senegal is a West African democracy and new oil and gas producer that uses the CFA franc, a currency pegged to the euro.

— What happened Senegal sent its draft 2027 budget to parliament, planning a deficit of 4.7% of economic output, against 7.6% in 2026.

— The numbers The deficit is about US$2.3 billion, on revenue of about US$10.2 billion and spending of about US$12.6 billion; interest alone costs about US$2.2 billion.

— Why it matters Senegal is negotiating with foreign bondholders and awaiting a US$2.2 billion IMF programme, and this budget is the plan both will judge.

— The catch Almost the whole deficit is interest on past debt, and the plan assumes growth of only 2.4% and a return of cheap foreign loans.

— Still open The date of the Assembly vote, the IMF board decision and the terms of any deal with bondholders are not known.

The Senegal budget deficit would fall to 4.7% of economic output in 2027, from 7.6% in 2026, under a draft bill before the National Assembly. That is FCFA 1,351.7 billion (about US$2.3 billion), against FCFA 1,735.2 billion (about US$3.0 billion) this year.

For US readers, the bill is the yardstick for Senegal’s foreign bondholders and the International Monetary Fund, known as the IMF. Dakaractu, Seneweb and Le Soleil published the figures on Wednesday 14 and Thursday 15 October.

What the Draft Budget Says

The bill counts on revenue of FCFA 6,012.1 billion (about US$10.2 billion), up 2.8% on the adjusted 2026 budget. Spending would fall 2.9% to FCFA 7,363.7 billion (about US$12.6 billion), a cut of roughly FCFA 220 billion (about US$375 million).

Seneweb, a Dakar news site, reported the Senegal budget deficit figures on Wednesday 14 October from the main lines of the draft law. The Senegal budget deficit plan rests on growth of 2.4% and inflation of 2.7%, according to the Ndarinfo news site.

Where the Savings Come From

The Senegal budget deficit shrinks mainly because general spending is cut, not because the state collects much more, Seneweb and Dakaractu wrote. Domestic revenue outside oil and gas is planned to rise only 0.2%, against a long-run trend above 8%, Dakaractu reported.

Energy subsidies, the state money that keeps fuel and power prices low, are on the cutting list, according to Ndarinfo. The cost is to fall to 1% of output a year by 2029, while small butane cylinders stay protected.

Interest Eats Almost the Whole Budget Deficit

Interest and debt fees come to FCFA 1,303.9 billion (about US$2.2 billion), about 96% of the planned deficit and about 22% of revenue. Before interest, the gap would be only FCFA 47.7 billion (about US$81 million), down from FCFA 450 billion (about US$767 million) in 2026.

The state also needs FCFA 6,608.7 billion (about US$11.3 billion) of financing in total. Of that, FCFA 4,552 billion (about US$7.8 billion) repays old debt and FCFA 480 billion (about US$818 million) clears arrears owed to domestic firms.

The IMF Programme Behind the Numbers

IMF staff and Dakar agreed on 1 September on a three-year credit facility of about US$2.2 billion. The Fund’s board has not yet approved it, and the money depends on Dakar fixing the misreporting of its debt.

The finance ministry expects over FCFA 800 billion (about US$1.4 billion) of cheap, long-term loans and budget support in 2027. The bill calls the return of such concessional financing the key to covering the budget.

Hidden Debt and the Bondholder Talks

The pressure traces back to a 2025 audit by the Court of Auditors, which found far more public debt than the previous government reported. The Fund later said the underreporting was deliberate, and Senegal’s earlier programme was frozen.

Dakar wants to rework its foreign debt, including Eurobonds, and a group of bondholders holding about US$2.2 billion warned against a haircut. A haircut means creditors accept less than they are owed.

Support for Poorer Families and New Taxes

Ndarinfo reported that family security grants for poor households double to FCFA 140 billion (about US$239 million), from FCFA 70 billion (about US$119 million). The programme would reach 1,000,649 households.

New stamp taxes are planned on sugary drinks, alcohol and tobacco, along with a tax on foreign digital services and a phone registration platform. The tax burden is put at 17.5% of output, according to Seneweb.

What It Means for US Readers

Holders of Senegal’s dollar bonds will read this budget as the starting point of the talks, since the deficit shapes the relief Dakar can seek. The United States is the IMF’s largest shareholder, so a failed plan could delay the Fund’s money.

Interest takes almost the whole Senegal budget deficit, so a small miss on revenue or growth would reopen the gap. The CFA franc is fixed to the euro, and on 15 October it traded at 586.7 per US$.

What Is Not Known

The date of the National Assembly vote and any changes to the Senegal budget deficit target are not known. The IMF board has not set a date to approve the programme.

Dakar has not said whether it will ask bondholders to take a loss on principal, or how large any cut would be. The growth forecast of 2.4% and the revenue gains are government assumptions that have yet to be tested.

More: Senegal news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Senegal’s planned budget deficit for 2027?

The Senegal budget deficit is set at FCFA 1,351.7 billion (about US$2.3 billion), or 4.7% of economic output. That compares with 7.6% in the adjusted 2026 budget.

How does Senegal plan to cut the deficit?

Mostly by spending less, with total spending down 2.9% while revenue rises 2.8%. Energy subsidies are on the cutting list.

Why does debt interest matter so much?

Interest and fees of FCFA 1,303.9 billion (about US$2.2 billion) equal almost the whole Senegal budget deficit. Without them, the budget would be close to balance.

What is the IMF’s role?

IMF staff agreed on 1 September to a three-year credit facility of about US$2.2 billion, but the Fund’s board has not approved it. The budget is the fiscal plan behind that deal.

Is the CFA franc tied to the dollar?

No, the CFA franc is fixed to the euro, so its dollar value moves with the euro. On 15 October the rate was 586.7 per US$.

Is the budget final?

No, the bill is a draft that the National Assembly must still debate and vote. The date of the vote has not been announced.

Sources: Seneweb, key figures of the 2027 budget, 14 October 2026; Dakaractu, Budget 2027, 15 October 2026; Le Soleil, 2027 spending, 15 October 2026; Ndarinfo, 2027 budget and subsidies, 15 October 2026; PressAfrik, 2027 finance bill, 15 October 2026.

TANZANIA · TRADE

Key Facts — The country Tanzania is an East African country whose Dar es Salaam Port serves Tanzania and landlocked neighbours such as Zambia and DR Congo.

— What happened On Wednesday 14 October the Transport Ministry’s top civil servant set a target of 1,500 rail containers a day from Dar es Salaam Port.

— The numbers About 500 a day would run on the Tazara line and up to 1,000 on a new 3.8-kilometre standard-gauge link.

— Rail now The Tazara line moves up to 100 containers a day, and two private depot operators are testing a service for about 300 a day.

— The scale The port handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26, so the rail target equals roughly a third of the busiest month’s daily flow.

— What it means for you Faster rail clearance could cut delays and costs on copper and cobalt shipments that pass through Dar es Salaam to world markets.

— Still open No start date, rail price list or cost has been published for the full 1,500 a day.

Tanzania has set a target of 1,500 rail containers a day out of Dar es Salaam Port, a sea gateway for East and Central Africa. Prof Godius Kahyarara, the Transport Ministry’s Permanent Secretary, told The Citizen on Wednesday 14 October that the plan uses railway lines that already exist.

For US readers, the target matters because the port serves Zambia and DR Congo, whose copper and cobalt exports feed American industry. Fewer trucks and faster clearance would cut the time and cost of moving those goods.

What the Ministry Said on 14 October

Prof Kahyarara said preparations were complete to use more rail to inland container depots, the yards where boxes are cleared. He said the aim is to cut the cost of congestion, which delays deliveries and ties up trucks.

The plan relies on lines that have been improved rather than newly built, he told The Citizen. The newspaper’s Gadiosa Lamtey reported the story on Thursday 15 October.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

How the 1,500 Containers Add Up

Two railways make up the total of rail containers. Tazara, owned jointly by Tanzania and Zambia, could carry about 500 a day, and the state operator TRC (Tanzania Railways Corporation) up to 1,000.

The Tazara line already moves up to 100 containers a day from the port, according to the Permanent Secretary. It runs 40 kilometres to depots along Nyerere Road, in Temeke, at the airport and at Mwakanga.

Private Operators Test the Tazara Line

Bravo Logistics and African Inland Container Depot have begun trial runs using hired locomotives and wagons, with capacity for about 300 containers a day. Other depots expected to join could add another 200 a day, which brings Tazara’s potential to 500.

TRC separately runs 22 kilometres of metre-gauge track serving freight and industrial areas in Ilala, Buguruni, Mandela Road, Mabibo and Ubungo. The Permanent Secretary said the existing lines have been improved and are already operating.

The New Standard-Gauge Link to Gate 14

TRC has extended its standard-gauge railway (SGR) by 3.8 kilometres to Gate 14 of the port. The Permanent Secretary said the link allows up to 1,000 rail containers a day to travel to Kwala, Morogoro, Bahi and Isaka.

To prepare, TRC bought diesel-powered wagons for shunting and is rehabilitating 300 metre-gauge wagons. The earnings of the standard-gauge line were covered in an earlier Rio Times report on US$64 million in revenue.

Why the Port Needs the Relief

Chief Government Spokesperson Gerson Msigwa said the port handled a record 138,000 containers in July 2026, the Daily News reported. At that pace the port moves about 4,450 containers a day, so 1,500 rail containers would be about a third.

Port Director Abed Gallus Abed told The Citizen the port handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26. He said moving 300,000 containers to the Kwala depot would still leave more than one million to handle elsewhere.

What Industry Groups Say

Meleck Shange, chairman of the Clearing and Inland Depots Association, said truck jams at the port had fallen after recent improvements. He credited a regional commissioner’s order that no trucks may park along roadsides.

Shange said some inland depots still need upgrades because heavy truck traffic crowds nearby neighbourhoods. He added that the port is adding berths and deepening its channel so larger ships can dock.

What It Means for US Readers

Zambia and DR Congo, major copper and cobalt producers, rely on Dar es Salaam as a sea outlet. Transit cargo rose 17% to 14.61 million tonnes in 2025/26, the Daily News reported on 2 October.

The Tanzania Ports Authority (TPA), the state port owner, is building a container facility with Dubai’s DP World and East Africa Container Terminal. The Daily News reported the plan on 8 September.

The Lobito Corridor, a rail route to Angola’s Atlantic coast backed by Washington, competes for the same minerals. A faster Dar es Salaam route therefore matters for supply chains.

What Is Not Known

No date has been given for when 1,500 containers a day will run, and no rail price list has been published. The Citizen noted that the commercial benefit depends on competitive tariffs, reliable train schedules and efficient handling at the port and depots.

The cost of the Gate 14 link and the new wagons was not stated, nor how many containers TRC carries now. Tazara’s present 100 containers a day is a fifth of the 500 a day it is expected to reach.

More: Tanzania news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Tanzania’s new rail container target?

Tanzania wants 1,500 rail containers a day from Dar es Salaam Port. About 500 would run on the Tazara line and up to 1,000 on the standard-gauge railway.

Who runs the railways involved?

Tanzania Railways Corporation is the state railway operator, and Tazara is the Tanzania-Zambia Railway Authority. Both lines connect the port with depots and inland destinations.

How many containers does Dar es Salaam Port handle?

The port director said it handled about 1.34 million containers in 2025/26. The government said July 2026 set a record of 138,000 containers.

Why does the port need rail?

Trucks carry most cargo out of the port and cause jams that delay deliveries and raise costs. Rail containers travel together in one train and take pressure off city roads.

Why should US companies care?

Dar es Salaam is an outlet for copper and cobalt from Zambia and DR Congo, which US industry buys. Smoother rail clearance can shorten delays on those shipments.

When will the 1,500 containers a day start?

No start date has been announced. Tazara carries up to 100 containers a day at present, and the standard-gauge line has been extended 3.8 kilometres to Gate 14 of the port.

GHANA · ECONOMY

Key Facts — The country Ghana is a West African democracy of more than 30 million people and a major gold producer, led by President John Dramani Mahama.

— What happened On Thursday 15 October, the Ghana Statistical Service said economic activity in July grew 7.4% from July 2025.

— The numbers Services grew 12.2%, industry 5.4% and agriculture 3.7%. The activity index reached 121.6, up from 113.2 a year earlier.

— The trend Monthly growth was 4.7% in April, 6.0% in May and 6.5% in June. The Bank of Ghana put second-quarter growth at 6.0%.

— The drivers Information and communication led services, mining and quarrying led industry, and crops and livestock led agriculture, the statistics office said.

— Still open The figure is an early monthly estimate, and official third-quarter growth data has not yet been released.

The Ghana economy grew 7.4% in July from a year earlier, the Ghana Statistical Service reported on Thursday 15 October. The pace is up from 6.5% in June, driven by a 12.2% surge in services led by telecoms and internet.

For US investors, the figure shows that Ghana’s recovery after its debt default and IMF rescue is still gathering pace. It matters most to holders of the restructured dollar bonds and to US-listed energy firms.

What the Statistics Office Reported for July

The Ghana Statistical Service is the government agency that counts the Ghana economy, headed by Government Statistician Dr Alhassan Iddrisu. It published the July figure in its Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth, an early monthly gauge that arrives before official quarterly figures.

The indicator rose to 121.6 in July from 113.2 in July 2025, a gain of 7.4%. A year earlier, growth in the same month was only 4.9%, so the comparison base was low.

The release was reported on Thursday by Citi Newsroom and by MyJoyOnline, two leading Ghanaian news sites. Both gave the same sector figures and the same 7.4% headline.

This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Services Drove the Jump

Services grew 12.2% in July, against 6.7% in the same month of 2025. The largest part of the Ghana economy includes telecoms, banking, trade, transport and government, and it supplied 63.8% of the month’s growth.

Within services, information and communication was the biggest contributor, the statistics office said. That covers mobile networks, internet providers and the software and data firms that serve Ghana’s more than 30 million people.

Industry added 20.5% of the growth and agriculture 14.1%, MyJoyOnline reported. Net indirect taxes made up the remaining 1.6%.

Mining Lifts Industry While Farming Slows

Industry grew 5.4% in July, compared with just 0.4% a year earlier. Mining and quarrying provided the main push in the Ghana economy, the statistics office said, in a country that is a major gold exporter.

Agriculture slowed to 3.7% from 8.2% in July 2025, with crops and livestock the main contributors. The cooler farm figure is the weak spot in an otherwise strong month, because farming employs a large share of Ghanaians.

Citi Newsroom reported the statistics office as saying the priority is to sustain services growth while strengthening agriculture. That points to a recovery that leans heavily on one sector.

How July Compares With Earlier Months

Monthly growth was 4.7% in April, 6.0% in May and 6.5% in June, according to Ghanaian outlets reporting each release. February was stronger, at 7.7%, so July marks a return to the early-year pace.

April looked weak against a high base, since April 2025 had grown 7.4%. The central bank, led by Governor Johnson Asiama, put real growth at 6.0% in the second quarter.

The Bank of Ghana held its policy rate at 14% in September, the third straight hold this year. Headline inflation was 5.2% in September, the statistics office said on Wednesday 7 October, up from 5.0% in August.

What It Means for US Readers

Ghana finished a US$3 billion IMF loan programme in July, and the IMF’s Africa director praised that record on Thursday 15 October. Faster growth helps the government raise tax revenue and keep paying the restructured dollar bonds US funds hold.

Inflation of 5.2% sits below the central bank’s target band of 6% to 10%, which leaves room for steady policy. Ghana’s oil and gold also matter to US-listed firms such as Kosmos Energy, a partner in the Jubilee oil field.

Travellers and exporters should see little change, because the Ghana economy figure does not alter US visa, tariff or security policy. It is a signal for investors, not a trigger for new rules.

The cedi trades at about 11.69 per US dollar on 15 October, according to open exchange-rate data. Growth numbers alone rarely move a currency, and Ghana’s inflation and central bank decisions matter more.

What Is Not Known

The statistics office has not said when it will publish third-quarter GDP, the full measure of output. Monthly estimates are provisional and can change when more data arrives.

How much of the services surge came from telecoms and how much from other activities is still open. Whether mining output rose on volumes or on higher gold prices is also unclear.

The Bank of Ghana has not said how the July figure will shape its next rate decision. Its September statement called the balance of risks to inflation and growth broadly balanced.

More: Ghana news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What does Ghana’s 7.4% growth figure measure?

It is the year-on-year rise in the Monthly Indicator of Economic Growth for July, compared with July 2025, and it tracks the whole Ghana economy. It is an early estimate that comes before official quarterly GDP.

Which parts of Ghana’s economy grew fastest in July?

Services grew 12.2%, led by information and communication. Industry grew 5.4% on mining, and agriculture grew 3.7%.

Is the Ghana economy growing faster than before?

July’s 7.4% beat June’s 6.5% and May’s 6.0%.

Why did Ghana’s agriculture growth slow?

Farm growth in the Ghana economy fell to 3.7% from 8.2% in July 2025, with crops and livestock still the main contributors. The statistics office did not give a reason for the slowdown.

Does the figure change anything for US investors?

It supports the view that the Ghana economy’s recovery after its debt restructuring is holding. It does not change any US rules on trade, travel or sanctions.

World.title: Somalia Constitution Bill Due in 2 Months
World.content:
SOMALIA · POLITICS

Key Facts — What is happening Somalia’s Council of Ministers, chaired by Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre, approved a plan on Tuesday, 13 October to implement the new constitution and gave a ministerial committee two months to draft a bill on the structure of government.

— Why it matters The bill would set the size and duties of the cabinet under the 2026 constitution, as a row over the government’s mandate continues and a deadline on dual posts has just passed.

— The numbers Two months is the drafting window, six months was the transition on dual posts that ended on 14 October, and the new law is described as the first of its kind since 1968.

— Who is who Hamza Abdi Barre is prime minister, Hassan Moalim Mohamud is the justice and constitutional affairs minister who chairs the committee, and President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s mandate is disputed by opposition figures.

— What to watch The two month drafting deadline, which ends around 13 December if counted from the cabinet meeting, a possible opposition case at the Supreme Court, and the elections set for 15 April and 15 May 2027, which the opposition rejects.

— What it means for you US travellers face no change to the Level 4 Do Not Travel advisory, and Washington’s counterterrorism partner is a government whose mandate the opposition contests, which could complicate security cooperation.

Somalia’s cabinet has given a ministerial committee two months to draft a law on how the federal government is built. The order lands as the opposition disputes the president’s mandate and a deadline on dual posts passes.

The Somalia constitution bill that the cabinet ordered on Tuesday, 13 October must be drafted within two months. It will set out the structure of the federal government, including the size and responsibilities of the cabinet, SONNA reports.

Somalia is a front-line state against the militant group al-Shabaab and a long-time security partner of Washington. How its government is organised, and for how long it governs, therefore matters well beyond Mogadishu.

What the Cabinet Decided on 13 October

SONNA, the Somali National News Agency, reported the resolution on Tuesday, 13 October. It says the Council of Ministers, the federal cabinet, met in extraordinary session that evening under Prime Minister Hamza Abdi Barre.

The cabinet appointed a ministerial committee, chaired by the Minister of Justice and Constitutional Affairs, to speed up implementation of the constitution. Dawan Africa, a regional news site, adds that the committee includes the interior, finance, endowments, education and information ministers.

Within two months, the committee must draft a bill on the structure of the federal government. The government calls it the first law of its kind since 1968, SONNA says.

Dawan Africa’s account of the resolution adds a directive to all government institutions. They must ensure that administrative measures without a constitutional basis are not carried out through conflicting procedures.

The Justice Ministry and other relevant bodies must also inform the public about how implementation will proceed. A separate technical committee will help schedule and monitor priority work, though its members have not been named.

Prime Minister Hamza said the constitution is in force and is being implemented in stages, SONNA says. He added that the government is working toward federal one person, one vote elections next year.

Dawan Africa also covered a press briefing on Wednesday, 14 October by committee chair Hassan Moalim Mohamud, the justice minister. It says he described implementation as phased work that needs new laws, new institutions and changes in how government operates.

Why the 14 October Deadline on Dual Posts Matters

The constitution took effect on 14 April 2026, the commission says, and a six-month transition ended on Wednesday, 14 October. The Independent Constitutional Review and Implementation Commission said on 7 October that it would then enforce the dual post ban.

Under the provisions the commission cited, a minister who also sits in parliament loses the cabinet seat. A lawmaker who accepts another government post loses the parliamentary seat.

The commission oversees the rollout, and chairman Burhan Aden Omar called enforcement a constitutional obligation, Dawan Africa reported. Dawan Africa said the rule could affect dozens of ministers and deputy ministers, but no official count was found.

Garowe Online, a Somali news site, said on Monday, 12 October that parliamentary leaders wanted the provisions enforced from 14 October. It added that some cabinet members from Jubaland and Puntland, two federal member states, had raised concerns.

Garowe also described open questions about how vacated seats would be filled and whether ministers could keep posts after leaving parliament. Much of its account is attributed to unnamed sources, so it is treated here as unconfirmed.

A Mandate Dispute Sits Behind the Plan

In May, President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud said the amended constitution gives the federal government a five-year term to 15 May 2027. Dawan Africa reported that he also said the executive and parliament would be separated and implementation had already started.

Opposition figures say his term ended on 15 May 2026, Garowe Online reported on Tuesday, 13 October. They accuse him of clinging to power and call for an inclusive electoral agreement.

The federal government is pushing a one person, one vote system, which it says lets citizens choose their own leaders. Critics, who are not named, say any process needs broad consensus to avoid deeper division.

Garowe Online reported on 12 October, citing unnamed sources, that the Supreme Court accepted an opposition lawsuit against the new constitution. The report says a senior Somali Salvation Council member filed it; accepting a case is not a ruling on the merits.

What It Means for US Readers

The US State Department rates Somalia Level 4, Do Not Travel, in an advisory issued on Thursday, 21 May 2026. Nothing in the cabinet’s decision changes that advice.

Washington has long backed Somalia’s government against al-Shabaab, and a contested political calendar can complicate that work. That is an assessment, and none of the sources describes a change in US policy.

Somalia’s finance minister, Bihi Iman Egeh, met World Bank and IMF officials in Bangkok this week, the Ministry of Finance said. The talks covered reforms and financing, and the ministry gave no figures.

Direct market exposure for US investors is minimal, so the practical stakes are security cooperation, aid and travel risk. Background on the wider region is collected in the Horn of Africa and the Red Sea hub.

What Is Not Known

It is not confirmed how many officials with dual posts chose one seat on 14 October. No official count of affected officials was found, and Dawan Africa’s own totals differed between April and October.

The full text of the cabinet resolution has not been seen, and the technical committee’s members are not named. The committee chair’s estimate of how long full implementation will take came from one outlet only, so it is not repeated here.

The Supreme Court case rests on unnamed sources, and no court statement or hearing date has been reported. Whether opposition leaders and the federal member states will accept the bill is also unknown.

What Comes Next

The two-month drafting window runs to about 13 December if counted from the cabinet meeting, although no start date was published. The bill is meant to fix the size and duties of the cabinet.

The cabinet plan does not set an election date, and it does not settle the dispute over the government’s mandate. The prime minister has said one person, one vote elections are the goal for next year.

On Thursday, 15 October, the national electoral commission announced parliamentary elections for 15 April 2027 and a presidential vote on 15 May. Dawan Africa and Garowe Online reported that the opposition rejects the timetable.

Frequently Asked Questions

What did Somalia’s cabinet decide on 13 October?

It approved a resolution on implementing the new constitution and set up a ministerial committee chaired by the justice minister. The committee has two months to prepare a bill on the structure of the federal government.

What is the 14 October deadline for ministers?

The constitution bars ministers from also sitting in parliament, and a six-month transition ended on 14 October. The constitutional commission said it would begin enforcing the rule from that date.

Who disputes the government’s mandate?

Opposition figures say President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s term ended on 15 May 2026. The president says the amended constitution gives the federal government a term to 15 May 2027.

Is it safe for US citizens to travel to Somalia?

The State Department rates Somalia Level 4, Do Not Travel, in an advisory issued on 21 May 2026. The advisory says not to travel to Somalia for any reason.

Does this affect US investors?

Direct exposure for US investors is minimal. The main relevance is security cooperation, aid and regional stability in the Horn of Africa.

SOUTH AFRICA · INVESTMENT

Key Facts — The country South Africa is Africa’s most industrialised economy, and KwaZulu-Natal is its eastern coastal province, home to the port city of Durban.

— What happened Investment pledges of R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) were made at the 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference in Durban, IOL reported on Thursday 15 October.

— The target The province had aimed for R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion), so the pledges beat the goal by nearly R30 billion (about US$1.8 billion).

— The pledgers 47 companies and entities made pledges, led by Senzo Esihle Rail at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion).

— The backdrop Soldiers were sent into central Durban on Saturday 10 October after days of anti-immigrant violence.

— Still open A pledge is a promise, not a contract, and the province has not said how much money has been committed in writing.

Investment pledges to KwaZulu-Natal, the South African province around the port city of Durban, reached R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion). IOL, a South African news site, reported the total on Thursday 15 October after the provincial investment conference.

For US readers, the figure matters because soldiers were sent into Durban days earlier over anti-immigrant violence. The investment pledges beat the province’s R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion) target by nearly R30 billion (about US$1.8 billion).

What Was Pledged in Durban

The 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference took place at the Inkosi Albert Luthuli International Convention Centre in Durban, IOL reported. A total of 47 companies and entities made pledges.

The largest single pledge came from Senzo Esihle Rail at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion). Azania MediaWorks followed at R6.5 billion (about US$0.4 billion), and Cedar Falls Properties 205 pledged R4.5 billion (about US$0.3 billion).

Bidvest Freight pledged R2.015 billion (about US$0.1 billion), Afchlor R1.75 billion (about US$0.1 billion) and AJ Property Holdings R1.072 billion (about US$0.06 billion). IOL named only these six amounts, so the other 41 pledges were not itemised.

Follow this story Get an email when there’s news on South Africa Email address Follow Free. One email a day at most, and only when there is news. This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Who Is Behind the Conference

Premier Thami Ntuli, the head of the provincial government, led the event. Trade, Industry and Competition Minister Parks Tau, the national minister in charge of trade policy, joined him.

Musa Zondi, the provincial minister for economic development, and Cyril Xaba, the mayor of the eThekwini municipality that governs Durban, also took part. Musawenkosi Myeni, chair of Trade and Investment KwaZulu-Natal, the provincial investment agency, joined Tau and Ntuli to launch an investment booklet for 2026 to 2028.

Ntuli told the audience that KwaZulu-Natal is “open for business”. He said the pledges would be spread across all districts, adding that “a province that grows in one place is a province at risk”.

Pledges Beat Last Year’s Result

Last year’s investment pledges came to R100.1 billion (about US$6 billion), The Mercury reported on 23 October 2025. This year’s total is about R24 billion (about US$1.5 billion) higher.

The 2025 investment pledges were expected to create about 260,000 construction jobs and more than 60,000 permanent jobs, The Mercury said. Projects were meant to start within three years, and Zondi said some businesses held back because they could not meet that timeline.

The Unrest Behind the Headline

Soldiers began patrolling central Durban on Saturday 10 October after days of anti-immigrant violence, as Rio Times reported at the time. The protests began at the city’s refugee reception office, where a movement called March and March campaigns against illegal immigration.

Police reported 19 arrests in Durban between Thursday 8 and Saturday 10 October. In September, police whisked the mayor away from a hostile crowd during earlier anti-immigrant protests in the city.

IOL’s headline said the billions were pledged despite the protests. The conference took place in the same city where soldiers had patrolled days earlier.

Why Durban Matters to Investors

Durban is South Africa’s third-largest city and home to one of Africa’s busiest container ports. Bidvest Freight, one of the named pledgers, is a logistics company.

The six pledges IOL named add up to about R50 billion (about US$3 billion), or 40 percent of the total. That leaves about R75 billion (about US$4.5 billion) in pledges from the other 41 companies and entities.

What It Means for US Readers

Investors with exposure to South African ports, rail and property will watch whether these investment pledges turn into signed projects. The rand figures also shift with the exchange rate, which stood near 16.58 rand to the US dollar on 15 October.

Travellers and companies with staff in Durban can weigh the investment message against the unrest of early October. Government travel advice remains the best guide to local security.

What Is Not Known

Nobody has said how much of the R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) is signed and funded. IOL named no US company and did not say how many pledges come from foreign investors.

The province has not published a full list of the 47 pledges or a timetable for the projects. It has also not said how many jobs this year’s investment pledges could create.

More: South Africa news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much did investors pledge to KwaZulu-Natal?

Investors pledged R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) at the 2026 KwaZulu-Natal Investment Conference in Durban. The province had set a target of R95 billion (about US$5.7 billion).

Who made the biggest pledge?

Senzo Esihle Rail made the largest pledge at R34.104 billion (about US$2.1 billion). It was one of 47 companies and entities that made pledges, according to IOL.

Are investment pledges the same as investment?

No, a pledge is a stated intention to invest, not a signed contract or money already spent. Projects can be delayed or dropped if funding or approvals fall through.

How does this compare with last year?

The 2025 conference produced R100.1 billion (about US$6 billion) in investment pledges, according to The Mercury. This year’s R124.5 billion (about US$7.5 billion) is higher.

Is it safe to travel to Durban?

Soldiers were sent into central Durban on 10 October after anti-immigrant violence, and police reported 19 arrests. Travellers should check their government’s travel advice and local news before visiting.

World.content:

DR CONGO · HEALTH FUNDING

Key Facts — The country DR Congo is a central African nation where an Ebola outbreak of the Bundibugyo strain has run since May.

— What happened On Wednesday 14 October, Africa CDC chief Jean Kaseya said about US$700 million of Ebola funds paid out by donors has not been traced.

— The numbers Donors say they paid out more than US$900 million, and about US$200 million has been traced, nearly US$100 million of it unspent.

— The reply Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba has threatened to strip the accreditation of aid groups that cannot show how they spent their funds.

— The outbreak Journal de Kinshasa put the toll at 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths on 15 October, with the east of the country hardest hit.

— US link The US State Department says Washington has provided US$887 million for this Ebola response, and a CDC order still bars travellers from DR Congo.

— Still open Kaseya has not said where the money sits, and no donor or aid group has answered in public.

Ebola funds worth about US$700 million have not been traced, the head of Africa CDC said in Kinshasa on Wednesday 14 October. Actualite.cd, Radio Okapi and Congo Quotidien, three Congolese news outlets, reported his remarks on Thursday 15 October.

Donors say they paid out more than US$900 million to the groups running the response, and about US$200 million has been traced. Washington says it has provided US$887 million to this response, though no report names any donor behind the missing money.

What Jean Kaseya Said in Kinshasa

Kaseya leads Africa CDC, the African Union’s public health agency, and has been in DR Congo since 13 October. He told a news conference that donors had sent him their Ebola funds figures through diplomatic notes.

Of the Ebola funds donors say they paid to implementing partners, the aid groups running the response, only about US$200 million has been traced. Nearly US$100 million of that has not yet been spent, he said.

That leaves about US$700 million still to find, money that in his words “exists”. He promised to press each partner for an account and said, “we will not let go”.
