This also signs you up to our weekday newsletter, Africa Intelligence. Nothing arrives until you click the confirmation link, and you can stop either with one click. Privacy policy

Why Tracing the Money Is Hard

The traced figure comes from a meeting convened by the National Institute of Public Health, known as INSP, with the health ministry’s technical lead. Fewer than 30% of the partners took part, and Radio Okapi reported that only those present declared amounts.

At a press briefing on 2 October, INSP director general Dieudonné Mwamba said only 25 of about 94 accredited partners had sent information, Actualite.cd reported. Those groups reported receiving US$226.3 million and spending US$127.4 million.

How Congo’s Government Is Responding

Health Minister Roger Samuel Kamba called the handling of Ebola funds a “flou artistique”, a French phrase for a deliberate-looking blur. He announced coercive measures against groups that cannot justify their funds, following an instruction from President Félix Tshisekedi.

Groups that fail to comply could lose their accreditation and face action by the immigration directorate, known as DGM. The government has written to the partners concerned, Actualite.cd reported.

Kamba said the first three-month response plan raised about US$227 million, of which nearly US$99 million was unused. He added that the state’s own US$50 million was spent transparently, according to a report sent to the prime minister.

Kamba also said the lack of visibility on partner funds complicates talks with the International Monetary Fund on budget support. The IMF lends to governments and often asks for proof that public money is tracked.

The Outbreak Behind the Money

The disease is Ebola of the Bundibugyo strain, for which no vaccine or treatment is approved. The World Health Organization declared a public health emergency of international concern on 17 May.

Journal de Kinshasa, a Congolese news site, put the toll at 9,144 cases and 4,410 deaths on 15 October. Ituri province in the east is at the centre, and Radio Okapi reported no new case for 21 days in Tchomia, a locality in Ituri.

Radio Okapi also listed a further US$80 million from the World Bank for the response on 15 October. The World Bank is the global development lender that funds public health and infrastructure projects.

A G20 meeting in New York raised about US$2.6 billion in Ebola commitments in September, Kaseya said at the time. He asked that the money reach people in need directly and that its use be tracked.

What It Means for US Readers

The State Department, which took over US emergency aid after USAID closed in 2025, said on 23 September that it had provided US$887 million. Rio Times reported that total when the latest US$267 million was announced.

No report ties the United States to the untraced Ebola funds, and the donors behind them are not named. Taxpayers still have a stake, because a leaky response can let the outbreak run longer.

The CDC says anyone who has been in DR Congo within 21 days cannot board a commercial flight to the United States. US citizens are told to stay outside DR Congo for 21 days before entering, and the page was updated on 13 October.

What Is Not Known

Kaseya has not said which partners hold the missing Ebola funds or where they went. Outlets quote the donor total as US$926.66 million or US$962 million, so the gap of about US$700 million is rounded.

No donor, aid group or health agency has answered in public, and no investigation has been announced. Journal de Kinshasa stressed that the statements point to a tracing problem, not to embezzlement.

More: DR Congo news in English, every day from The Rio Times.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is Africa CDC?

Africa CDC is the African Union’s public health agency, based in Addis Ababa and led by Jean Kaseya. It coordinates Africa’s response to outbreaks such as Ebola.

How many Ebola funds are untraced in DR Congo?

Kaseya said about US$700 million of the Ebola funds donors say they paid out has not been traced. Donors report more than US$900 million, and about US$200 million has been traced.

Does untraced money mean it was stolen?

No report says so, and Kaseya says the Ebola funds exist. Journal de Kinshasa stressed that the statements show a tracing problem, not embezzlement.

Which outbreak is the money for?

It is for the Bundibugyo strain Ebola outbreak in DR Congo, centred on Ituri province. No vaccine or treatment is approved for this strain.

Can Americans travel to DR Congo?

The CDC bars anyone who has been in DR Congo within 21 days from boarding commercial flights to the United States. US citizens should stay outside DR Congo for 21 days before entering.

World.title: DR Congo Ebola Aid Over US$700M Unreported
World.content:
DR CONGO · EBOLA FUNDING

Key Facts — What is happening Africa CDC, the African Union health agency, said on Wednesday, 14 October, that more than US$700 million of Ebola response money paid to partners working in DR Congo is unknown to national authorities.

— Why it matters Donors pay for the Ebola response through international groups, so an accounting gap about three quarters the size of the payments raises oversight questions for every donor government, including Washington.

— The numbers Donors paid nearly US$962 million to international organisations and NGOs; the groups that shared figures declared about US$220 million received, US$120 million spent and US$100 million unspent, leaving more than US$700 million unreported.

— Who is who Africa CDC is the African Union’s continental health agency, led by Director General Jean Kaseya, and the INSP is Congo’s national public health institute, which convened the partners to report their funds.

— What to watch Africa CDC and the government plan to reconcile every payment, and the agency would back suspending the accreditation of organisations that stay silent, though no date or name has been announced.

— What it means for you Americans who fund global health through the government or charities should watch whether donors demand itemised accounts from partners, while the statements announce no change to travel or health advice.

Africa CDC says more than US$700 million of Ebola response money is unknown to national authorities in DR Congo. The agency says donors paid the funds to international partners, not to the Congolese government.

More than US$700 million of DR Congo Ebola aid is unknown to national authorities, Africa CDC said on Wednesday, 14 October. Director General Jean Kaseya spoke in Kinshasa, and the agency repeated the figure in a statement dated Thursday, 15 October.

Donors paid nearly US$962 million directly to the international organisations and NGOs that run the response, not to the Congolese state. The groups that shared figures with officials declared receiving about US$220 million.

The Gap in DR Congo Ebola Aid Reports

Only about 30% of the organisations attended a verification meeting convened by the head of the INSP and shared financial data. The INSP is Congo’s national public health institute, and Dr Hyppolite Kalambay, Africa CDC’s country director in Congo, supported the meeting.

Those groups said they had received about US$220 million, of which US$120 million was spent and US$100 million remains unspent. Subtracting that from nearly US$962 million leaves more than US$700 million that national authorities cannot account for.

Radio Okapi, a Congolese radio network, gave a similar picture of the Wednesday press conference. It put the traced amount at about US$200 million and the unspent sum at about US$100 million.

Ask Open the full Ask Rio Times →

What Africa CDC Says Happens Next

Africa CDC says it will work with the government to reconcile the funding and identify what each organisation received. The exercise is to document spending, remaining balances, activities and results.

The agency calls the partners’ lack of cooperation unacceptable and says sovereignty carries duties to respect national coordination and accountability rules. It would back administrative measures the government judges necessary, up to suspending or withdrawing an organisation’s accreditation.

Africa CDC may also alert authorities in other African countries to the names of organisations that do not comply. Its written statement does not name the organisations that failed to report.

Africa CDC Stops Short of Alleging Theft

In an interview with Actualite.cd, a Kinshasa news site, Kaseya said the money being sought is with the partners, not the government. He called it unclear management and added that he was not yet speaking of embezzlement.

The written statement describes a reporting gap, saying the amounts remain unknown to national authorities. It says the partners have not provided the information, which is a different finding from lost money.

That wording matters because some headlines have called the sum untraceable or missing. The statement itself does not say any money was lost, stolen or misused.

Earlier Calls for Transparency

On 4 October, Africa CDC said it backed the Congolese government’s call for stronger transparency and traceability in Ebola funding. It promised to strengthen its Financial Tracking Mechanism, which gathers partner data and flags funding gaps.

That statement put announced donor commitments at US$2.9 billion, far above the nearly US$962 million now said to have been paid. Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka urged rapid disbursement of those pledges at a G20+ meeting in New York on 23 September.

Africa CDC also said it supports administrative action against organisations that miss reporting rules, in line with national law. President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo had led a high-level meeting on Wednesday, 5 August that set priorities on coordination and financial accountability.

What It Means for US Readers

The State Department announced an additional US$267 million for the Ebola response in DR Congo on 23 September. The Africa CDC statements do not say whether any US money sits inside the unreported amount.

For US readers, the question is oversight: will donors demand itemised accounts from the groups that spend their money? US charities and contractors working in Congo could face tougher reporting demands, because Africa CDC backs sanctions on groups that stay silent.

Travellers should note that the finding concerns accounting, not the outbreak, and the statements announce no change to health advice. Nothing in the statements points to a change in entry rules for Congo.

What Is Not Known

The statements do not name the organisations that failed to report or say how much each donor paid. They also do not say whether any US money is in the unreported amount.

The figures differ across statements, with about US$200 million, US$220 million and US$228 million given for the amount already traced. No audit report was linked in any of the statements, and the numbers come from Africa CDC and its Congolese partners.

Kaseya said in the interview that US officials promised a list of every partner that received money. No US statement confirming this was found.

He also said Africa CDC will publish a report on where each amount went. No publication date has been given.

What Comes Next

Africa CDC and the Congolese government now have to reconcile the payments, and no deadline has been announced. The step to watch is whether the government suspends the accreditation of any organisation that stays silent.

Nothing in the statements says the Ebola response has stopped or that any money has been shown to be stolen. The gap concerns reporting, and it will narrow only if the partners publish their figures.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much Ebola money is unaccounted for in DR Congo?

Africa CDC says more than US$700 million is unknown to national authorities. Donors paid nearly US$962 million, and partners have declared receiving about US$220 million.

Does Africa CDC say the money was stolen?

No, its statement describes a reporting gap and does not allege theft or misuse. Director General Jean Kaseya told Actualite.cd he was not yet speaking of embezzlement.

Who received the money?

Donors paid it directly to international organisations and NGOs that run the response, not to the Congolese government. Only about 30% of those groups attended the meeting where they were asked to report.

What happens to organisations that do not report?

Africa CDC says it would support government measures up to suspending or withdrawing their accreditation. It may also alert authorities in other African countries to the names of non-compliant groups.

Does this affect US readers or travellers?

It raises oversight questions for donors such as the United States, but the statements do not say whether US funds are involved. The finding concerns accounting, and the statements announce no change to health advice.

Sources: Africa CDC statement of 15 October 2026; US State Department media note of 23 September 2026; Africa CDC statement of 4 October 2026; Actualite.cd, interview with Jean Kaseya; Radio Okapi; Actualite.cd, report of 15 October (all accessed 15 October 2026).

World.title: What to Do in Cancún in October 2026
World.content:
CANCÚN · Culture

A week-long rock festival at a resort, a symphony in a cenote and free theatre downtown. The rest of the month, day by day.

Beachfront hotels along the Zona Hotelera in Cancún. File photo (dronepicr, CC BY 2.0 via Wikimedia Commons).

CANCÚN — This guide is for people who live here, not weekend tourists. It covers things to do in Cancún in October 2026 from Friday 16 October to Halloween, with venues, dates and practical notes for expats and long-stay visitors.

October in Cancún is hot, humid and often wet, with brief heavy showers and the tail end of hurricane season. The Atlantic season officially runs until 30 November, so keep an eye on weather alerts before planning outdoor events.

The month has a clear shape. Free municipal and cultural events fill the first weekend of this guide, the big rock festival takes over a hotel-zone resort from 20 to 25 October, and Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October before Día de Muertos on 1 and 2 November.

Mexico’s federal mandatory-rest-day list does not include 12 October 2026; after 16 September, the next generally applicable federal mandatory rest day is 16 November 2026, followed by 25 December 2026. That means banks and most shops keep normal hours through the rest of October.

Friday 16 to Sunday 18 October: Free Culture Downtown

Cancún’s municipal programme leans on free events at Teatro de la Ciudad, the city’s main theatre in the centre. Prices below are as listed by the Riviera Lowdown events calendar, with pesos converted at about 18.4 pesos per US dollar (RT spot, 15 October 2026).

Friday 16 October, 8:00 p.m. Rocktubre Teatro de la Ciudad, Cancún · Free A free rock evening at the city’s main municipal theatre. It is an easy first night out for residents who live downtown.

Friday 16 October, 9:00 p.m. Retro Disco Centro Cultural Underground Xtabay, Cancún · Free A free retro dance night at an independent cultural centre. It suits long-stay visitors who want a local crowd rather than a hotel-zone club.

Saturday 17 October, 6:00 p.m. Décadas Parque de Las Palapas, downtown Cancún · Free A free open-air music session in the park that serves as downtown’s social square. Arrive early on a Saturday evening, because the park fills with families.

Saturday 17 October, 8:00 p.m. Art After Dark Marina Puerto Cancún · MXN 350 (about US$19) An evening art event at the marina development on the edge of the hotel zone. It is the more upmarket pick of the weekend.

Saturday 17 October, 8:00 p.m. Multiverso de la Locura Centro Cultural Toltecayotl, Cancún · MXN 250 (about US$14) A paid evening show at a community cultural centre.

Sunday 18 October, 6:00 p.m. Soy Puro Mexicano Teatro de la Ciudad, Cancún · Free A free Sunday-evening show at the municipal theatre. It is a gentle way to end the weekend.

The Sands Rocks at Paradisus: 20 to 25 October

The biggest music event of the month is not a normal concert. SANDS 2026 is an adults-only private event that takes over the Paradisus Cancún resort in the hotel zone from Tuesday 20 to Sunday 25 October 2026, with attendance limited to 1,200 guests.

The announced line-up is Orchestral Manoeuvres in the Dark, Bobby Brown, Queensrÿche, Cutting Crew, Dishwalla, Winger, Sheila E. and The Smithereens. Tickets are sold as resort packages through the organiser at thesands.rocks, not as single-night entries, and the organiser has not published a day-by-day running order.

During SANDS, 20 to 25 October Cutting Crew at The Sands Paradisus Cancún, hotel zone · Package price on the organiser’s site The British band behind the 1980s hit “(I Just) Died in Your Arms” lists this show on its own tour page. Because the festival is a private package, residents cannot simply buy a ticket for one night at the door.

Late October: A Symphony in a Cenote and Halloween

Friday 30 October Symphony in a Cenote Fairmont Mayakoba, Riviera Maya near Playa del Carmen · Hotel booking The hotel announced a one-night orchestral concert inside a cenote, limited to 50 guests, with private transport from the resort. Ask the hotel on +52 984 206 3000 for the current booking terms, because its own event page still says details are coming soon.

Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October. Many bars, hotels and expat groups host parties that night, so book tables early and expect higher prices for taxis late in the evening.

Planning your Cancún in October

Carry an umbrella and expect sudden downpours, especially later in the day. Tropical systems can bring longer rain, so check forecasts before travelling far.

Downtown venues such as Teatro de la Ciudad and Parque de Las Palapas are in the centre of the city. The hotel zone, where Paradisus and the marina sit, is a taxi or bus ride away.

Getting around at night is easiest by taxi or ride-hailing app, though availability can be patchy late in the evening. Agree a fare before you get in, or use an app that shows the price first.

Smaller venues often take cash only, so carry some pesos. For paid events, buy from the venue or organiser, because Mexican listings change dates and prices at short notice.

Día de Muertos is on 1 and 2 November. Altars and decorations begin to appear in public spaces in the last days of October.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the biggest music event in Cancún in October 2026?

SANDS 2026 at Paradisus Cancún runs from 20 to 25 October as an adults-only private event limited to 1,200 guests. Queensrÿche, Cutting Crew, Winger and Sheila E. are on the announced line-up.

Can I buy a single-night ticket for The Sands Rocks?

The organiser sells the festival as an all-inclusive resort package at thesands.rocks. It has not published single-night entry or a day-by-day running order.

Is there a public holiday in Cancún in October 2026?

12 October 2026 is not a mandatory rest day under Mexico’s Federal Labor Law; Día de la Raza, now Día de la Nación Pluricultural, is commemorated but is not a federal labor holiday.

What is the weather like in Cancún in October?

Expect hot, humid days with brief heavy showers and a continuing tropical-cyclone risk. The Atlantic hurricane season officially runs until 30 November.

Are there free events in Cancún this month?

Yes. Rocktubre and Soy Puro Mexicano at Teatro de la Ciudad, Décadas at Parque de Las Palapas and Retro Disco at Centro Cultural Underground Xtabay are listed as free on 16, 17 and 18 October.

World.title: Credit Card Purchases Offer New Leads in Killing of American in Costa Rica
World.content:
Supermarket purchases and a hotel stay allegedly paid for with a dead American’s credit cards have given investigators new leads in the search for a woman suspected in his killing in Playas del Coco. The transactions reportedly included purchases at supermarkets in Playas del Coco and Brasilito, lodging at a hotel in Flamingo and food bought at a small store in Abangares.

Investigators believe the woman later went to San José. The purchases have helped authorities reconstruct part of her movements after she left the condominium where the victim was found. The findings add detail to the investigation into the death of a 74-year-old American in Playas del Coco on September 27. Investigators had been examining whether the victim’s bank cards were stolen and subsequently used. The latest information identifies several locations where those purchases allegedly occurred.

The victim, identified by his last name Fleming, entered a condominium in Sardinal de Carrillo with the woman at approximately 4:50 p.m. She left sometime later. His body was subsequently discovered with head injuries believed to have been caused by blunt objects. Fleming was reportedly a retired businessman who had been living in Playas del Coco, one of Guanacaste’s busiest beach communities.

The Judicial Investigation Agency (OIJ), released surveillance footage on the 12th as part of a public appeal to identify the woman. Investigators described her as light-skinned and slim, with black hair, standing approximately 1.60 meters, or 5 feet 3 inches. At the time, she was wearing sandals, blue denim shorts and a white bra-style top with chain-like details across the front. Security footage captured her movements, providing investigators with images to circulate publicly.

Anyone who recognizes the woman or has information that could help investigators identify or locate her can contact the OIJ’s confidential tip line at 800-800-0645.

World.title: Costa Rica’s Public Schools Have Lost 180,000 Students in Five Years
World.content:
Costa Rica’s public schools have 179,568 fewer students than they did in 2021, a drop of about 16.5% in five years, as the falling birth rate empties classrooms. Public enrollment fell from 1,087,606 students in 2021 to 908,038 in 2026, according to Ministry of Public Education (MEP) data. The ministry projects another decline next year, to 873,086 students, nearly 35,000 fewer.

Public schools are losing an estimated 30,000 to 42,000 students a year. Twenty-five public schools closed between 2019 and 2022, and 51 more between 2023 and 2026. Private schools are moving in the other direction. Private enrollment grew from 81,220 students in 2021 to 93,755 this year, an increase of 12,535.

Education Minister Leonardo Sánchez Hernández attributes the public decline mainly to the shrinking number of children in Costa Rica. He estimates that families switching to private schools account for no more than 7% of the drop.

Citing figures from the National Institute of Statistics and Census (INEC), the minister said the fertility rate fell from 1.78 to 1.12 children per woman between 2014 and 2024, and the crude birth rate dropped 23% between 2020 and 2025. Sánchez also pointed to post-pandemic adjustments in enrollment records, migration and students leaving school altogether. Ministry figures count 9,662 students who have dropped out of the education system this year.

Researchers and private school representatives offer additional explanations for the private sector’s growth. Dagoberto Murillo Delgado, a researcher with the State of Education report, said smaller families may have more money to spend on each child’s schooling, and higher-income households may be choosing private options.

Antonio Fernández Rojas, executive director of the private schools association ADEC, said the pandemic pushed some families to make the switch. Parents cite English instruction, stronger academics and smaller class sizes as reasons for the move. The trend is part of a wider demographic shift in which Costa Rica’s population could begin shrinking earlier than expected. With the ministry projecting tens of thousands fewer students each year, the pressure on the public school network is set to continue.

World.title: Jamie Young’s murder trial delayed again, rescheduled for Friday
World.content:
Jamie Young’s murder trial delayed again, rescheduled for Friday

By Breaking Belize News Staff: The murder trial of Jamie Caesar Young, accused of fatally shooting his former girlfriend’s new partner during a high-speed pursuit along the Philip Goldson Highway in 2024, has been postponed yet again.

Young was scheduled to stand trial before High Court Justice Candace Nanton on Thursday, October 15, but the proceedings could not begin due to unforeseen circumstances. The matter was adjourned to Friday, October 16, at 9:00 a.m.

Young, who is represented by attorney Dr. Lynden Jones, is charged with the March 16, 2024 murder of 30-year-old former Belize Defence Force soldier and bus driver Damion Dominique Baptist of Burrell Boom.

According to police, Baptist was travelling with Young’s former girlfriend when Young allegedly pursued them in a grey pickup truck along the highway near Ladyville.

Investigators allege that Young repeatedly pulled alongside their vehicle and fired shots, eventually striking Baptist in the head and causing him to lose control of his red Ford Fusion, which crashed into a lamppost near Our Lady of the Way RC School.

Baptist was transported to the Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital, where he was pronounced dead.

Young was subsequently arrested and charged with murder and aggravated assault against the woman.

The latest adjournment follows an earlier postponement on October 5, when the trial could not proceed because Young’s attorney was reportedly ill. BBN previously reported on that delay.

The case is now expected to proceed on Friday morning.

World.title: Belize City teen takes rap and gets 2 years in jail for unlicensed Glock 17 so his sister can go free
World.content:
Belize City teen takes rap and gets 2 years in jail for unlicensed Glock 17 so his sister can go free

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 19-year-old Belize City man who pleaded guilty to possessing an unlicensed Glock pistol, resulting in the withdrawal of a firearm charge against his older sister, has been sentenced to two years in prison.

Aaron Ayren Pitter, of Pitter Street, was sentenced on Thursday, October 15, before a Magistrate in Court #5 at the Belize City Magistrate’s Court. His sentence was ordered to take effect from August 18, 2026, the date he pleaded guilty.

The conviction stems from a police search conducted on August 17 at a residence on Pitter Street, where officers from the Violence Prevention and Enforcement Team discovered a Glock 17 Gen 4 9mm pistol wrapped inside a pair of blue short pants hidden in a hole beside a bathtub.

The firearm was fitted with a black magazine and red extension, but police confirmed that the gun and magazine contained no ammunition.

According to police, Pitter arrived home while officers were conducting the search and admitted that the firearm belonged to him, telling officers, “Da feh me, big man. I have knowledge that was there.”

Pitter and his 20-year-old sister, Gregoria Veronica Pitter, were initially jointly charged with keeping a firearm without a gun licence. However, after Aaron accepted responsibility and pleaded guilty, prosecutors withdrew the charge against his sister, allowing her to walk free.

As previously reported by Breaking Belize News, the Magistrate initially encouraged Pitter to seek legal advice before accepting his guilty plea, but the teenager insisted on taking responsibility for the weapon so his sister could go free.

During Thursday’s sentencing, Pitter offered no mitigation. Although he had initially faced a possible five-year prison term, the Magistrate imposed a two-year sentence, retroactive to August 18.

World.title: “I just want to be your mother-in-law”: Daughter-in-law drops harm charge against ‘ma-lee’
World.content:
“I just want to be your mother-in-law”: Daughter-in-law drops harm charge against ‘ma-lee’

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A Belize City woman who was arrested on a bench warrant after repeatedly missing court appearances has been spared further legal trouble after her daughter-in-law, who accused her of causing harm more than two years ago, asked the court to withdraw the charge.

Angela Copious appeared before a Senior Magistrate in Court #2 on Wednesday, October 14, after being detained over the holiday weekend for failing to attend previous court hearings.

Copious was charged with causing harm to her daughter-in-law following an alleged altercation on July 26, 2024.

In court, Copious explained that she had been seriously ill and claimed her daughter had emailed medical documents to explain her absences. However, the court had no record of receiving those documents.

The matter took an unexpected turn when the daughter-in-law appeared and informed the Magistrate that she had forgiven her mother-in-law and no longer wished to pursue the case. She requested that the charge be withdrawn so both women could move on with their lives.

Faber also asked that they be bound over to keep the peace, but the Magistrate did not impose such an order.

With the charge withdrawn and her bail not revoked, Copious was allowed to leave court.

Before departing, a relieved Copious turned to her daughter-in-law and told her, “I just want to be your mother-in-law.”

The emotional exchange brought an end to a criminal complaint that had been pending since July 2024.

World.title: Belize participates in U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State
World.content:
Belize participates in U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State

By Zoila Palma: Today, Oscar Arnold, Chief Executive Officer for Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, is participating in the U.S.-Caribbean Dialogue, hosted by U.S. Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau.

The Ministry says that the high-level dialogue provides an important platform to strengthen regional partnerships and advance shared priorities in security and defense coordination, strategic economic growth, disaster response, and regional health cooperation.

CEO Arnold is joined by the Ambassador of Belize to the U.S., Nestor Mendez, and Counsellor, Alexya Perez.

“Belize remains committed to constructive engagement and regional collaboration with the Caribbean and its partners,” the Ministry said.

World.title: Belize City man fined $55 for riding bicycle up-stop on his own street
World.content:
Belize City man fined $55 for riding bicycle up-stop on his own street

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 26-year-old Belize City man found himself in trouble with the law after police caught him riding his bicycle against the flow of traffic on the very street where he lives.

Jermaine Lewis, a resident of King Street, was detained on Saturday, October 10, 2026, after police observed him riding his bicycle in the wrong direction along the one-way street.

Lewis was escorted to the nearby Precinct 1 Police Station, also located on King Street, where he was charged with causing a bicycle to proceed up a one-way street.

He appeared before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Tuesday, October 13, and pleaded guilty to the traffic offence.

The Magistrate imposed a fine of $50 plus $5 court costs, giving Lewis until November 30, 2026, to pay or face one week in prison.

Riding a bicycle against the designated flow of traffic is an offence under Belize’s traffic laws, and similar violations have resulted in fines and, in some cases, imprisonment for unpaid penalties.

World.title: International News: Strong El Niño raises global concerns over wildfires, food security and power shortages
World.content:
International News: Strong El Niño raises global concerns over wildfires, food security and power shortages

By Zoila Palma: An exceptionally strong El Niño weather cycle is contributing to drought, wildfires, power shortages and growing food security concerns in several parts of the world, with scientists warning that its effects could intensify as the phenomenon approaches its expected peak in December.

In Indonesia, prolonged dry conditions have contributed to fires in forests and plantations in Borneo and South Sumatra, triggering a regional haze crisis that has affected neighbouring Malaysia and Singapore.

Authorities and conservation groups have rescued dozens of orangutans from the fires. Meanwhile, Brazil’s Amazon region has also experienced widespread fires, with Amazonas state recording nearly four times as many fire hotspots in September as in the same month last year.

In Myanmar, authorities have warned of possible electricity outages as unusually high temperatures increase power demand, while the Philippines is preparing for higher energy consumption and potential declines in hydropower production. The impacts are also raising concerns about food security, with International Monetary Fund Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva expressing concern about the global consequences and saying the IMF is preparing to support countries that may struggle to cope.

The World Meteorological Organization has warned that El Niño is likely to bring above-average temperatures to much of the world and alter rainfall patterns, increasing the risk of droughts and floods.

World.title: Wrong And Strong: ‘Dads’, 61, fined $110 for riding bicycle up-stop and upstarting police
World.content:
Wrong And Strong: ‘Dads’, 61, fined $110 for riding bicycle up-stop and upstarting police

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A 61-year-old Belize City man who was caught riding his bicycle against traffic on a one-way street ended up facing two charges after allegedly refusing to cooperate with a police officer.

Jose Augustine August appeared unrepresented before the Belize City Magistrate’s Court on Wednesday, October 14, where he pleaded guilty to causing a bicycle to proceed against the designated direction of a one-way street and obstructing a police officer.

According to police, the incident occurred on Sunday, October 11, on Cemetery Road, where August was intercepted for riding his bicycle in the wrong direction. He subsequently obstructed a female corporal while she was executing her duties.

August admitted both offences and did not dispute the prosecution’s allegations. When given an opportunity to offer mitigating circumstances, he remained silent.

The Magistrate imposed a fine of $50 for each offence, along with $5 court costs on each charge, bringing his total penalty to $110.

August was given until November 30, 2026, to pay the fines or face one week in prison for each offence.

World.title: Charge dropped against man accused of going equipped to steal but remains behind bars
World.content:
Charge dropped against man accused of going equipped to steal but remains behind bars

By Breaking Belize News Staff: A man who has spent three months behind bars because he could not post bail received some good news in court on Wednesday, October 14, when prosecutors withdrew one of two criminal charges against him.

Wilfred Dixon, 39, was initially charged with going equipped to commit burglary or theft and handling stolen goods after police allegedly found him with a tool kit containing a grinder in Hattieville on July 13, 2026.

During his latest appearance at the Belize City Magistrate’s Court, a police prosecutor informed the court that the prosecution was withdrawing the charge of going equipped and would proceed to trial solely on the handling stolen goods charge.

Dixon, who remains unrepresented, was provided with eight pages of disclosure and three photographs. He disputed part of a witness statement alleging that he was seen throwing an object.

According to previous BBN reporting, police allegedly spotted Dixon carrying the tool kit in a yard near Locario Street in Hattieville around 4:50 a.m. When approached, he reportedly fled and later discarded the kit near Mile 16 on the George Price Highway.

At his initial arraignment, Dixon denied wrongdoing, telling the court, “I nuh guilty because I nuh thief it. I found it dah Sibun.”

Although he was granted bail of $800 plus one surety, Dixon has remained at the Belize Central Prison because he has been unable to secure someone to sign his bail.

His trial for handling stolen goods is scheduled for November 13, 2026.

After 50 years on the market, the delicious, creamy drink that ‘boosts you up’ is a household name in Jamaica.

World.title: Prison officials deny reported fight between P Diddy and Dudus
World.content:
American rapper P Diddy and Jamaican drug lord Christopher 'Dudus' Coke a

Prison officials are reportedly denying a reported physical altercation between American music mogul Sean ‘Diddy’ Combs and convicted Jamaican drug lord Christopher ‘Dudus’ Coke, which resulted in the rapper being rushed to hospital on Wednesday.

A TMZ report on Wednesday said the confrontation reportedly erupted after Combs allegedly caused trouble that resulted in disciplinary action against fellow inmates. The Bad Boy for Life singer reportedly sustained a head injury and was subsequently transported to an outside medical facility for treatment.

But the Federal Bureau of Prisons is denying that the fight took place.

“While, for privacy, safety, and security reasons, we do not comment on the conditions of confinement for any individual in our custody, we can tell you that the story you are referring to is false and did not happen. Sean Combs is in the custody of the Federal Bureau of Prisons and is incarcerated at the Federal Correctional Institution Fort Dix. Beyond this, we have no additional information to provide,” a spokesman for the Federal Bureau of Prisons was quoted as saying in a statement to The Daily Mail.

Combs was sentenced last year to just over four years in federal prison after being convicted on prostitution-related charges involving two of his former girlfriends.
