World.title: US dollar exchange rate slightly rises against Iraqi dinar
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate for the US dollar against the Iraqi dinar experienced a slight increase on Thursday in both Baghdad, the Iraqi capital, and Erbil, the capital of the Kurdistan region of Iraq.

The US dollar exchange rate rose in Baghdad’s al-Kifah and al-Harithiya stock exchanges, reaching 1,665.5 Iraqi dinars compared to 1,665 Iraqi dinars on Thursday morning.

The exchange rate in currency exchange shops in Baghdad ranged between 1,670 Iraqi dinars and 1,660 Iraqi dinars, Shafaq News reported.

In Erbil, the US dollar exchange rate also increased, fluctuating between 1,664 and 1,663 Iraqi dinars.

US dollar exchange rates rose noticeably in the Baghdad and Erbil markets on October 7, following the cabinet’s decision to revalue the official rate of the local currency, causing turbulence and instability in the parallel market.

Iraq officially depreciated its national currency, with the baseline dropping from about 1,300 Iraqi dinars to 1,500 dinars per US dollar.

The Iraqi cabinet approved the structural adjustment, which marks a 14.5 percent decline compared to the previous official framework that had been in place since early 2023.

Following the announcement, parallel market rates in Baghdad and Erbil soared, with exchange shops reporting market gains of more than 1,700 Iraqi dinars per US dollar.

World.title: Infantino offers apology but ‘no answers’ at FIFA meeting over World Cup plan
World.content:
Zurich – FIFA president Gianni Infantino gave “no satisfactory answers” when grilled Thursday during a meeting to discuss his attempts to sell stakes in the World Cup to private investors, senior members of football’s global governing body said, but he did offer an apology for the failed project.

“We asked a great many critical questions, but there were no satisfactory answers from my point of view,” said Bernd Neuendorf, the head of the German Football Association (DFB), who is also a member of the FIFA Council.

Neuendorf was speaking after the Council met behind closed doors at the body’s Zurich headquarters, where Infantino’s FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal was one of the main topics on the agenda.

Infantino has been under severe pressure since his announcement in late July that he wanted to open FIFA’s premium competitions such as the World Cup to private investors.

That plan was ultimately abandoned in the face of widespread criticism, with a rebellion led by European governing body UEFA, the Asian Football Confederation (AFC) and CONCACAF, which runs the sport in North and Central America and the Caribbean.

“I think we had the opportunity to say what we felt, and we spoke a lot about the issues,” Debbie Hewitt, the chair of the English Football Association who is also a FIFA vice-president, told reporters, before adding that Infantino had said sorry.

“I think it is fair to say Gianni apologised at the beginning for what had happened, and he said that with some contrition, and then there were no holds barred in terms of what we felt about what happened.”

Hewitt and Neuendorf are among the 36 members of the FIFA Council, along with Infantino.

Infantino has headed FIFA since 2016 and is running for re-election next March, despite calls for him to stand down in the wake of the FFE plan.

For the moment, no heavyweight candidate has put themselves forward to run against him.

“We were asked to submit our questions” in relation to the plan which was not put to the FIFA Council before the July announcement, Hewitt said.

“One of the disappointing things was we didn’t get answers. We didn’t get answers to anything we had specifically requested, for example getting the papers from FFE, and so we asked the question why and why not.”

– ‘Nothing has shifted’ –

Many leading European national associations have withdrawn their support for Infantino in the upcoming election because of the uproar caused by FFE and other controversies, including his relationship with US president Donald Trump.

Chief among those were Infantino’s decision to create a FIFA Peace Prize and award it to Trump at last December’s World Cup draw, and the decision to suspend a ban for United States striker Folarin Balogun following a red card during the World Cup after Trump intervened directly by phoning Infantino.

“I speak for myself as a Council member — from my position nothing has shifted,” Hewitt added. “I have no new information that makes me feel any differently to how I felt when I went in, other than we do have a president of FIFA who is apologetic about what has happened, and secondly a promise again that we will get the information that we have requested.”

FIFA was expected to put forward a plan at the Council meeting to set up a $6.35-billion development fund for the next four years.

To finance the development fund, which would allow money to be distributed to FIFA’s 211 federations as well as to the regional confederations, it would draw in part on its financial reserves after a commercially successful 2026 World Cup.

The plan would allow for the payment of $25 million to all 211 member federations.

Infantino may hope the latest plan reinforces his position ahead of the election.

The deadline for submitting candidacies is November 18.

World.title: Air routes between Iraq, Kuwait officially reopened
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Air routes between Iraq and Kuwait officially reopened on Thursday following a temporary suspension due to security developments in the region.

The flight corridors resumed operations at 2:00 p.m. Baghdad time, reversing a temporary suspension triggered by regional security developments and escalating geopolitical tensions.

The return of aviation travel is being closely monitored to guarantee civilian flight safety in a challenging regional climate.

The International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) oversees the new operating arrangements. Iraq, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates all participated in technical discussions and official clearances.

Aircraft must follow specific flight patterns and maintain predetermined heights. This enables regional air traffic controllers to maintain close coordination and ensure safe separation of airplanes.

The Iraqi Ministry of Transport mentioned in a statement that the system will be implemented gradually, with the participating Gulf States constantly monitoring operations to respond fast to any unexpected technical or operational issues.

The prolonged conflict in the Middle East has caused significant disruptions to aviation networks across the region.

Before the arrangement, the framework supported by the ICAO was not yet operational, but it is now helping to restore essential transit paths. However, regional aviation authorities are still closely monitoring real-time security risks.

World.title: Three dead as Istanbul sees heaviest rainfall in 80 years
World.content:
Istanbul – Istanbul was battling on Thursday to recover from flooding caused by what officials described as the heaviest rainfall in at least 80 years, as the toll rose to three dead and five missing.

The rain began lashing Turkey’s largest city in earnest on Wednesday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters.

“We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942,” Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.

The death toll from the floods rose to three when authorities found a man’s body near a park in the Kagithane area on the European side, Gul’s office said in a statement.

The storm also claimed the life of a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said.

Five others were missing, officials said.

In Beykoz, on Istanbul’s Asian side, DHA news agency said another man had died after falling into a well while trying to drain the water at a school construction site.

There was no immediate official confirmation of his death.

– Dramatic images –

Istanbul municipal teams and firefighters were carrying out cleanup operations at schools, football pitches, garages and other sites on Thursday, pumping water out of flooded areas and clearing mud, an AFP photographer reported.

On Wednesday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home “unless absolutely necessary” and advising those living in basement properties “to spend the night on safer, higher floors”.

Dramatic footage posted online late Wednesday and collated by DHA showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.

Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.

Power and water cuts have also hit areas of the city, notably in Sariyer where shopkeepers could be seen trying to salvage their goods from the mud, an AFP journalist said.

– Floods in other cities –

Heavy rainfall in the nearby province of Sakarya caused a two-storey villa on the banks of a stream to collapse in Sapanca neighbourhood. As the house had been evacuated earlier, no one was killed or injured.

And in the neighbouring Kocaeli province, a stream overflowed in Gebze district, sweeping away a driver who was later rescued by emergency workers with ropes. In another district, Basiskele, one man was missing after being carried away by floodwaters, reports said.

Forty-three flights bound for Istanbul Airport had to be diverted Wednesday, as did three flights heading for Sabiha Gokcen on the Asian side, which temporarily suspended take-offs due to strong winds, the transport ministry said.

Turkey’s AFAD disaster agency has set up a crisis desk to manage incidents caused by the heavy rainfall, which by nightfall Wednesday had risen to 1,277 flooding incidents, 15 landslides, 47 people stranded and two roofs blown off.

The heavy rains are expected to continue over the weekend.

World.title: Italian football suffers new blow with Champions League misery
World.content:
Rome – Still reeling from the national team’s failure to qualify for a third consecutive World Cup, Italian football hit a new low this week when for the first time all four Serie A teams competing in the Champions League suffered defeats.

Roma collapsed against Real Madrid at the Stadio Olimpico, conceding three goals in the final seven minutes to lose 4–3 on Wednesday.

“We went from a moment of great euphoria to deep disappointment,” bemoaned Roma coach Gian Piero Gasperini.

In their first Champions League home match since 2018, Roma let a famous win slip from their grasp despite leading 3-1.

Inter Milan, runners-up in 2023 and 2025, fell to the most surprising loss for the Italian quartet, stunned by a hat-trick from Italian-German sensation Nicolo Tresoldi in a 4-3 defeat by Club Brugge at the San Siro.

In their first-ever Champions League away match, ambitious Como took an early lead in Rotterdam only to ultimately go down 3–2 to Feyenoord.

A similar fate befell Napoli, who scored first at Villarreal before losing their footing in Spain and being beaten 3-1.

With the exception of Inter, every Serie A team led at some point, yet none managed to hold onto their advantage.

Defending narrow leads was long considered a hallmark of Italian clubs, who have won 12 European Cups and reached 30 finals between them.

Seven-time champions AC Milan and two-time winners Juventus failed to qualify for the competition this season.

– ‘Forgotten how to defend’ –

“Have they forgotten how to defend in Italian football?” asked former Milan and Real Madrid coach Fabio Capello.

With the notable exception of 15-time European champions Real Madrid, the Serie A teams’ conquerors on matchday two of the league phase were relatively modest opposition.

“Knowing how to defend has almost become something to be ashamed of,” said Napoli coach Massimiliano Allegri.

“In the Champions League, opponents make very few mistakes. You have to be patient and stay focused on the ball. All these goals conceded clearly show that much greater attention is required defensively.”

The recent European record of reigning Italian champions Inter has been disastrous, losing seven of their last eight Champions League matches.

Debate regarding the standard of the Italian top flight has reignited.

Serie A clubs spent heavily in the close season, but their financial might is still dwarfed by that of England’s Premier League giants and Champions League holders Paris Saint-Germain.

Compared to the golden days of the 1990s, when Italian clubs regularly broke the world-record transfer fee, the country struggles to attract the best players from abroad.

None of the four Serie A sides who competed in the Champions League last season, Inter Milan, Napoli, Juventus and Atalanta, made it past the last 16.

That was the fourth time in six seasons Italy was not represented in the quarter-finals, after a run of having at least one team in the last eight in 15 of the previous 18 years.

The national team failed to reach the World Cup earlier this year, losing a qualifying play-off to Bosnia and Herzegovina as the four-time world champions missed out for a third straight edition.

The Azzurri have not even played a World Cup knockout match since beating France in the 2006 final on penalties.

Since the return of Roberto Mancini as coach in August, Italy have shown signs of a resurgence, holding France to a 1-1 draw at the Stade de France on October 2 and posting two Nations League wins over Turkey.

But in the Champions League, the four Italian clubs have mustered just four points — three for Cesc Fabregas’s Como and one for Roma — and are languishing towards the bottom of the standings.

Real Madrid coach Jose Mourinho, however, does not share the prevailing Italian pessimism, despite leading his side to wins over his former club Inter and Roma in recent weeks.

“Both Inter and Roma are truly at a very high level,” insisted Mourinho, the last coach to win the European Cup for a Serie A team with Inter in 2010.

Inter, Roma, Napoli and Como all have winnable home Champions League matches as they look to bounce back next week, against Shakhtar Donetsk, Slovan Bratislava, Bodo/Glimt and a floundering Manchester United respectively.

World.title: US producer prices see biggest jump since 2022 in added challenge to Trump
World.content:
Washington – US wholesale inflation surged past analysts’ expectations in September, marking its biggest jump since 2022 as the war in Iran sent fuel prices rocketing, government data showed Thursday.

The latest numbers, coming a day after hotter-than-anticipated consumer inflation, underscore the challenges that President Donald Trump faces in cooling prices and winning over cost-weary voters in November’s midterm elections.

The Producer Price Index was up 6.3 percent from a year ago last month, according to the Labor Department, significantly above the 5.5 percent expected in a forecast published by MarketWatch.

The acceleration from August was also the biggest year-on-year jump since December 2022, the department said.

On a month-on-month basis, PPI rose by 1.3 percent, the widest advance since March 2022. This was similarly a sharp increase from the 0.5 percent rate in August.

Half of the September uptick for goods costs can be “traced to prices for gasoline, which jumped 20.3 percent,” the report said.

“The indexes for diesel fuel, fresh and dry vegetables, jet fuel, residential electric power, and crude petroleum also rose,” it added.

A day prior, government data showed that the consumer price index — a key gauge of inflation — climbed more than expected to 3.7 percent in September.

While price increases may not lock in a second consecutive interest rate hike this month by the US central bank, the odds of higher rates to tamp down inflation have climbed.

With a second straight day of “higher-than-expected inflation numbers, it seems the Fed will have no choice but to raise rates again this year,” said Chris Zaccarelli, chief investment officer of Northlight Asset Management.

– Consumers losing steam? –

Even though US consumer spending appears to be holding up, analysts expect household behavior to reflect the growing pinch from rising costs.

A separate Commerce Department report showed Thursday that retail sales grew by 0.8 percent month-on-month in September to $745.0 billion. This was slower than the 1.3 percent pace in August.

The numbers, adjusted for seasonal changes but not inflation, likely reflect the sharp price hikes in energy costs too.

“That headline figure doesn’t tell us much about the health of the consumer, as it was almost entirely driven by a price-related jump in gasoline spending,” said Michael Pearce of Oxford Economics.

He expects consumers will lose steam heading into the year-end holiday shopping season, bogged down by higher prices.

Sales continued to rise at restaurants and bars, by 1.1 percent, likely due to spending by higher-income households, Pearce said.

Sales sharply rose at gasoline stations by 6.4 percent.

Excluding gasoline stations, however, retail sales rose a tepid 0.2 percent.

“The moderation in core retail sales, along with a sharp pullback in auto sales, suggests that real consumer spending was likely flat in September,” Nationwide chief economist Kathy Bostjancic warned in a note.

Stripping out auto sales and that at gasoline stations, overall retail sales was also just up by 0.2 percent from the prior month.

“The key to sustaining resilient spending will be the health of the labor and equity markets. If the unemployment rate remains low, meaning consumers have a job, they will continue to spend, even if more cautiously,” Bostjancic said.

World.title: Ukraine’s Zelensky defies Trump with Russian refinery strikes
World.content:
Kyiv – Ukraine will no longer abide by US President Donald Trump’s demands not to strike Russian oil refineries, President Volodymyr Zelensky said in remarks published Thursday, amid deepening tensions between the two leaders over a US-Russia diesel agreement.

Relations between Kyiv and Washington have soured since last week, when Trump eased sanctions on Russia in exchange for Moscow releasing large amounts of diesel onto global markets.

Zelensky described the deal as a “weak decision”, saying it would encourage Russia to prolong its four-and-a-half-year war with Ukraine, while several of Ukraine’s European allies criticised the agreement.

Addressing the criticism on Saturday, Trump claimed Ukrainian attacks on Russian oil refineries were to blame for rising diesel prices and said it was “time for Ukraine to get a new president”.

“The block (on attacking refineries) is out,” Zelensky told the Financial Times in an interview published on Thursday. “We’re done.”

Trump had announced on Sunday a surprise “energy ceasefire” between Russia and Ukraine, which Zelensky said he knew nothing about.

And earlier this week, Ukraine reported disruptions to a critical US satellite communications system that its army uses on the battlefield.

“We need HONESTY from our partners about this war,” Zelensky wrote on social media on Thursday.

In an interview with British journalist Piers Morgan on Wednesday, Zelensky agreed that he felt “betrayed” by Trump’s diesel-supply deal with Russia’s Vladimir Putin.

He also questioned the advice that Trump was receiving, after senior Ukrainian officials in Kyiv openly accused the United States of helping Russia.

“It’s painful when President Trump chooses one side, not our side,” he said.

“I think his advisors are wrong… This is not (the) right side of history.”

Since launching a full-scale invasion of its neighbour in 2022, Russia has systematically hit Ukrainian energy infrastructure, leading to energy and heating shortages — while Ukraine has hit back at Russian oil refineries it says fund the war.

More recently, Trump’s war in Iran has led to oil shortages and ensuing price spikes, creating major headwinds for his Republican Party ahead of midterm elections early next month.

– Satellite row –

The Kremlin accused Ukraine on Thursday of derailing US peace efforts by resuming its strikes.

Russia on Thursday reported that an oil refinery in Ryazan, south of the capital, Moscow, had been hit in a “large-scale attack”.

Kyiv “continues to launch strikes against these facilities,” Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told reporters.

“It is coming into serious conflict with the peace efforts of the United States and American negotiators, who are making vigorous efforts to initiate the peace process,” he added.

Much of the outrage in Ukraine this week has been over restrictions to the Starshield satellite communications system that its military relies upon to detect incoming Russian attacks and to coordinate its frontline response.

Defence officials confirmed that the United States had threatened to withdraw intelligence-sharing if Ukraine continued long-range strikes on Russian oil refineries.

Powerful ballistic missiles struck Kyiv and the surrounding region on Tuesday and Wednesday night, before air raid sirens could sound warning people to take cover.

But tech billionaire Elon Musk, who has also called for Zelensky to be replaced as leader, said his SpaceX company was not behind any disruption to the Starshield system.

“Starshield systems are owned and controlled by the US government,” he said.

“Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS,” he added, referring to Trump.

Ukraine uses the Starshield system from Musk’s SpaceX for battlefield communications, mid-range strikes on Russian-occupied territory and interceptor drones.

It is separate from the parallel Starlink civilian satellite system, which Ukraine also uses but not for offensive operations.

Speeds were slower on Wednesday, affecting connectivity, officials said.

Russia has intensified its bombardment of Ukraine and its capital in recent months, leading to mounting civilian casualties and disrupting daily life for citizens.

Moscow currently occupies around a fifth of Ukraine, including Crimea, which it annexed in 2014.

World.title: BP to help Iraq produce 450,000 barrels per day from Kirkuk oilfields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The development plan for four oilfields in northern Iraq has entered a new phase, a move aiming to support Baghdad’s efforts to increase oil production capacity to 10 million barrels per day over the coming years.

The Iraqi Ministry of Oil announced on Thursday that operations for four major oilfields in the northern province of Kirkuk have been transferred to a joint operating body. This initiative aims to consolidate efforts to develop oil and gas assets and to enhance the efficiency of the country’s resources.

Iraqi Minister of Oil Basim Khudair oversaw the transfer of the management of the Kirkuk oilfields from the North Oil Company and the North Gas Company to a joint operating entity. The action is part of the government’s strategy to enhance the nation’s resources and optimize the performance of its production sectors.

These developments are bolstered by British Petroleum’s (BP) participation in a project to develop four oilfields in Iraq, a move that aligns with larger attempts to broaden the base of foreign partners.

The development plan intends to achieve a significant increase in oil and gas output in the next few years.

Khudair highlighted that the transition of operations to the joint operating entity represents a significant milestone in the initiative to develop the four Kirkuk oilfields.

The plan aims to reach an oil production level of 450,000 barrels per day, in addition to 500 million standard cubic feet of gas per day, according to Khudair.

The four oilfields—Kirkuk, Bai Hassan, Jambur, and Khabbaz—are key oil assets in northern Iraq and represent an important part of the government’s plans to increase production.

In 2025, BP reached a deal with Iraq’s North Oil Company to develop oil fields in the northern Iraqi province of Kirkuk, with investments projected to reach $25 billion.

Khudair affirmed that BP is a strategic partner in the oil and gas sectors. He noted that working together as a team will support the project’s implementation and help address any obstacles that may arise during the development phases.

The development plan for the Kirkuk fields includes training Iraqi workers, transferring expertise and technology, and implementing community-focused initiatives, such as building service facilities for the local population.

World.title: HC bars fuel-run boats on Dal Lake, pushes for cleaner alternatives
World.content:
SRINAGAR: J&K high court directed authorities Thursday to ensure no fuel-powered motorboats, including motorised shikaras and jet skis, operate on Srinagarâs Dal Lake in a move that would halt 166 such vessels.

The HC cited growing pollution for the curbs -- which came in the middle of the tourist season -- and directed govt to explore whether fuel-powered boats could be replaced with solar-powered or battery-run alternatives.

âThis court is convinced that in modern times, when lake systems have become a growing concern for civilisation, steps are being taken to exclude activities which would cause pollution. It would be also important that whatever policy is framed is more reasonable while balancing tourism activities, pollution, as well as uniformity between the players involved,â a division bench of Chief Justice Pushpendra Singh Bhati and Justice Rajesh Sekhri said.

The bench made it clear that the restrictions would apply with immediate effect. âIn case any motorised boat is allowed to ply, it shall be held as contempt of todayâs order,â the HC said.

Fuel boats used by the administration for emergency services, law and order, disaster management and rescue operations will be exempted from the order, the HC said. This came after additional advocate-general (AAG) Mohsin Qadri, appearing for govt, argued that such boats be spared.





The order came on a batch of petitions by some owners of fuel-run boats who had moved the HC against the transport departmentâs failure to renew their licences. They argued that the delay violated their fundamental rights to life and livelihood. During the hearing, AAG Qadri conceded that pollution was a problem and called for a balance between tourism and cleanliness of the lake. Qadri also highlighted Dalâs civilisational importance for J&K.

World.title: PM Modi to visit Canada on December 11-12 as India, Ottawa push to boost ties
World.content:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will visit Canada on December 11-12, the High Commission of India in Ottawa announced on Friday, as both countries seek to strengthen bilateral ties and advance cooperation across key sectors.

The announcement followed a telephone conversation between PM Modi and Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney, during which the two leaders agreed to build on the recent positive momentum in relations and pursue concrete outcomes in trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people exchanges.

In a post on X, the Indian High Commission said, "Honâble PM Shri Narendra Modi will visit Canada on 11â12 December 2026."

It added, "In the recent conversation with Rt. Hon. PM Mark Carney, both the leaders agreed to build on the positive momentum in ties and work towards concrete outcomes in trade, energy, technology, security and people-to-people ties."

During their conversation on Tuesday, PM Modi described the exchange as warm and productive, reiterating the importance of strengthening the India-Canada strategic partnership.

World.title: SC's quota ruling hits opposition's 'appeasement politics': BJP
World.content:
BJPâsGaurav Bhatialauded the âlandmarkâ ruling

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: BJP Thursday said the SC judgement holding that quota benefits cannot be claimed by converts was "historic", adding it is a "massive blow to the appeasement politics" of Congress and other opposition parties which have sought to provide reservation to Muslims on the basis of religion.While upholding the Madras HC order that a person converting to Islam can't claim reservation under backward class category solely on the basis of conversion, SC also held that a person who professes a religion other than Hinduism, Sikhism or Buddhism cannot be considered a member of Scheduled Castes (SC).BJP's Gaurav Bhatia lauded the "landmark" ruling, which is a boost to the party's long-held position that Muslims and Christians cannot claim rights accorded to Dalits because of their SC family background and that OBC reservation cannot be provided on the ground of religion."The appeasement politics of 'Congress Jinnah Party' has got a massive blow after the judgement was delivered," he said, noting that Congress govts have tried to give backward quota reservation to Muslims. TMC had done the same in Bengal and SP also advocated a similar quota, he added.

World.title: ‘Harassment’ of journos: SC seeks reply of police
World.content:

on a PIL by NGO âNetwork of Women in Mediaâ seeking an independent probe, headed by a retired woman judge, into alleged incidents of sexual harassment of women journalists when they were covering the Oct 10 protests.

Such harassment of woman journalists, who form a class by themselves and must be protected while discharging their professional duties, must stop, she said.

Jaising opposed and asked how police, which is accused of molesting a woman journalist, would investigate its officer. It must be handed over to an independent inquiry panel headed by a retired woman judge and comprising a retired woman IPS officer and eminent women representatives from civil society and NGOs.

World.title: If every citizen becomes a journalist, it will create problems for all, says SC
World.content:
"Will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist" the court said.

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday said it will be problematic if every citizen becomes a journalist as PILs sought protection of the right to freedom of expression of freelancers, independent journalists and reel-makers who descend in large numbers at protest venues already teeming with hordes of accredited reporters from registered media houses.Senior advocate Indira Jaising complained to a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justice Joymalya Bagchi that Delhi Police did not recognise independent and freelance journalists covering the protests and insisted on Press Information Bureau (PIB) accreditation. She said there must be a national protocol for police not to obstruct the professional work of any journalist who has an identity card from the employer.CJI Kant, however, struck a note of caution. âWe must also keep one thing in mind. If everyone starts becoming a journalist, it will create problems for every other person,â he said. Justice Bagchi said, âIt will require a detailed examination whether the right to freedom of expression will empower every citizen of this country to be a journalist. That is difficult. There are layers of protection for accredited journalists, those employed in registered media houses or whether they are freelance journalists, influencers or reel-makers.âCJI Kant said, âThe issue requires detailed examination â whether there should be a certain category of journalists to whom extra level of protection should be given.â Justice Bagchi added, âThe Working Journalists Act makes classes among journalists. We must examine all that.âSolicitor general Tushar Mehta said in the present era of digital technology, any person with a mobile phone could claim to be an independent or freelance journalist when he/she would, in fact, be only making reels to garner popularity on social media to earn money by either presenting one-sided stories or sensationalising incidents.Mehta supported the contention that women journalists should not be harrassed, but argued that the same consideration should be extended to women police personnel as well.

Virtually inaugurating five development projects covering airport infrastructure and strategic road connectivity in Ladakh worth around 3,350 crore, Modi said govt aims to develop modern infrastructure in the region while taking full care of the local environment.

Prioritising the educational empowerment of the younger generation so they do not have to migrate to other cities, PM highlighted the construction of a major centre of excellence in Leh alongside advancing proposals for satellite campuses of IIT Jammu and IIM Jammu.

"Our special focus is on the new generation of Ladakh. The youth of Ladakh will now be able to get better opportunities for higher education, research, and new skills right in their own region," he said.

World.title: NIA court declares Rajouri man ‘proclaimed offender’; orders encounter-site phone data be sealed
World.content:
JAMMU: In separate orders in two terror-related cases, a special NIA court in Jammu has declared a Rajouri native allegedly living in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir a âproclaimed offenderâ for repeatedly failing to appear before the court, while directing that forensic data extracted from a cellphone recovered at an encounter site be kept confidential and treated as âprotected materialâ.

Special Judge Prem Sagar passed the orders in separate proceedings on Wednesday.

In the first case, the court declared Mushtaq Ahmed Mir, a native of Thanamang village in Rajouriâs Darhal tehsil, a proclaimed offender under BNSS Section 84. According to a report submitted by Darhal SHO, Mir allegedly crossed the Line of Control in 1995-96, joined terrorism and subsequently took shelter in PoK. A non-bailable warrant issued against him remained unexecuted.

The court had issued a proclamation on July 20, 2026, directing Mir to appear. Despite publication in national and local English-language newspapers on Aug 13, he neither appeared nor surrendered. Observing that Mir was allegedly evading the legal process and that his arrest was not imminent, the court ordered that its proclamation order be sent to Govt Ranbir Press, Jammu, for publication in the Official Gazette.

World.title: Congress questions MEA’s silence on proposed Rubio-Jaishankar meeting
World.content:
The Congress on Thursday (October 15, 2026) asked why the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) was “silent” about a proposed meeting between the U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, in Mumbai.

It was not surprising that the U.S. Ambassador to India, Sergio Gor, had provided more details on Mr. Rubio’s forthcoming visit to Mumbai, Congress general secretary (communications) Jairam Ramesh said.

“It is also not wholly surprising to hear him say that Mr. Rubio will meet Government of India officials in Mumbai. But what is quite extraordinary is his statement that ‘we expect the Minister Dr. Jaishankar to be joining us there along with other individuals’,” Mr. Ramesh said.

“Since when has the announcement of India’s Minister of External Affairs’s meetings within India been outsourced to somebody other than the official spokesperson of the MEA?” he added.

The Congress’s dig at the government followed remarks by Mr. Gor during an interactive session at the Bloomberg New Economy Forum here, where he said Mr. Rubio would meet Indian government officials in Mumbai.

“We expect that Minister Dr. S Jaishankar will be there along with other individuals from Delhi, who will make a trip up there to see him in Mumbai,” Mr. Gor.

It is not surprising that the US Ambassador to India has just given more details on US Secretary of State Marco Rubio's forthcoming visit to Mumbai. It is also not wholly surprising to hear him say that Mr. Rubio will be meeting Govt of India officials in Mumbai. But what is quite extraordinary is his statement that "we expect the Minister Dr. Jaishankar to be joining us there along with other individuals". Since when has the announcement of India's Minister of External Affairs meetings within India been outsourced to somebody other than official spokesperson of the MEA? India gets to know from the US Ambassador just as it first got to know from Mr. Rubio himself on the evening of May 10, 2025 that Operation Sindoor had been halted. Why is the MEA silent on the External Affairs Minister's tryst with Mr. Rubio in Mumbai? — Jairam Ramesh (@Jairam_Ramesh) October 15, 2026

“India gets to know from the U.S. Ambassador just as it first got to know from Mr. Rubio himself on the evening of May 10, 2025 that Operation Sindoor had been halted. Why is the MEA silent on the External Affairs Minister’s tryst with Mr. Rubio in Mumbai?” Mr. Ramesh said.

Mr. Rubio will first visit Samarkand in Uzbekistan, before travelling to Mumbai, and Jamnagar in Gujarat, from October 17-22, 2026.

World.title: PAC grills Centre, States on ‘fraud markers’ flagged by CAG in SC scholarship schemes
World.content:
The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) of Parliament on Thursday (October 15, 2026) grilled the Union government and several State governments over their responses to gaps, including “fraud markers”, in the implementation of pre- and post- matric scholarships for Scheduled Caste students identified by the Comptroller and Auditor General of India.

The PAC, headed by Congress MP K.C. Venugopal, is likely to move privilege notices against the Chief Secretaries of six States who were supposed to appear before it on Thursday (October 15, 2026) to explain the gaps flagged in the 2025 CAG report but failed to do so, The Hindu has learnt. Further, with the Union government responding to the gaps by saying the implementation burden was on State and Union Territory administrations, the PAC has given the Union Social Justice and Empowerment Ministry one month’s time to submit a detailed action-taken report on each of the issues flagged by the CAG.

In its 2025 report, the CAG audit had flagged a plethora of issues related to the administration of the pre-matric and post-matric scholarships for SC students. These included 40.75 lakh beneficiaries from as many as 14 States receiving scholarships with delays ranging from one to 90 months; over 3.5 lakh beneficiaries not receiving their scholarships at all; over 5,700 cases of scholarships being disbursed without proper checks of income eligibility; over 6,000 cases of non-SC beneficiaries receiving the scholarships meant for SC students; and issues related to beneficiaries receiving double payments, short payments, and excess payments.

During the PAC hearing on Thursday (October 15, 2026), the Chief Secretaries of Uttar Pradesh, Karnataka, Punjab, Odisha, Bihar, and Madhya Pradesh were supposed to appear for briefing the Members; however, none of the States had deputed the respective officials, sources told The Hindu. Further, the committee Members questioned the Secretary, Social Justice and Empowerment, on why action-taken reports against each point highlighted in the CAG audit were not submitted.

The Social Justice Ministry is learnt to have told the committee that since the implementation of the scholarship schemes rests with the State governments, it was unable to file action-taken reports as the respective State governments had not shared them with the Union Ministry. Upon further questioning, the Union Ministry has assured that the reports will be submitted in a month’s time.

Both the pre-matric and post-matric scholarship schemes are Centrally sponsored schemes, with the Union government sharing the financial burden on a 60:40 ratio with State and UT governments (90:10 for northeastern States). From 2017-24, a total of 52,878 crore was spent on these two schemes, of which about ₹30,234.5 crore came as the Union government’s share.

The committee went on to ask the Union Ministry why the CAG audit had shown continuing instances of fraud markers (such as same caste certificates being used by multiple beneficiaries in Uttar Pradesh, students in Odisha receiving scholarships in seemingly common bank accounts, and over ₹13 crore being paid in Haryana to beneficiaries where Aadhaar and bank details were not matching) if Direct-Beneficiary Transfers alongside the Aadhaar Payment Bridge System were meant to weed out dummy beneficiaries, as stated by the Union government.

The committee also pointed out during the hearing that the shift to the DBT method had resulted in significant drops in the number of beneficiaries in both the pre-matric and post-matric scholarships for SC students. It noted that despite time for recovery, the 2025-26 figures for the post-matric scheme had reached only 36.07 lakh beneficiaries against a target of 76.55 lakh beneficiaries.

World.title: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh to represent India at upcoming SCO Heads of Government meeting
World.content:
Defence Minister Rajnath Singh will represent India at the upcoming two-day meeting of the Council of Heads of Government (Prime Ministers) of the Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 19 and 20, while Prime Minister Narendra Modi is expected to participate virtually, a senior government official said on Thursday (October 15, 2026).

The meeting will be held under Tajikistan’s SCO chairmanship for the year and is expected to focus on strengthening practical cooperation among member states, particularly in trade, investment, transport and logistics.

Ties with Tajikistan

The official said Mr. Singh would also hold a bilateral meeting with Tajikistan during the two-day visit. The discussions are expected to provide an opportunity to review bilateral ties and explore avenues for further cooperation.

The agenda of the SCO meeting is expected to cover trade and economic cooperation, investment, industrial collaboration, transport and logistics, the development of the creative and digital economy, innovation and financial interaction. Social, cultural and humanitarian cooperation will also figure in the deliberations.

The meeting will bring together heads of government and designated senior representatives of SCO member states to discuss regional cooperation and economic engagement.

Prime Minister Modi usually attends the meetings of the Council of Heads of State of SCO, as he did at the 26th meeting held in Bishkek, Kyrgyz Republic, from August 31 to September 1 earlier in the year.

Separately, China’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced on Thursday that Premier Li Qiang would visit Tajikistan from October 18 to 20 at the invitation of Tajik Prime Minister Kokhir Rasulzoda. Mr. Li will attend the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting during the visit.

Other member states, including Russia, Pakistan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan, Iran and Belarus, are expected to be represented by their heads of government or designated senior officials.

The SCO, which brings together countries across Eurasia, provides a platform for cooperation on regional security, economic development and cultural exchanges. The Council of Heads of Government is one of its key mechanisms for discussing economic and other areas of practical cooperation.

World.title: Morning Digest: ECI to hold summary revision of rolls in 17 States, UTs; India sourced more than two-thirds of its August oil imports from just three countries, and more
World.content:
Amid anti-SIR protests, ECI orders annual SSR to enrol voters in 17 States, UTs

Amid protests against the special intensive revision (SIR) and Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, the Election Commission of India (ECI) on Thursday announced the special summary revision (SSR) of electoral rolls in 17 States and Union Territories, including poll-bound Uttarakhand, Uttar Pradesh, and Punjab. The SSR seeks to enrol new voters and update electoral rolls.

No SoPs shared regarding auto-generated Form 7s with State Electoral Officers

With thousands of names deleted from electoral rolls during phases 2 and 3 of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) using auto-generated Form 7s digitally signed by Electoral Registration Officers (EROs), it has now emerged that this exercise is being carried out by State poll authorities without the Election Commission of India (ECI) issuing any written protocol or Standard Operating Procedure (SOP).

India sourced more than two-thirds of its August oil imports from just three countries

In a sign of increasing concentration of India’s oil supplies and its limited options to source from, latest data shows that more than two-thirds of the country’s oil imports came from just three countries — Russia, the U.S., and the UAE — marking a record high share.

Shooting at elementary school in Oregon leaves at least five dead

At least five people are believed to be dead following a shooting at an elementary school on Thursday in the U.S. city of Bend, Oregon, according to two law enforcement officials with knowledge of the case.

Anti-CEC protest: ‘Why is PM Modi shutting down Delhi to protect one man?’ asks CJP’s Dipke with Central Park shut ahead of ‘Tiranga’ march

Ahead of the Lehra Do Tiranga (Wave the Tricolour) demonstration called by youth organisations on Friday (October 16, 2026), the New Delhi Municipal Council (NDMC) announced that Central Park in Connaught Place will remain closed to the public on Friday and Saturday (October 17, 2026), citing “administrative reasons”.

Rahul Gandhi urges President to reconsider Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Governor over pending CBI probe

Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha, Rahul Gandhi, on Thursday wrote to President Droupadi Murmu, urging her to ask the Centre to reconsider Dushyant Gautam’s appointment as Sikkim Governor until the ongoing Central Bureau of Investigation probe into the alleged ‘VIP’ angle in the 2022 Ankita Bhandari murder in Uttarakhand is completed.

Protester may need ear surgery after alleged assault in detention, medical reports show

Fidal Royas travelled the length of the country from his hometown in Kerala to Delhi to fight for democracy and demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. He returned home 11 days later to seek treatment for severe ear injuries that may require surgery after having been hit, kicked, and slapped while detained by the Delhi police on October 11.

Unemployment rate in country stands at 5% in September, stable compared to August: NSO

The Unemployment Rate (UR) in the country stood at 5% in September, stable compared to August, according to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by the National Statistics Office (NSO). The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation said in a release on Thursday that the rural UR remained “broadly stable” at 4.2%, against 4.1% in August, while urban UR marginally rose from 6.8% in August to 6.9% in this month.

Amid rift buzz, Shivraj Chouhan meets CM Mohan Yadav with delegation of tribals on demolition drive

Union Agriculture Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan called on Madhya Pradesh Chief Minister Mohan Yadav with a delegation, days after he criticised the State Government over the demolition of houses of 12 tribal families in Kosmi village under his stronghold Budhni assembly constituency. State Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) president Hemant Khandelwal also attended the late-night meeting at the CM residence in Bhopal.

World.title: CM alleges KCR drawing water ‘illegally’ to his farmhouse
World.content:
Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy alleged that a canal had been dug from Kondapochammasagar to Panchapandavula Cheruvu and that water was being pumped directly to the hundreds of acres of BRS chief K. Chandrasekhar Rao’s farmhouse.

The Chief Minister asked what the justification was for diversion of water to KCR’s farmhouse and challenged him to agree to the removal of the pump connection. He proposed the constitution of a fact-finding committee to investigate the matter and establish where the water from Panchapandavula Cheruvu was being supplied.

The Chief Minister challenged the Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) to participate in a debate in the Legislative Assembly on Krishna and Godavari water-sharing issues, alleging that the previous government had compromised Telangana’s water rights.

The government was ready to discuss how the State’s interests had been affected and asked the BRS leadership to stop making what he described as false allegations against the government. “People will not believe you if you keep repeating falsehoods. As long as you continue to lie, we will continue to tell the truth,” he said.

World.title: Surveillance strengthened on paddy movement in Tiruvallur
World.content:
The Tiruvallur district administration has tightened surveillance on movement of paddy after complaints of bags being brought in by traders to direct procurement centres (DPCs).

Farmers have alleged that traders, including a few from neighbouring States, submit papers belonging to farmers and sell procured paddy.

“This, we hear is happening in Ponneri and Uthukottai areas. It should not be allowed. Farmers who are in distress seem to be pledging their crops with the traders and then giving the harvested crop to them. As the payment at the DPC may be better, the farmers are giving their adangal and chitta,” said a farmer, who did not want to be named.

Inspection at border checkposts

District Collector S. Kavitha said that inspections were being carried out at border checkposts, teams of officials from the Revenue and Agriculture departments are being told to verify registrations and the quantity of procurement and the variety.

“We have created awareness among farmers that a two-year procurement ban would be imposed on those who gave their adangal to traders. The digital crop survey has been made mandatory from crop standing in the fields. If there are any discrepancies, special teams have been formed to verify the farmers’ fields,” she said.

Andhra Pradesh truck seized

Following such measures, a team of Revenue Department officials have seized a truck containing 16 tonnes of paddy from Andhra Pradesh in Anna Nagar in Uthukottai taluk.

Tiruvallur district has around 1.06 lakh hectares of land under paddy cultivation. This time, of the 70 DPCs approved, 58 have been opened and are functioning.

“The remaining will be opened based on the harvest schedule in those taluks. So far 9,600 tonnes of paddy have been procured from 1,300 farmers,” an official source said.

World.title: HC directs State to issue instructions to all  departments to scrupulously adhere to prescribed timelines for receipt, consideration and disposal of representations
World.content:
The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court has directed Tamil Nadu Chief Secretary and Secretary to Human Resources Management Department to issue instructions to all the departments to scrupulously adhere to the prescribed timelines for receipt, consideration and disposal of representations submitted by retired government employees, their family members and the public.

Justice B. Pugalendhi directed that the existing mechanism for monitoring the disposal of representations should be effectively implemented. Failure, without sufficient cause, to dispose of a representation within the prescribed time should be viewed seriously. Appropriate disciplinary action should be taken against officers responsible.

Article 350 of the Constitution provides that every person shall be entitled to submit a representation for the redressal of any grievance to any officer or authority of the Union or a State in any of the languages used in the Union or in the State. The right to submit a representation to the authorities for the redressal of grievances is a constitutional right, the court said.

The court said the instructions issued by the government, in the form of government orders, circulars and office manuals, prescribing the time limits for disposal of such representations were intended to ensure that the right was meaningfully exercised and grievances brought before the authorities were dealt with within a reasonable time.

The instructions also constitute an essential aspect of the duties of the government employees entrusted with the receipt and disposal of such representations. Failure to discharge such obligation within the prescribed time would amount to dereliction of duty and may, depending upon the circumstances, constitute misconduct, the court said.

The court said such persistent inaction, despite repeated government instructions and judicial intervention, cannot be permitted to become an accepted feature of public administration.

The consequence of such avoidable litigation was not confined to the consumption of valuable judicial time. It also resulted in avoidable expenditure both to the litigant and to the State, the court said.

The court was hearing the batch of petitions filed by retired government employees and legal heirs of deceased government employees seeking family pension, revision of retirement benefits and payment of arrears. The court directed the authorities concerned to consider and dispose of the representations in three months.

World.title: Dengue testing stepped up in Chennai, over 4,500 cases recorded this year
World.content:
With dengue cases crossing 4,500 in Greater Chennai Corporation (GCC) areas, the Health Department has directed that all fever cases be tested, Principal Secretary to Government, Health and Family Welfare Department, Darez Ahamed, said on Sunday. He added that no dengue deaths had been reported.

Speaking to reporters after inspecting dengue prevention works in the Teynampet Zone, Mr. Ahamed said the State had recorded 20,000 cases so far, and that all fever cases were being tested to identify and manage the disease.

In Chennai, 16,254 tests have been conducted and 4,592 people have been affected by dengue this year. The number of cases recorded in September was 1,293. More than 100 medical camps were being held every day, and 3,703 mosquito eradication workers had been deployed, Mr. Ahamed said.

Mr. Ahamed inspected a medical camp at East Namasivayapuram, and mosquito eradication works, including drone-based larvicide spraying, along the Cooum. He also went door-to-door, distributing awareness pamphlets, on Sunday.

GCC Commissioner G.S. Sameeran said dengue incidence was gradually declining and that intensive prevention works would continue.

He said that desilting of 44 waterways and drone-based biological solutions were being undertaken.

A total of 1,400 km of the 1,600 km of stormwater drains, identified with blockages, had been desilted, he said. The remaining 200 km would be completed within the week, he added. Chennai has over 3,000 km of stormwater drains, besides 250 km under the Highways Department. Priority works under the Mamallan Reservoir project are planned for completion in October, he said.

Dr. Sameeran said ₹100 crore had been allocated for monsoon precautionary works and there was no shortage of funds for these works.

For long-term capital works, the GCC plans to tap foreign financial assistance schemes, including those of the World Bank and JICA, he said.

The Commissioner further said that fines, totalling ₹7.2 lakh, had been imposed in the past month on commercial establishments, organisations, and houses for failing to remove garbage.

World.title: Joint sitting of Parliament endorses emergency, governor's rule in KP amid opposition outcry
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: A joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday gave its approval to the Centre’s imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa amid a strong protest from the opposition.

The joint session had been summoned to discuss separate resolutions on the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in KP, where the opposition’s PTI was in power.

During the session, which was addressed by both members of the treasury and opposition benches, the government justified its decision while the PTI lambasted the Centre and the allegations levelled against the party.

The Centre took the measures on Oct 11, citing the provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The move followed weeks of political tensions between the Centre and the PTI — as well as negotiations to bridge their differences — after the latter announced a long march to Islamabad to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan.

During Thursday’s joint sitting, opposition members turned up carrying placards inscribed with slogans, such as “emergency na manzoor (emergency is unacceptable)”.

PM Shehbaz, who attended part of the session, shook hands with opposition leaders of both the Senate and the NA, pictures and footage showed.

Parliamentary Affairs Minister Tariq Fazal Chaudhry tabled the two proclamations and separate resolutions regarding the emergency and governor’s rule.

After hours-long debate, NA Speaker Ayaz Sadiq put the two resolutions to a vote, while opposition members chanted “emergency unacceptable”.

The resolutions approving emergency and governor’s rule were then passed.

At the outset of the proceedings, Chaudhry also presented a motion under Rule 232 of the Parliament (Joint Sitting) Rules 1973 to suspend certain sub-rules so he could move the resolutions.

As loud noes echoed and opposition members chanted “emergency na manzoor”, the speaker again put the motion to a vote by asking the members to stand up, which was then adopted with 214-56 votes.

Subsequently, Chaudhry moved two resolutions before the joint sitting — one for approving the Proclamation of Emergency under Article 232 and the second for the proclamation of governor’s rule under Article 234.

Law Minister Azam Nazeer Tarar then opened the discussion on the two resolutions and said members of the treasury benches were ready to reply to any query raised by the opposition.

Explaining the constitutional process to approve the resolution for emergency, he said the joint sitting could reject it by a total majority, ie 51 per cent. Similarly, the resolution for governor’s rule also required a total majority of votes for approval.

The joint sitting also offered prayers for the lives lost, mostly of children, in a roof collapse in Peshawar.

The joint session took place a day after both Houses of Parliament, in separate sittings, passed resolutions endorsing the imposition of emergency in KP.

According to Article 232 , if the “president acts on his own, the Proclamation of Emergency shall be placed” before both Houses of the Parliament for approval by each House within 10 days.

Meanwhile, a proclamation for governor’s rule issued under Article 234 “shall be laid before a joint sitting and shall cease to be in force at the expiration of two months”, unless a joint sitting approves its extension. However, such a measure shall not remain in force for more than six months.

Naqvi notes ‘clear stance’ of PTI lawmakers

Speaking during Thursday’s joint sitting, Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi urged the opposition to stick to facts when recounting the dialogue held with the government, asserting that the Centre had “no option left” but to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

“By God, our hearts did not want to do this,” Naqvi remarked, adding that the treasury members were trying their best so that the measures were not taken in KP.

“I will request only that you let facts remain facts. […] We had no option left, after which we did this and you will definitely oppose it, but we should consider the facts,” the minister said as he sought to provide a “clarification” on the allegations levelled by the opposition.

“Please do not say that we misused terrorism.”

He also refuted what he said was the opposition’s stance that the government delegation left the talks. “We did not get up and leave […] we did not even urge you to hurry up.”

Naqvi, who was part of the government’s delegation during the Oct 3 talks, emphasised: “We tried until the last minute […] It was our effort until the last hour that this (emergency/governor’s rule) is not imposed.”

The minister said the federal government offered its KP counterpart to declare emergency in “12 districts, on which you said fine, let’s do it”. He claimed that PTI’s Asad Qaiser, who was present during the talks, was willing to sign an agreement, but he advised the latter to consult the KP government first.

Pointing towards the opposition benches, Naqvi affirmed that the government was not levelling allegations against them. “I vouch for those sitting here that you were not even a single step behind on [countering] terrorism,” he added.

The minister referred to a video clip — later sharing it on his X account — in which KP Information Minister Shafi Jan was asked to declare that the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) was a terrorist group.

“Those individuals in the TTP who are against the state are terrorists,” Jan responded.

Addressing the opposition members, Naqvi further said: “I believe that you, and those we spoke to, particularly Asad Qaiser sahib, as he responded on [the issue] of terrorism that day, I guarantee that even we were not thinking of the things they were speaking on.”

He went on to acknowledge that all those present in the meeting “had an absolutely clear stance [on terrorism] that we will do this for Pakistan”.

The interior minister, holding a paper, said he suggested to even exclude a term about the PTI calling off its long march, but PPP Vice President Sherry Rehman insisted on keeping it.

Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi holds a paper during a joint sitting of Parliament on Thursday. — screengrab via DawnNewsTV

Naqvi noted that Sohail Afridi, the KP chief minister whose role is now non-functional, had not gone to the site of “even a single operation with the army and only used to say ‘I cannot afford this politically’”.

The minister recalled his efforts to sort out differences between the Centre and KP, such as meetings between Afridi and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on the issue of provincial funds.

While saying he did not deem it appropriate to speak about Afridi in his absence, Naqvi claimed he and the PTI leader had discussed a plan to strengthen police forces in five KP districts.

He said the federal government wanted a meeting of the provincial apex committee to be held.

“A press release had to be issued, which would state that we will fight against terrorism together. You can ask for that press release, what was written in it and what happened; everything is before you.”

He recalled that some personnel were martyred in an attack “the same day”, adding that it took place in February.

“We requested the CM sahib and took him to the funerals with us. That was the last day when CM KP attended the funeral of any army officer or jawaan (soldier),” he added.

The minister concluded his speech by reaffirming the Centre’s determination to fight the wave of terrorism. He said the fight could not be waged on “under two [different] policies” of the federation and the province.

He urged the PTI to hold discussions with the KP government on what matters were wrong, adding: “No political party should be accused of terrorism. This is a major thing. But if something has happened, it should be fixed.”

Gohar objects to allegations of ‘backing terrorists’

Speaking on the Parliament’s floor, PTI interim chairman Barrister Gohar Ali Khan said the country was going through a “very fragile situation”.

He lamented that the KP government was accused of “backing terrorists”.

“The prime minister has alleged that we are supporting terrorists. We are disappointed to hear that. You have to apologise to the entire population of KP and us,” he said.

“Prime minister, you have given a message to the entire world that one of the federating units of the country was backing terrorists,“ Gohar added.

He highlighted that the opposition stood with the government during a war with India. “But today we are called supporters of terrorists,” he regretted.

Barrister Gohar rejected the proclamation of emergency and declared that the PTI will make the country stronger and eradicate terrorism when it comes into power again.

He also rejected the government’s claims that PTI leaders did not attend funerals of martyrs, recalling that he himself had attended multiple funerals in KP.

Gohar said the PTI was willing to engage in dialogue with the government provided that its demands were met.

He lamented that speeches of opposition members were not shown in the media.

Speaking to the media at Parliament after the session, Gohar again condemned the move to impose the emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

He noted that the production orders for two detained opposition MNAs — Sanaullah Khan Masti Khel and Dawar Khan Kundi — were issued on Wednesday, yet they were not brought to Parliament during the joint session.

Gohar said by removing the PTI from power in KP would not affect the party’s popularity as “its strength is the public”. But, he continued, “we condemn the illegal and unconstitutional dismissal of a provincial government. We will raise our voice against it at every forum”.

He then condemned terrorism, responding the federal government’s allegations that the PTI supported terrorism. He warned that accusing a provincial government of supporting terrorism would have “serious implications for Pakistan” internationally.

The PTI chairperson added that the prime minister had made a “mistake by making a political statement in a federal cabinet that a provincial government was supporting terrorism”.

“Don’t politicise the issue of terrorism,” Barrister Gohar urged.

“Do not put the nation and the federation at stake for the sake of your narrative. This (terrorism) is not just an issue for a province or the federation. Rather, it was a state-level issue. Time will prove that your decision was political,” he added.

He also rejected the allegations that the PTI was the reason behind the breakdown of talks with the government ahead of the imposition of governor’s rule in KP.

Dar defends ‘difficult decision’

During the joint session, speaking towards the end of the debate, Deputy PM and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar defended the federal government’s “difficult decision” to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP.

Dar said that the decision was “categorically” in accordance with the Constitution and appealed to the opposition “not to misinterpret or misquote facts” to save personal politics.

“Let me remind you of the history,” he said, saying that the menace of terrorism emerged after the 2014 Army Public School attack in Peshawar.

The PML-N leader recalled that a multi-party moot was held following the attack, with PTI in attendance and on board with the counterterrorism decisions, including the National Action Plan (NAP).

The deputy premier recalled that Operation Zarb-i-Azb and Operation Raddul Fasaad were launched against terrorists, adding that data showed their activities had “ended after the operations”.

“We all are Pakistanis […], but we all have the clarity in our minds regarding the facts,” Dar emphasised. Referring to the opposition, Dar said he could see the PTI was against terrorism, but asked who those “few” were who he alleged opened the borders and let the terrorists enter Pakistan.

“There are a few individuals in the party (PTI) who are responsible for the terrorism reaching its peak,” he claimed. “For how long will we keep repeating the same mistakes due to our petty politics and some individuals?” he asked.

On political reconciliation, Dar said that the menace of terrorism should be dealt with before any other matter. “If not now, then when?”

He also criticised Afridi for holding mobilisation campaigns across Pakistan while his province reeled from the threat of terrorism. Dar contended that the province had “collapsed in terms of governance”.

Referring to the federal cabinet’s Oct 11 meeting in which the decision was made to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Dar said that PM Shehbaz left the meeting by saying “it’s now or never” to deal with the deteriorating security situation.

Achakzai blames ‘faulty decisions’

Speaking in the Parliament, NA Opposition Leader Mehmood Khan Achakzai blamed “faulty decisions” of the country’s rulers for the current situation.

He enquired about the whereabouts of Afridi, who was reported to be in preventative custody.

Achakzai, who leads the opposition alliance Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-i-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP), accused PML-N’s Sadiq of not running the house judiciously as the speaker.

He said the opposition was ready for dialogue on issues such as empowerment of Parliament and eradicating terrorism of all kinds.

“If you hold dialogue on these issues, we will give unconditional support,” he added.

The opposition leader compared the KP imbroglio to the 1971 separation of East Pakistan, noting that Afridi was called a “terrorist”.

“Were multiple attacks on the heads of different political parties in the past in KP committed by Sohail Afridi?” he asked.

Achakzai said terrorism was introduced by those who had brought fighters for the Soviet-Afghan war. “When the Afghan war was over, these terrorists were left free in the tribal areas of the country and they started killing Pakistanis,” he added.

The opposition leader then mentioned the reported deaths during the July unrest in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK).

The TTAP chief sought meetings of incarcerated PTI founder Imran Khan with his family, friends and party workers. He questioned who had “sent” ex-premier Nawaz Sharif to exile in Saudi Arabia and who “murdered” ex-PM Benazir Bhutto.

The NA speaker took exception to Achakzai’s remarks on his chairing of the session.

“You are saying to me that I am not running the House correctly. You have not read Rule 30. Someone takes their mobile phone; someone disrupts [the proceedings].”

Sadiq further said recordings of members’ speeches that were “anti-state” would not be uploaded on the NA’s social media accounts.

Meanwhile, Senate Opposition Leader Allama Raja Nasir Abbas accused the government’s delegation of derailing the dialogue with the opposition, including the Oct 3 talks.

The Majlis Wahdat-i-Muslimeen (MWM) chief said some more time should have been allowed to make the talks successful and called for resolving the public’s issues instead of blaming each other.

The senator contended that people voted for the PTI in large numbers during the February 2024 general elections in reaction to Imran’s imprisonment.

Noting that this was his first tenure as a parliament member, Abbas said he realised that the Constitution was a safeguard of the rights of people. He further claimed he did not receive a salary or any perks and privileges from the Senate.

‘We kept waiting’: PPP’s Rehman recounts Oct 3 talks

In her remarks, PPP’s Rehman asked the PTI to define its agenda and reasons for its long march, which the party had announced to stage towards Islamabad but remained within KP.

The senator added that President Asif Ali Zardari and PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari had insisted on resolving issues through dialogue because terrorism was a red line for them.

She called on the opposition not to dictate to the government and to avoid giving lectures on patriotism.

Rehman emphasised that everyone was trying to find common ground and “a path of action”.

The PPP leader objected to the opposition’s claims that the government delegation left the Oct 3 talks.

“We kept waiting for you. The speaker and I ordered food for you as leaving was not being considered. We could have sat till 5am or 6am,” she said.

Rehman asserted, “We had said we would wait further […] This is not fair to say that we said ‘we are leaving’. Definitely not. Opposite.”

Speaking on the topic, the NA speaker — who chaired the talks — also remarked, “What was the hurry in launching the long march?”

Sadiq referred to a post on X made by Afridi about going ahead with the long march even as the negotiations were underway.

“You said to ignore it, so we kept ignoring it till 3am, so I think, if you want to sit again [at the table] then do not go into further details. Those things took place in confidence; bury them here.”

The PPP vice president remarked that the country faced several emergencies, including those regarding education and poverty, that needed to be seen holistically.

“If you think PPP is going to support any sort of emergency which is against the Constitution, you are wrong,” she declared.

“This Constitution has bound the country together through difficult times. We remember the lessons from the fall of Dhaka,” she said.

“PPP has seen many phases of the path towards democracy. It (martial law) was a dark chapter in history; we do not want the country to go through such an experience again,” Rehman said, recalling “sacrifices” made by her party.

JUI-F says no ‘evidence’ presented

Senator Kamran Murtaza of the Jamiat Ulema-i-Islam-Fazl (JUI-F), who had earlier submitted a resolution opposing the imposition of governor’s rule in KP, contended that no documentary evidence was presented before the Parliament for the decision.

He argued that the proclamation under Article 234 required a report from the KP governor, but in this case, Governor Faisal Karim Kundi had not presented a report explaining why governor’s rule was necessary.

The JUI-F senator said the security situation in Balochistan was also grave and pointed out that a provincial government now had its writ in the Katcha areas without an emergency being imposed there.

Murtaza stressed that free and transparent elections under a fair election commission were the only solution to the existing problems.

World.title: FBR extends deadline for filing income tax returns to Oct 31
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: The Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) has further extended the date for filing income tax returns for 2026 to Oct 31.

The notification, posted on the FBR’s X account, said: “In exercise of the powers conferred under Section 214A of the Income Tax Ordinance, 2001, the Federal Board of Revenue is pleased to further extend the date of filing of income tax returns for tax year 2026 upto October 31, 2026, in the case of persons who were required to file their returns by September 30, 2026, and whose date of filing had earlier been extended up to October 15, 2026.”

It added that the deadline had been extended “in view of requests received from various trade bodies and tax bar associations”.

Previously, the board had extended the date to Oct 15, from the original deadline of Sept 30.

Trade bodies and professionals had sought an extension of the deadline, citing delays in the issuance of return forms and heavy online traffic as major hurdles in timely filing.

Federation of Pakistan Chambers of Commerce and Industry President Atif Ikram Sheikh had also formally urged the government to extend the deadline for filing income tax returns to Oct 31 to facilitate trade, industry, and other tax filers. However, initially the deadline had been extended till Oct 15.

The Karachi Tax Bar Association (KTBA) had also submitted a five-page letter to the Member Inland Revenue (operations), highlighting several issues, including delays in the issuance of draft notifications and persistent technical glitches in the IRIS portal, which hinder the smooth filing of tax returns.

The total returns filed until Oct 14 had reached to 6.71 million against 4.99m returns filed during the corresponding period last tax year, according to official data available with Dawn — an increase of 34.38 per cent. Until Sept 30, the total number of returns filed was 5.76m compared with 3.98m filed during the corresponding period last year, showing an increase of around 45 per cent.

Total tax paid with returns till Oct 14 stood at Rs66.81 billion, about 14.61pc more than last year’s Rs58.29bn.

In 2026, returns filed by non-salaried individuals, a category that covers traders, shopkeepers, professionals and the self-employed individuals, rose by 46.35pc, from 3.04m to 4.45m.

Returns by salaried individuals rose by 16.16pc to 2.18m, from 1.88m in the corresponding period last year.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs3.63 per litre, raises high-speed diesel rate by Re0.31
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Rs3.63 per litre, but raised that of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.31 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs390.23 per litre, while HSD will cost Rs396.96 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices are applicable for Oct 16 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Meanwhile, the government has reintroduced a raft of austerity measures in response to rising fuel prices amid the ongoing Middle East conflict. Under these measures, markets are required to close by 9pm and fuel allocations for official vehicles has been cut by 50 per cent for three months.

On September 13, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also announced a “ relief scheme ” for users of motorcycles, autos and vehicles of up to 800cc to “alleviate the burden” of rising global oil prices.

Previously, on July 17, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

Prior to this, the government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.
